392.label: Top: a missed knight royal fork (very often Ne2+) winning the queen by exploiting king-queen alignment; medium blurs to other missed king-queen tactics — discovered checks and pins — plus broader missed winning shots, still mostly material- or queen-winning.

412.label: Top: in a won pawn endgame, plays a slow centralizing KING move instead of immediately pushing the passed pawn, forfeiting the single decisive tempo in the pawn race; medium keeps the 'squandered a winning advantage by failing to push the pawn now' core but broadens the wasted move beyond king moves (prophylactic pawn/quiet moves) and occasionally into the middlegame.

399.label: Top: a relocating major piece (rook/queen, or king) leaves a previously-defended knight/rook hanging to immediate capture; medium blurs the abandoned unit to a pawn (f7) and the mechanism to discovered-attack and missed-defense cases where the squandered move forfeits a winning advantage.

393.label: Top boards drop a minor piece in the opening (the unsound Bxf7+ sac, or a bishop/knight lost to a pawn thrust exploiting a pin/loose piece); medium broadens to dropping the exchange, a pawn, or making positional/structural concessions, occasionally outside the opening.

402.label: Top boards hang a piece outright (often a rook taken by a bishop) when a king/rook/pawn move abandons a defender or steps into an attacked line; medium boards blur into quiet moves that neglect king safety and concede a winning attack or forced mate, with a few missed-win outliers.

414.chip: Traded queens, surrendering winning attack (any edge)
414.label: Top: a queen capture/exchange that voluntarily trades off the queen and surrenders a winning king-side or mating attack (constant: queens-off kills the attack); medium broadens to queen trades that throw away any winning advantage—including allowing forks, passed pawns, or discovered attacks—and blurs into simply mishandling/hanging the queen outright.

418.label: Top: cleanly hangs a freshly developed piece (queen/bishop) to a one-move capture in the opening—by stepping into a pawn's path or ignoring a free recapture/threat; medium blurs to material lost via short multi-move tactics (deflection, pins, opened diagonals) plus positional and king-safety lapses, including some missed wins.

430.label: Top: in a winning middlegame, squandered a FORCED MATE by playing a slow/defensive or non-forcing move (often retreating the key attacking piece, frequently the queen, out of the king zone); medium blurs to missing any winning continuation — move-order errors, piece retreats, greedy captures, missed forks — where the squandered win is a large advantage or material rather than strictly a forced mate.

410.label: Top boards uniformly move a knight onto a square where it is captured for free (usually knight-takes-knight, including failed forks); at medium this blurs to sacrificing or trading away a key knight, leaving it en prise after another move, and occasionally hanging a different piece such as a bishop.

417.label: Top boards are almost uniformly greedy queen captures of a defended central knight (Qxd4/Qxd5/Qxg4) that immediately get recaptured, hanging the queen for a minor piece; medium blurs to rooks and bishops capturing/overextending into loss of material or the exchange, plus a few loose moves and unsound sacrifices, with only the 'self-inflicted material loss via a flawed capture/move' thread held in common.

396.label: Top: a quiet, non-forcing move (knight/bishop/pawn/rook, no capture/check) leaves a minor piece loose, the king exposed, or loses tempo, and drops material/initiative in a short forced sequence; medium broadens to slow moves that simply walk into a knight fork (Nc4/Na4/Ne4) or central break winning a piece, while skipping the position's available active resource.

419.label: Constant across all boards: the move leaves king/piece exposed so the refutation opens with a tempo-gaining check that wins material or crashes through — at the peak this is spectacular king-attack sacrifices (Bxf7+, Nh6+) and a back-rank Re8+ shot, while medium narrows to a plain undefended bishop/rook grabbed after an intermediate check (Nxf3+→Qxf4, Bd4+→Bxd1).

433.label: Top is almost uniformly the queen snatching the 'poisoned' b2/b7 pawn and getting trapped/chased (Rb1/Rb8, Na4, Nb5) for net material; medium keeps the greedy-pawn-grab theme but broadens the offending piece — bishop (Bxc2/Bxc7/Bxh7), knight (Nxd4), rook (Rxc2), or queen elsewhere (Qxa7/Qxb5) — all refuted by an immediate tactic.

416.label: Top is constant: an h-pawn push (h6/h3) played to 'ask the question' of an active/pinning bishop near the king, which loosens the shelter and is refuted by a sacrifice (or skips a winning tactic like Nxd4/Qxf7+); medium blurs to any flank pawn (f6/g6/a-/h4) chasing a knight or queen, punished by Greek-gift/exchange sacs, back-rank mates, or pure tempo loss.

432.label: Top: in a won (endgame) position the player makes a passive king/piece move that declines a free one-move capture of an undefended enemy piece (rook or queen, also bishop/knight), throwing the win away; medium broadens to any quiet (usually king) move that squanders a won/drawn position—skipping winning captures or pawn pushes, allowing forks, passed-pawn breaks, or king invasions.

420.label: At the peak a winning side hangs material—often the queen—or walks straight into a forced mate by playing the wrong (frequently king/queen) move instead of the available crush; at medium it blurs into slow, passive, tempo-losing moves that merely squander the win or forced mate without always immediately hanging material.

438.label: Top is invariably the unsound Bxf7+/Bxf2+ bishop sacrifice — taking one pawn with check then getting recaptured for nothing; medium keeps the f7/f2 sac as the core but blurs into other premature king-hunt blunders that hang material (Qh4+, Qxf7+, even castling into a trap).

397.label: Top: greedily captures a pawn or trades off the key attacking piece, discarding a forced mate / decisive kingside attack; medium broadens to materialistic or natural moves that instead miss a lesser tactical win or simply hang a piece.

434.label: Top: a quiet/passive non-defensive move ignores a FORCING refutation (knight fork or forced mate) and drops material; medium keeps the same 'ignored-the-tactic-and-loses' pattern but broadens the neglected motif to pins, discovered attacks, king-hunts and plain hanging captures.

439.chip: Hangs piece via quiet move (vs missed wins)
439.label: Top: a quiet developing/repositioning move (most often a bishop, in the opening) hangs the player's own piece by declining the available capture/exchange; medium blurs to other piece types and shades toward quiet moves that merely skip a winning capture or combination rather than dropping material outright.

440.label: TOP is tightly unified: the engine's best move was to castle (O-O/O-O-O) but the player instead pushed a pawn, moved the queen, or grabbed material, leaving the king stuck in the center to be smashed by tactics over the next 2-3 moves; MEDIUM keeps the king-safety-neglect core (g4, Nxe5, Qh5, Re1 instead of castling/defending) but blurs to include other 'natural-but-inferior' moves — passive piece placement, an overloaded-defender rook lift, and a directly hung bishop — where the recommended move was no longer specifically O-O.

451.label: At the peak, a quiet/centralizing queen move in a winning position skips a non-forcing tactic that wins the enemy queen outright (Qxf5+, Bxh6); at medium it blurs to skipping a faster forced-mate sequence while already up material.

446.label: At the peak, the player relocates/advances a piece while ignoring fianchetto tension on the long diagonal—skipping the needed Bxg2/Bxg7—and hangs a bishop (b2/b7/g7) or loses material along that diagonal; at medium it blurs into any piece move that hangs material or drops tempo/king safety, only sometimes diagonal-related.

437.label: Top boards are central minor-piece captures (mostly Nxe5/Nxd5) where the opponent's pawn recapture (dxe5/exd5/cxd5) hits a second piece—usually the f6 knight—with tempo and wins material; medium keeps the greedy/eliminating-capture surface but broadens the punishment beyond the pawn-recapture-tempo to move-order queen hangs (Kxf7→Qxd8, Nxc3→Qxa5), ignored counter-threats, and even mate.

431.label: At the peak the player pushes/locks a central pawn (e4/d4/d5) or grabs the wrong pawn instead of the correct central capture (exf4/dxe4/dxe5/bxc5) that wins material or keeps a winning edge; at medium it broadens to other declined or mistimed captures (free pawns like Nxg4, recaptures, cxd5/exf4) plus a couple of king-safety slips.

435.label: Top: in a lost/critical endgame a quiet king/pawn move skips the one decisive one-ply resource—usually capturing a hanging enemy piece (or it hangs its own); medium broadens to quiet endgame moves that leak material over 2-3 moves or merely concede a structural/tempo edge, with several non-blunder false positives.

426.label: Top boards hang the player's own queen via an attacking/checking/developing move that ignores the en-prise queen; medium boards blur in both directions — hanging or failing to capture any piece (minor, rook, exchange) and pointless tempo-losing checks that squander a win.

449.label: Top is uniformly declining the one winning rook exchange/capture (Rxb4/Rxe4/Rxd5/Rxc4) that converts a won rook endgame; medium blurs to missing captures of other pieces (Bxh4, Nxc8, Nxe3, Rxf7) and to hanging material by walking past the key tactical capture.

443.chip: Inefficient king move, pawn promotion (any piece)
443.label: Top: king moves meant to shepherd one's own passed pawn that step to a tempo-losing square (occasionally squandering the drawing fortress or a faster win); medium broadens to other pieces and general endgame conversion errors around a passed pawn.

459.label: At the peak the player consistently loses the queen outright—moving it (or a pawn/king) so it sits en prise to an enemy queen/rook for free; at medium this broadens to hanging other pieces (rook, bishop) or voluntarily trading the queen into a hopelessly lost endgame.

442.label: At the peak it is consistently a dominant, centralized knight voluntarily captured/swapped for a passive minor piece or pawn while already winning (Nxg6, Nxb6, Nxc4, Nxe5, Nxc3) — surrendering the linchpin and squandering the edge; at medium the same knight-for-inferior-piece trade persists but blurs to also include knight captures that overlook tactics (missing Ne2+ fork), grab the wrong/looser piece, or outright hang it.

456.label: Top boards uniformly hang the queen by playing a quiet move while it's directly attacked (classically a bishop's Bxd8); medium boards broaden to hanging any material—rook, bishop, exchange, or even walking into mate—and sometimes merely missing a free capture in a winning position.

448.label: At the peak it's a knight capture/recapture that either trades into a lost position or drops the knight outright (Nxf6, Nxd3, Nxd5); at medium the same faulty-capture pattern blurs to bishop and pawn captures—and defender-removing moves—that likewise hang material or strip a key defender.

452.label: Top: a tempting check with a major piece (queen or rook) that drops the checking piece to immediate recapture or a losing trade, collapsing a won game; medium broadens to disadvantageous queen trades and non-check captures refuted indirectly by a fork.

469.label: Top boards are king or rook moves that blow a passed-pawn promotion race by neglecting the immediate push or the only correct king route (drawn/losing positions needing one exact move); medium broadens to any tempo-wasting endgame move — slow pawn advances (b5, c5, g4) and king detours — that loses the race, with the material verdict drifting between throwing away a win and merely accelerating a loss.

475.label: Top: an active rook check is dropped onto a minor piece's capture square, losing the exchange (knight/bishop takes the rook); medium broadens to any piece hung—queen, bishop, or a move that leaves a piece undefended—often without the check.

454.label: Top: in won (mostly endgame) positions a passive king move — tucking/centralizing instead of the decisive promotion, capture, or rook-trade — with several actually being 0cp non-blunders; medium broadens to pawn pushes, checks and rook/queen moves that genuinely throw away the win by hanging material, allowing perpetual check, or missing a tactic.

470.label: Top boards are textbook early queen sorties (Qh5/Qd5/Qxd4) that hang a piece or get chased for crushing tempo loss; medium blurs to later misplaced-queen excursions that mostly just lose tempo (Qb3/Qc4/Qb5), plus a few non-queen moves allowing a fork/pin or skipping a win.

482.label: Top: king marches directly into a forced checkmate (mostly mate-in-1/2 nets); medium broadens to king moves (and occasional king-exposing piece moves) that invite damaging checks costing material or forcing a slower mate.

471.chip: Hangs bishop on open diagonal (or any piece/line)
471.label: Top: a move opens or abandons the long diagonal, hanging the (usually fianchettoed) bishop — Bxg7/Bxb2/Bxg2; medium blurs to rooks/knights left undefended on freshly-opened files or diagonals, with a couple of endgame/king-safety outliers that don't fit cleanly.

477.chip: Hangs king to tempo pawn push (often kingside)
477.label: Top: kingside pawn shoves (g4/f4/h4/gxh5) meant to chase the enemy queen for a tempo, which instead shatter the king's shield and force mate; medium broadens to tempo-gaining pawn moves anywhere on the board, punished by anything from mate down to simple material or positional loss.

484.label: Top: pure king-and-pawn endgames where a premature pawn push or a king step that breaks the 'king-first'/opposition rule throws away the win (e.g. ...g2 instead of Kg4, Kc4 abandoning the b6-pawn); medium blurs into rook and other endgames with tempo-losing king/queen moves that merely forfeit efficiency or conversion, mixed with many 0cp non-blunders.

457.label: Top: declines the only saving queen trade and gets mated/overrun by the enemy queen's attack on the king; medium broadens to ignoring forcing tactics generally — hanging a rook/exchange, walking into a knight fork, or even missing a winning capture.

487.label: Top: a tempo-losing or awkward move (often a queen sortie or self-blocking the queen's retreat) leaves the queen trapped/forked and lost to a forcing refutation; medium keeps the 'move allows a tactical refutation that wins material' core but broadens the lost material to exchange/piece/pawn (king-safety, opened diagonals, deflections) and even slides into a missed endgame win.

472.label: Top: king/centralizing moves that throw away a winning or drawn endgame (faulty technique or walking into a back-rank/skewer check); medium broadens to rook, bishop, knight and pawn moves that mishandle passed pawns or give pointless checks, losing the win or draw over the following moves.

461.label: Top: in a won endgame the rook (or queen, with check) captures the enemy passed pawn but is recaptured, trading a major piece for one pawn and squandering the win; medium blurs into broader passed-pawn mismanagement — wrong blockades, premature/incorrect pushes, and even grabbing a pawn instead of mating or winning material.

490.label: Top: in a won endgame a materially-safe queen check is played from the wrong square (or a pawn is grabbed), squandering a forced mate/win into a draw or equality; medium broadens to king retreats and other safe non-checks that throw away a winning advantage.

476.label: Top: a quiet king (or king-shielding) move walks into a forced checking net or mate, losing decisively; medium broadens to king moves that abandon a defended piece (often a rook) or step into a single fork, hanging material more simply.

488.label: Top boards uniformly play a slow quiet/prophylactic move (pawn push, retreat, castle) that skips a forcing minor-piece win — especially a ...Bxh6 queen-deflection or a central knight fork (Nxd4→Nxf3+) winning material; medium boards keep the tactical-oversight core but blur the direction, adding moves that hang the player's own material or ignore the opponent's tactic rather than purely missing a win.

478.label: Top: a rook capture/trade (usually grabbing the enemy passed pawn) that swaps rooks into a clearly lost king-and-pawn endgame; medium broadens to other unfavorable rook trades and greedy captures that simply hang material—plus a few king moves ignoring an en-prise rook or skipping a forced win.

499.label: Top boards are pure king-and-pawn endgames where a king move or wrong pawn push (instead of the sole correct capture/exchange — often an en passant or move-order finesse) hands the opponent an unstoppable passed pawn that wins over 2-3 moves; medium blurs into rook endings, missed pawn breaks, and slow tempo-losing moves that mishandle passers more generally (with a couple of non-endgame outliers like a back-rank mate).

491.chip: Hangs rook on self-opened diagonal (fianchetto→any line)
491.label: Top is uniform fianchetto pawn pushes (g6/b6) clearing the long diagonal to hang the corner rook (Bxh8/Qxh8); medium keeps the line-opening idea but broadens the victim from rook to exchange or even the king (mate down the opened diagonal) and bleeds into removing-defender/trapped-piece/direct-hang cases.

500.label: Top: a premature central pawn break (esp. ...d5/d4) removes the support of its own e-pawn and hangs it; medium broadens to any pawn push — flank advances (a4/g5/f3) and undermining moves — that drop material to tactics (forks, skewers, en passant) or simply squander a winning edge.

504.label: Top: queen parked on a square covered by an enemy pawn, lost to a trivial pxQ that throws away a forced mate; medium blurs into broader conversion blunders—capturing with the wrong piece (queen then taken by pawn), hanging a minor piece, and even materially-safe moves that miss a forced mate.

496.label: Top: player declines an elementary free capture of a hanging enemy piece—almost always a rook (board 1 a queen), instead making a passive king/bishop move that throws away the win; medium blurs to missing the single critical move in general, including a non-capturing king-tempo needed to stop a pawn in a pawn race.

493.label: Top boards are all premature passed-pawn pushes (e2/d2/c7) that hand the opponent a clean blockade (Re1/Rd1/Bxd2) and convert a winning game into equal/losing; medium blurs to other premature pawn advances and captures that squander a winning position, where the refutation is sometimes a mate or hung king (fxg7, exd7, a7→Qh1#) rather than just a quiet blockade.

511.label: Top: an opening bishop sortie to enemy fianchetto/edge squares (h6, b7, a6, h3) hangs the bishop for free; medium broadens to knights, queens, and rooks hung on similar unsupported aggressive forays or pawn-grabs.

480.label: Top boards are won positions whose precise conversion is a queen-trade-with-check (Qe5+/Qg4+/Qd3+) that the player skips with a natural/greedy move, keeping queens on and inviting perpetual or mate; medium boards broaden to any missed forcing shot in a winning position (forks, pins, in-between checks, Bxe6+) where direction blurs between truly hanging material and merely squandering the win.

498.label: At the peak the player grabs a promotion-threatening passed pawn in an endgame and the immediate recapture wins back the rook/queen/bishop—often collapsing a win into an insufficient-material draw; at medium it broadens to ordinary pawn/piece grabs that lose material more indirectly (deflection, trading the lone defender) plus a few non-capture positional king moves and even a missed free capture.

510.label: Top: in already-losing endgames a quiet king move skips the ONLY saving queen trade/simplification and leaves the queen hanging; medium broadens to other pieces (bishop/knight) left hanging by quiet developing or non-forcing moves across phases, occasionally a missed simplification rather than a hang.

509.label: Top: an already-losing king actively walks onto an exposed square (Kb7/Kc6/Kf5/Kf4/Kg6) that converts slow resistance into a short forced mating net; medium blurs to other king-safety collapses where almost any move (rook/bishop/knight, not just the king) allows or fails to prevent forced mate, plus a couple of missed mates/winning tactics.

513.label: Top boards consistently swap a slow developing/prophylactic move for the winning d4/d5 central pawn break (typically exploiting an exposed bishop on c5/c4), while medium blurs into other missed forcing breaks (e5/e6) and into allowed tactics/king-safety and hanging-piece lapses.

515.label: Top: castling (O-O or O-O-O) walks the king straight into a concrete tactical refutation — usually hanging a piece (Be7/Ne7/Bc4) or inviting a fork/pawn-storm that wins material; medium keeps the castling-into-punishment core but blurs to other 'natural' safety/developing moves (king march Kf5, piece relocations Nb7/Bg7, discovered-attack and fork setups) that ignore an immediate tactic and lose material.

489.chip: Hangs material via quiet move (queen-win at peak)
489.label: Top: in a won position a passive/quiet move (retreat, development, castling) overlooks capturing the en-prise enemy queen — almost always the pawn grab exf6 — and hangs own material; medium broadens to any quiet/positional/tempo-losing move that hangs material or surrenders the edge with no hanging enemy queen present.

506.label: Top: a slow, non-checking move (often a queen relocation) abandons king defense and walks into forced mate; medium broadens to the same passive-move pattern hanging material, losing tempo into a loss, or skipping a forcing win.

521.label: Top boards consistently hang own material to an opponent's tactical shot (fork/skewer/discovered attack/removal-of-defender after the played move), while medium boards blur the direction—still hanging in some cases but increasingly missing a material-winning capture or wasting a critical tempo with a slow/positional move.

505.label: Top: a quiet pawn/piece move squanders a crushing winning attack by skipping an available forcing check (with a few outright queen/knight hangs); medium keeps the skipped-forcing-check theme but with smaller still-winning margins, wrong check move-orders, and an occasional defensive hang.

520.label: Top is rock-solid: a bishop developed to g4/g5 in the opening on an illusory pin, hanging free to Qxg4/Qxg5; medium blurs to the same Bg4 fake-pin punished by other captors or mere tempo loss, plus other opening piece-hangs (Ng5, Bb2, Bxd4, e5/e3).

512.label: At the peak the player moves a piece to/away from a guarded square and is punished by a removal-of-defender capture ending in a knight fork/infiltration (Bxa6→Nxc7+, Bxf6→Nxd5); at medium it blurs to any piece move that abandons a key square/diagonal (Qd2 dropping the d1-h5 guard), letting a forcing sequence win material without a clean fork.

507.label: Top boards are sharp won-endgame collapses where a slow king centralization walks into a knight fork losing the queen or misses a forced mate; medium boards broaden to milder tempo-losing king/queen/rook moves across queen, rook, and pawn endgames that merely slow or forfeit the win.

522.label: At the peak: a won endgame where a check or quiet king/piece move skips grabbing an undefended enemy piece—almost always the queen; at medium it broadens to missing smaller free captures (bishop/rook) or grabbing a lesser target, blurring into general failure to play the precise winning move in an already-won position.

516.label: Top: passive/weakening moves let the opponent break through on the player's own king (ignored pawn storm, Bxg7 and Nxh6 sacrifices); medium broadens to a greedy capture/misplaced piece that simply surrenders a winning advantage without any king attack.

523.label: Top: a quiet developing pawn/bishop move in an equal opening directly hangs a piece or queen by abandoning its defender or stepping into a capture; medium keeps the material loss but broadens the mechanism to forks and slips in a couple of opposite-direction missed wins.

518.label: Top: a winning side overlooks an immediate capture of a hanging minor piece (often the Nxe5/Nxg4 bishop-grab) and throws away a decisive edge; medium broadens to skipping the single best move that keeps the win — including positional/tempo breaks and even allowing opponent forks or mate, with a few boards instead being greedy hangs.

530.label: Top: a forced mate (often the back-rank Ra7+/Rgb7# rook mate) thrown away by a quiet pawn/king move instead of the forcing check; medium keeps the 'skipped a forced win' core but broadens to any decisive tactic — knight forks, mate-in-1, tempo-gaining checks, discovered-check mates — still via a non-forcing alternative.

529.label: Top: a winning side ignores its rook left en prise to an enemy bishop's diagonal (king/pawn/rook move blunders the rook); medium keeps the 'leave own material hanging' core but blurs the captured piece (queen, knight, bishop) and capturer (knight as well as bishop), plus drifts into trapped-piece and positional/trade sacrifices.

541.label: Top boards all miss capturing a free, undefended ROOK in an already-won position (one queen case); medium broadens to overlooking any hanging enemy piece — bishop, knight, rook or queen — typically by playing a king/quiet move or grabbing a lesser pawn instead.

531.label: Top: hangs the queen (usually while offering a queen trade) to a capture-with-check that collapses king safety into forced mate; medium broadens to hanging rooks/knights or removing a key defender that permits a mating attack, plus some non-blunders/tempo-losses mixed in.

536.label: Top: in a won pawn endgame the KING walks off a critical/passed pawn (to grab a lesser pawn or head the wrong way), squandering the win and usually hanging that pawn; medium blurs to non-king pieces (bishop/knight/pawn moves) and to failing to blockade the opponent's passer, with several entries being near-best non-blunders.

538.label: Top: king moves in (near-pure) pawn endgames that lose the opposition/tempo and throw away a drawn or won promotion race; medium broadens to other pieces and general passed-pawn mishandling, including king/piece moves that walk into forks, skewers, or hang material.

543.label: Top: a capturing rook trade (Rxd7+, Rxc2, Rxe1...) that simplifies into a lost or dead-drawn king-and-pawn endgame, throwing away the advantage; medium blurs to any simplifying capture/check that backfires — outright hanging the piece, queen trades, failed promotion sacs, or move-order errors — losing material or squandering a forced win.

550.label: Top positions are all already-losing king-and-pawn endgames where a tempo-wasting move (locking a-/b-pawns with a4/b4/c5, a move-order slip, or a wrong-direction king walk) loses the pawn race and lets the opponent's passer promote; medium broadens to general losing-endgame king misplacements that surrender tempo — now including bishop/rook endings and a couple where the bad king square allows a skewer or mating net rather than a pure pawn race.

556.label: Top boards are pointless rook checks that throw away a won rook/pawn endgame by checking instead of centralizing the king (Ke4); medium broadens to other tempo-wasting moves and checks (bishop/king/knight, or abandoning a key pawn) that similarly squander a winning endgame.

552.label: Top: from a won position the player overlooks an immediate one-move kill — a back-rank/forced mate-in-one or grabbing a hanging enemy queen/rook — and instead plays a passive king move; medium keeps the 'squandered win' core but blurs to longer forced mates (mate-in-6/8) and winning captures botched by wrong move-order, greedy pawn grabs, or stepping into mate.

535.label: Top: king steps to the wrong square in a pure pawn/piece endgame, abandoning a critical drawing/blockade/opposition square so the enemy passed pawn promotes, the king infiltrates, or a free capture (Kxf5/Nxd4) is forgone; medium broadens to include pawn pushes and milder king misplacements, several only marginally (or not) losing.

546.label: Top: a rook (often swung to the a-file/edge or a pointless check) makes a passive, tempo-wasting move that abandons its only defensive job in a lost-or-drawn endgame—failing to blockade a passer or shield the king—allowing forced promotion or mate; medium broadens to any piece (bishop, knight) and to passive/tempo-losing moves that instead squander a winning position.

534.label: Top: a quiet queen/rook relocation to an 'active' square abandons the sole defensive/perpetual check and walks into a forced mate; medium broadens to also missing one's own forcing wins (perpetual/fork/check) and assorted tactical hangs (pin, hanging piece) in similarly sharp positions.

555.label: TOP: king-and-pawn endgames where a slow king move or premature pawn push wastes a critical tempo and loses the pawn race/promotion; MEDIUM keeps the endgame king-move theme but broadens to passed-pawn blockade failures, king exposure to pawn-checks, and occasional off-theme positional slips.

561.label: Top: in a winning opening Black/White plays a routine developing/capturing move and misses the crushing Qh4+/Qh5+ diagonal check punishing a missing f-pawn (winning a rook); medium: same 'missed winning shot vs exposed king' idea blurs into other missed tactics — a delayed Qh5+, a ...Ndb4/Nxd3+ fork, ...Nxe5 capture, or the ...d5 central break.

566.label: Top boards miss a forcing queen/bishop check that delivers forced mate (player instead made a quiet developing move or a non-mating 'wrong check'); medium broadens to checks that win decisive material rather than mating.

557.label: Top: a rook/king move (often a greedy capture) fails to control the enemy passed pawn's queening square, letting it promote with check/tempo; medium broadens to abandoning any critical endgame duty — guarding the promotion square OR a hanging piece, or losing a key tempo.

551.label: Top: in a losing/equal position the player plays an 'active' queen reposition or a king move that declines the ONLY saving queen capture/trade (best move is almost always Qx...), hanging the queen or walking into a forced mate; medium keeps the identical 'should have played the queen capture' theme but blurs the direction — now including equalizing trades, tempo-losing queen retreats, and missing queen captures that win a free rook/knight.

572.label: Top: a slow, non-forcing KING move in a passed-pawn endgame wastes the one tempo needed to win/draw (letting the enemy king blockade or escape, or skipping a forcing check/fork/promotion); medium blurs to any passive piece move (queen, knight, rook, pawn) that declines the more active/forcing continuation and squanders the advantage, sometimes even dropping material.

571.label: Top: in a winning opening position, the player skips a forcing queen check — almost always Qa4+ (or Qa5+) along the a4-e8 diagonal against the uncastled king — that wins an undefended minor piece (knight on e4/e5, bishop on g4/c5); medium keeps the 'missed forcing tactic on an undefended piece' core but blurs the mechanism, mixing other queen checks (Qb6+, Qh4+/mate, mis-routed Qa5+) with cases where the player instead hangs or fails to defend an undefended piece (Bh2+/Rxd2, exd5 winning Bb4, ignoring the Nd4 tension).

579.label: At the peak the feature is consistent promotion mistiming—delaying or mis-ordering a pawn promotion (not promoting immediately/with check) and squandering a forced mate while still winning; at medium it blurs into broader passed-pawn endgame errors, e.g. an actual blunder that lets the opponent's pawn become a monster passer (direction flips from 'missed win' to 'allowed/lost material'), with some near-0cp endgame noise mixed in.

570.label: Top boards miss an immediate forcing win from a winning position — usually a tempo-gaining check/fork/promotion (Rd4+, Nf6+, Rf2+, Rf4+, d5+) the player skips for a slow pawn/king move; medium boards broaden to quieter missed conversions in won endgames/middlegames — wrong king move-order, failing to activate before pushing, or declining a winning capture (Bxe6, Re7), with several near-0cp false positives diluting both tiers.

563.chip: Hangs piece on tempo move (often queen)
563.label: Top: a tempo-gaining move attacking the enemy queen that overlooks the player's own hanging major piece (queen/rook), often by vacating the line-blocking defender; medium broadens to other repositioning/pawn 'chasing' moves that hang material or even allow mate, plus some positional errors and a missed queen-grab.

567.label: Top: from a clearly winning (~ -3) position the player captures a queenside pawn/piece with their dominant infiltrated queen or bishop (Qxb1, Bxb3, Qxa3), letting a clean recapture dissolve the whole advantage; medium blurs the same theme to abandoning any active outpost piece (Nxb3, Nf4) or premature captures that simply hang material or expose the king (e5, fxe5, Bxb6).

583.label: Top: a (usually centralizing) king move walks straight into a forced mate, often enabled by a direct or discovered check; medium narrows to the same king-centralization blunders refuted by direct-check mating nets (Qxf7+, e5, Rf8+).

576.chip: Passive move worsens lost endgame (top: mate)
576.label: Top: an already-lost endgame where a slow king/pawn/bishop move abandons a key defensive square and walks the exposed king into a forced rook mate (king_safety #); medium blurs to any passive, materially-'safe' move in a difficult/lost endgame that simply accelerates the loss by ceding the remaining defense and letting the opponent's rook/knight dominate, with no single clean tactical motif.

581.label: Top boards are active-looking developing moves (esp. ...Bc5) that ignore the king's exposure on the open d-file and get punished by Bb5+/Qxd8+ checks or O-O-O contesting the file; medium broadens to other king-safety lapses (weakening ...c5, passive Be3) that invite a general attack — though several top boards leak into pure material drops (forks, hanging pawns).

585.label: Top: a queen gives a forcing-but-pointless check in a clearly winning endgame, wasting the tempo needed to centralize/progress and bleeding eval (or even a forced mate); medium broadens to rook checks and a few non-checking inefficiencies (quiet misplacements, a greedy capture) that likewise squander the won technical endgame.

547.label: Peak is a rook capture/trade that liquidates into an already-lost K+P promotion race (frequently the engine's own 'lose slower' best move, removing the last racing/defending piece); at medium it blurs to other pieces and even non-captures—king walks, pawn pushes, queen retreats—that abandon a defender or key square and throw away a won, drawn, or holdable endgame into mate or material loss.

580.label: Top: a winning position thrown away by a natural quiet/repositioning move that directly hangs material (back-rank mate, en-prise rook, or check-fork); medium broadens to slow non-forcing moves that merely forfeit a forced mate/promotion without losing material.

586.label: Top boards are uniformly a queen grabbing an undefended rook along an open diagonal (Qxa8/Qxh8/Qxg8) while the player instead makes a safe non-capturing move; medium broadens to missing other free material/tactics (Qxb7, Qxd7, knight fork) and blurs in the opposite direction with several positions where the move actually hangs own material to a refutation (Nd6, Rxd3, Nxb5 mate).

591.label: Top boards are uniform: in the opening, a move ignores the central d4-vs-e5 pawn tension and hangs the undefended e5 pawn to a simple dxe5 (or hangs a piece onto a pawn-controlled central square like dxc4/dxc5); medium keeps the opening-center theme but blurs to broader material loss — hanging pieces to pawn breaks, overloaded defenders, move-order/tempo errors, and even some missed central captures.

596.label: Top: a forced checkmate is thrown away by playing a quiet/non-forcing move instead of a decisive queen check (Qe2+, Qg2+, Qd1+, Qxg3+); medium keeps the 'skipped the forcing finish' core but broadens to non-queen forcing moves (bishop checks, rook sacs) and to cases where the miss only slows the mate or wins material rather than mating at once.

592.label: Top boards are uniformly premature queen checks (Qa5+/Qa4+/Qh4+) against an uncastled king that get blocked with tempo, wasting moves and often leaving the queen offside; medium broadens to bishop and rook checks (Bb4+, Bb5+, Re1+) and to cases where the checking piece itself hangs material outright.

590.label: Top: king moves in already-lost endgames that drift to an inferior square, losing a critical tempo (pawn/promotion race) or stepping into a decisive check; medium broadens to king moves that walk straight into knight forks/checks costing material, plus a few non-king tempo errors.

599.label: Top: a passive/retreating move squanders a forced mate launched by a forcing check (king hunt); medium broadens to missing forcing tactics that win material — intermediate checks, capture-order finesses, or grabbing a pawn/exchange — not strictly mate.

612.label: Top is almost exclusively the unsound Bxf7+ bishop sacrifice (with a couple of Bxf2+) against an exposed/uncastled king that simply recaptures and consolidates with no attacking follow-up; medium keeps Bxf7+ as the core but blurs into other unsound bishop sac-checks near the king (Greek-Gift Bxh2+, Bxf2+, Bxb2+) on various squares.

587.label: At the peak, in winning positions the player makes a greedy capture or careless piece move that hangs a piece while overlooking a stronger forcing shot (often a winning check or forced mate); at medium it blurs to materially-safe moves that merely squander the advantage—missing a forcing check, wasting a tempo, or letting a won endgame slip toward a draw.

565.label: Top: an undefended enemy bishop on g4/g5 that also attacks the queen is left uncaptured (Qxg4/Qxg5), with the peak blunders often hanging the queen outright; medium broadens to any undefended minor (knights, bishops on f5/a6) simply not grabbed for free, with no own-material loss.

593.label: Top: a routine opening move (h6/d6/Bc5/Nf6) ignores a knight fork — almost always Nd4 hitting the exposed enemy queen (usually Qf3), often adding a secondary win of a bishop or Nxc2+; medium keeps the 'punish the exposed queen' theme but broadens the forking piece beyond the knight (Nh4/Nd5, plus bishop double-attacks like Be5 and Greek-gift tries) and widens the second target to rook, with a few own-material hangs (b2/f7) blurring the direction.

617.label: Top boards are nearly all unsound sacrificial checks (especially the Bxf7+ bishop sac) that hand back a full piece for one pawn with no follow-up; medium keeps the 'flashy check that backfires' theme but blurs the direction — some still hang material (Nxe5, Bxf7+, Bd6), while others are materially-safe checks that squander a forced mate or win (Ng6+, Rd5+, Rd2+) or merely lose tempo (Bg5+, Nh4+, Rd8+).

611.label: Top: a defender (usually the king) deserts the decisive passed pawn in a won endgame, letting it be captured and the win drawn; medium broadens the same desertion to any guard (queen, bishop, knight, king) abandoning any material—pawn or full piece—across all phases, including a couple of near-trivial cases.

619.label: Top: in clearly winning pure pawn endgames the player pushes a pawn (or makes a passive king move) instead of the decisive king march/activation, throwing the win away to a draw; medium keeps the winning-endgame-with-safe-material signature but blurs to other endgame types (rook, passed-pawn, king-safety) and wrong-direction king/tempo-losing moves, with a few outright piece tactics (fork, back-rank) and several near-0cp false positives mixed in.

620.label: Top: a kingside capture (pawn or king recapture) that leaves the queen undefended on the open d-file, losing it to Qxd8/Qxd1; medium broadens to any winning-position-throwing move that allows a central tactic winning a rook/pawn or merely surrendering the win.

603.label: In a won endgame the player makes a quiet/king move instead of the decisive queen tactic — top boards all skip a free capture of the opponent's hanging queen (Qxd7/Nxe7/Bxh6), while medium broadens to declining the queen trade (Qxd1) that forces the fastest mate.

600.label: Top boards hang the queen (or the piece a missed forcing queen-trade / capture-with-check would have saved); medium broadens to hanging any piece or pawn through slow, greedy, or loosening moves that overlook the opponent's tactic (fork, trap, overload, opened line).

623.label: Top boards are won (mostly endgame) positions ruined by a tempting capture or simplifying trade that liquidates the advantage into a draw/loss—occasionally even ignoring a forced mate; medium broadens to non-capturing positional or back-rank moves that similarly throw the win away, so it blurs from 'greedy capture/trade' to 'any move that squanders a win.'

607.label: Top: ignored a free undefended enemy queen (usually on the d-file/back rank) while playing a routine developing or prophylactic move; medium blurs both the piece (rook/minor/exchange captures) and the direction (also hanging one's own piece by abandoning a defender).

624.chip: Hangs piece in king-attack sac (often Bxh3)
624.label: Top is uniformly an unsound bishop sacrifice on h3/h6 (gxh3 Qxh3 refuted by Nh2/Nd4), hanging a full piece to crack the enemy king's pawn shield; medium keeps the king-attack sac flavor (Bxg2, Bxh6, Bh6) but broadens to general material-losing moves and hangs (Qxb2, Nxe5, Bd6, even a missed fork).

626.label: TOP: in king-and-pawn/passed-pawn endgames the king greedily captures a pawn and ends up too far away to catch the enemy passed pawn, which queens and flips a won/level position to lost; MEDIUM keeps the passed-pawn-promotion-via-misplaced-piece theme (king or even bishop strays, fails to blockade) but blurs to include non-capturing king moves and a few other endgame king-stray tactics (skewer/fork/attack on the wandering king).

616.label: Top: misjudges the g4-bishop's pin on Nf3 — either greedily grabbing the d4 pawn (refuted by Qxd4/Bb5+) or missing the ...Bxf3 shot that wins the loose Bg5; medium keeps the f3-square theme but blurs into other f3 tactics (Nxf3+ forks/recaptures) and miscalculated central pawn grabs (d4/e4/c3) that drop material to a refutation.

631.label: Top: a material-safe pawn advance/exchange in a won K+P endgame liquidates the winning pawn structure straight into a theoretical draw (missed win, not a hang); medium blurs this into premature pawn breaks / tension-release that squander a winning advantage in any phase, plus a few off-pattern misjudged trades and positional slips.

630.label: Top: a quiet non-forcing king/rook move (0% checks) ignores the tactical demand and hangs material—most often a rook to open-file/back-rank infiltration or a king-safety collapse; medium keeps the same passive-move-instead-of-forcing-move behavior but blurs in direction, now equally often MISSING a forcing win (free piece, fork, mate, promotion) as hanging material.

634.label: Top boards invariably capture the enemy queen, stripping the last back-rank defender (or file-blocker) and walking into forced back-rank mate; medium broadens to lesser captures, rook trades, or quiet moves that equally ignore the looming back-rank mate (plus a couple of non-back-rank greedy-capture outliers).

639.label: Top boards uniformly skip a forced checkmate (in 1–4), almost always because the player grabs material or makes a tempting capture instead of mating; medium boards keep the 'pass up the kill' theme but blur the peak's pure mate into missing any decisive winning shot—forced mate, a material-winning tactic, or a move that even lets the opponent generate counterplay/perpetual.

640.label: Top: in a totally won K+pawn endgame the player declines the instantly-decisive queen promotion (often promotion-with-check) by shuffling the king or underpromoting, forfeiting a forced mate/win; medium blurs to milder king-move tempo losses and a skipped winning capture in the same won pawn endgames, several barely losing eval.

647.label: Top: player captures an undefended piece (rook/bishop/queen) and misses a clean mate-in-one; medium keeps the same capture-over-mate pattern but broadens to forced mates that are still essentially M1 (incl. snatching the enemy queen) rather than always a pure single-ply mate.

635.label: Top: gratuitous knight checks (Nd6+/Nf6+/Nc7+/Nxa7+ etc.) that abandon a strong outpost and either hang/trap the knight or waste tempo when a quiet best move (Bb2, Nc4, Rg1) was far better; medium blurs to other-piece checks (Bxc2+, Bxh2+) and increasingly to checks that squander a FORCED MATE or clean material win (Ne4+, Ne3+, Ng5+), so the consequence shifts from hung-material toward missed-win.

641.label: Top: a quiet retreat/develop/king move in a winning position skips a simple capture of an undefended enemy piece (full piece won); medium broadens to passive moves that squander smaller material or positional edges (a pawn, a tempo, a forcing line), occasionally even ignoring the opponent's own threat.

648.label: At the peak it's a tempting queen check (Qb6+/Qe4+/Qf2+) that hangs material or throws away a win/draw because the opponent interposes and gains tempo on the queen; at medium it blurs to a capture-with-check that safely grabs a pawn but misses a forced win of a piece.

645.label: Top boards are aggressive queen moves (often a check, e.g. Qf6+/Qc1+) that simply hang the queen to a capture along an open file/diagonal; medium broadens to other pieces—and to queen/rook retreats that abandon a defensive square—losing material or allowing a winning/mating attack.

657.label: Top: a minor piece is developed onto a square where a pawn or the queen captures it for free (clean one-move hang); medium broadens to tempo-losing opening misdevelopment that ignores the central tension and drops material more slowly.

643.label: Top: a king (or rook) move walks off the defense of an undefended pawn—usually a passed pawn in the endgame—letting it be captured for free; medium keeps the 'abandon a defensive/tactical duty, lose material' core but broadens to queens/bishops deserting their post, hanging a whole piece, or collapsing king safety.

650.label: TOP boards desert a defender of the king/back rank, forcing mate or a major-piece loss; MEDIUM boards keep the same neglect-of-defense root but blur to merely dropping a pawn or piece (and occasionally to missing a win).

633.label: Top: in clearly winning positions a faulty capture/recapture order (often allowing an opponent promotion) hangs material to an overlooked counter; medium broadens to quiet pawn/retreat moves in merely-better positions that drop material to the opponent's next capture.

651.label: Top: all endgame pawn pushes that lock/fix the structure and squander pawn tension instead of the correct capture or king move; medium blurs to broader premature pawn advances (plus a few non-pawn moves) that ignore the position's needs, sometimes hanging material or missing a tactic rather than just decaying positionally.

659.label: Top boards all miss capturing a free undefended knight (Qxg5/Qxg4) in the opening; medium boards blur into a grab-bag of missed tactics, hung pieces, and positional/endgame errors where the clean 'queen-takes-knight' signature dissolves.

669.chip: Hangs king to forcing check (king move)
669.label: Top boards are king moves that tuck into a corner/edge (Kg8, Kh8, Kh2, Kxh3) and walk straight into a mate or a material-winning check/fork; medium broadens to include non-king moves (e.g., Nb1) that still leave the king exposed to a winning check, and a few peaks even blur toward non-check piece forks/discovered attacks (Bd1, Qf6).

670.label: Top boards are constant: a greedy recapture/development leaves White's own queen or bishop undefended on the open 5th rank, snapped off by Black's queen sliding across it; medium broadens to other undefended-piece losses, including those exposed only after a 2-move forced sequence (e.g., forced queen trade then bishop grab), and the captured square need not lie on the 5th rank.

668.label: Top: a routine opening developing move ignores central pawn tension or a hanging minor piece, punished by ...e4/...d4 tempo gains or an immediate capture; medium blurs to ignoring any urgent demand in any phase (king-safety pawn weakening, trapped piece, missed Nxe5), so 'failure to address the critical issue' stays constant while the issue type and material/positional outcome diverge.

653.label: At the peak, a quiet non-capturing bishop/knight move throws away a forced mate or a free enemy-queen capture; at medium the same passive-piece-move pattern blurs into hanging one's own piece (or missing smaller wins) and spreads from the queen to any piece.

642.label: At peak activation the player throws away a forced mate, usually by hanging a rook or knight where it's instantly captured; at medium activation it broadens to any piece (incl. bishop) and increasingly to materially-safe moves that merely miss the forced win/mate, so the hangs-vs-misses direction is genuinely 50/50.

656.label: Top: a quiet developing/repositioning move (knight/bishop/queen) skips the precise forcing reply—usually a center/queenside pawn capture or intermediate check—and drops a pawn (or the whole edge) once the opponent resolves the tension favorably; medium blurs the neglected resource into any critical break, including pawn storms, passed-pawn advances, pin-exploiting captures, and king-safety lapses, losing material or a winning advantage.

672.label: Top boards are slow prophylactic/flank moves (Kb8, a6, h6, b6, Qc7, Kf1) that waste a tempo and skip the thematic central pawn break (d5/e5/f6/d4) against an exposed/uncastled king; medium blurs to any natural-looking move chosen over the single required precise move—slow development, wrong pawn capture/advance (Nbd2, f3-not-f4, fxe5, dxc4), or even king/rook moves that walk into the refutation—still squandering a clear advantage.

665.label: Top boards uniformly center on a hanging queen—the player either misses capturing the enemy's undefended queen or drops a piece by carelessly moving their own; at medium the queen focus blurs to any hung/missed material (rook, exchange, promotion, positional).

685.label: Top: a premature aggressive check (mostly Qh4+/Qh5+, plus knight checks like Ng5+/Ne5+) that directly hangs the checking piece to an obvious recapture; medium broadens to the same forcing/premature checks and queen sorties that instead merely lose tempo or squander a winning advantage (with one outright missed mate).

673.label: Top boards directly expose or strip the guard of a piece (frequently a bishop, or a removed king-defender) that falls to an immediate capture/attack; medium boards broaden to multi-move tactical refutations and quieter positional/structural concessions that also lose material.

681.label: Top: the player's own queen move offers or walks into a losing queen exchange (sometimes hanging the queen on the recapture), losing material or dissolving their own attack; medium blurs to other piece/pawn moves that allow the opponent a favorable queen trade or fail to make a needed one, with a few missed tactical wins mixed in.

687.label: Top: skipped an immediate, usually check-giving, pawn promotion that wins by force; medium: still a missed forcing win but blurs from pure promotion to intermediate/discovered checks, mate-nets, free captures, and even defensive moves stopping the enemy's promotion.

678.label: Top boards hang a kingside pin/pressure bishop (Bg5/Bg4, occasionally Bb4) by retreating or developing instead of the forced resolving capture (Bxf6/Bxf3/Bxc3); medium blurs to any hung piece — and sometimes a skipped winning capture — after a quiet 'natural' move (castle/develop/queen-shuffle) that ignores the central/pin tension.

697.label: Top: a routine flank pawn-poke 'asking the question' of a pinning bishop (h3 vs Bg4) that skips the winning Bxf7+ king-fork shot; medium keeps the lazy 'ask-the-question' pawn move (a6/h6/a3/h3) but broadens the punishment to varied missed-or-allowed tactics (other forks, free captures, sac shots).

693.label: Top: in a won position passes up a winning queen check / capture-with-check (often Qxe6+) for a quiet queen retreat; medium keeps the missed-forcing-check theme but broadens to checks by bishop/knight, capture-order errors and missed mates, plus a few cases where the quiet move instead hangs material to an enemy fork/discovered attack.

686.label: Top boards are uniformly Black mishandling the e5-attacked f6-knight in an open game — propping it with the Qe7 'pin' or retreating it (Nh5/Ng4/Ng8/Ne4) instead of the freeing ...d5, dropping ~200-300cp; medium blurs this into any awkward piece relocation/repositioning (bishops, knights, castling, pawn pushes) that ignores the concrete threat and hangs material across pieces and phases.

692.label: Top: slow/passive tempo-wasting moves (queen or rook retreats, non-urgent pawn pushes) that cede the center and initiative, punished by a central pawn break; medium broadens to passive moves that additionally drop a pawn/piece or expose the king.

710.label: Top boards are uniformly a rook capturing a pawn-defended centralized minor (Rxd4/Rxe4/Rxd5) that a pawn simply recaptures, dropping the exchange; medium broadens to dropping the exchange/material by other means—rook recaptured by king (Rxh2 Kxh2), rook left en prise to pawn/bishop, or the wrong piece used to recapture.

712.label: Top: in a clearly winning opening position the player makes a quiet move (often a pawn push) that drops a whole piece to an immediate free capture (Qxg4, Nxc5, Qxb3); medium broadens to dropping pawns, walking into pins/forks over 2-3 moves, or unsound sacs — with a couple of cases blurring into pure tempo/positional loss or a missed bigger capture.

700.label: Top: an opening king retreat (typically Ke8/Kf8) steps into a devastating check like Qh5+ that wins material or forces mate; medium broadens to other piece moves that allow a forcing check, fork, or attack winning material.

701.label: Top: a natural move (develop/castle/trade/push) hangs a piece or exchange to a forcing check or fork, typically with an exposed king or after a queen trade; medium broadens to skewers, tempo-losses and move-order slips, and increasingly to materially-safe moves that simply miss a winning tactic.

717.chip: Hangs material on queen-chasing pawn (any piece)
717.label: Top: an opening pawn thrust (b4/c4/c5/g6) meant to chase the enemy QUEEN with tempo that instead hangs material or surrenders tempo; medium keeps the tempo-grabbing pawn push but broadens the harassed target to rooks and bishops, with occasional missed-win or non-pawn cases.

707.label: Top: forcing checks (often by rook) in clearly-won endgames that lose tempo by driving the enemy king to a better square; medium broadens to premature checks by any piece that squander a winning advantage or even a forced mate.

688.label: Top boards are winning positions squandered when a queen/rook abandons back-rank or king-defense control (about half pass up a crushing back-rank shot like Rc8/Re8/Rd8, half walk into the back-rank mate/material loss); medium blurs to vacating ANY key square—hanging a piece, allowing a fork, weakening the king, or just missing the precise winning capture/tempo—so the constant 'left a key square in a won game' holds but the back-rank specificity and the hung-vs-missed direction both dissolve.

716.label: Top: hangs a rook, usually via a king move that abandons its defense; medium broadens the hung unit to bishop/knight/queen(fork) and bleeds into softer positional/missed-win errors.

720.label: Top boards almost uniformly skip a queen capture of an undefended piece WITH CHECK (Qxc1+/Qxe1+/Qxc8+/Qxa1+) — usually by retreating the queen instead; medium blurs to any overlooked forcing win (other-piece captures with check, plain winning captures like Qxa8, missed mates Rg8#, or wrong-order captures losing the exchange).

728.label: Top: a clearly won (mostly pawn) endgame is thrown away to a draw/loss via a technique error — premature pawn push, wrong capture/check move-order, or king stepping off the key pawn; medium blurs to all endgame types and to marginal/zero-cp tempo losses, several of which aren't real blunders at all.

718.label: Top boards are clean endgame piece-hangs, usually a king (or knight) move that abandons a defender or steps a piece/promotion next to the enemy king; medium boards blur into broader endgame material errors — forks, rook-trades into lost pawn endings, trapped pieces, and pointless tempo-losing checks.

726.label: Top boards uniformly squander a forced mate by a slow non-forcing move instead of the decisive passed-pawn breakthrough (e.g. hxg6, letting Black play gxh5); medium blurs to general failure to convert won positions (tempo-losing rook moves, missed prophylaxis/tactic) and includes several 0cp false-positive non-blunders.

715.label: Top boards hang or trade off the bishop that was the critical defender — losing it outright via a move-order slip or surrendering a passed-pawn blockader/king-shield; medium broadens to generic bishop exchanges that merely concede the bishop pair or worsen the structure.

723.label: Top boards are minor pieces (knight ~2/3, bishop ~1/3) hung by a natural developing move that overlooks an immediate pawn-capture or check-fork in a drawn opening; medium broadens to routine/passive moves (castling, repositioning, flank pawns) that neglect the position's tactical demand and bleed material, advantage, or king safety beyond the opening.

735.label: Top positions are uniformly an ignored forced mate-in-1 against the player's own king (a queen–bishop diagonal battery crashing into h7/h2/g2 that the move failed to block); medium blurs this to slower forced mates (M2–M3) and to plain material loss — hanging a rook, allowing a remove-the-defender shot, or greedily grabbing a pawn/piece while the decisive threat loomed.

727.label: Top boards are a quiet (usually queen) move in an already-winning position that skips a decisive rook capture/strike exploiting a loose or overloaded enemy piece (Rxe5/Rxd5/Rxe6/Rxf7); medium keeps the 'winning but played the wrong, safe move' core while the missed blow broadens to sacrifices and forcing combinations (Nxg7, Rxf2) and the played move broadens beyond the queen.

704.label: Top: in a completely won, usually forced-mate position the player makes a slow repositioning move (king march, rook to 7th, queen/bishop relocation) instead of the available winning capture—typically just taking a hanging enemy piece—throwing away the mate; medium: the same urge to play a natural non-forcing move blows only a general win or holdable edge, where the missed best move broadens to quiet positional/defensive/endgame moves and the error sometimes flips to hanging one's own material.

691.label: Top: in lost endgames the king/pawn walks past a free hanging enemy piece (usually a rook, sometimes queen/minor) instead of the only-move capture; medium blurs into the opposite—greedy pawn grabs and pushes that hang the player's own material or allow mate, sometimes in the middlegame.

719.label: Top boards are greedy material grabs that strip a defender and expose one's own king to a decisive enemy-queen attack; medium boards keep the queen-centric theme but blur—some are the same king-exposure hangs, others flip direction to a safe move that misses a tactic winning or trapping the enemy queen.

749.label: Top: pushing the h-pawn (mostly ...h5, one h4) to 'support' a pinned/active bishop on g4/g5 that simply drops to hxg4/hxg5 — the recapture only regains a pawn; medium narrows to ...h5 propping Bg4, refuted by hxg4 hxg4 Ng5 hitting f7.

744.label: At the peak the player is already winning and skips a clean capture of a hanging enemy piece (queen or bishop) — Qxe1, Kxd8, Kxa3, Kxe6 — throwing the win away; at medium it blurs into any imprecise conversion of a won position (tempo loss, wrong king direction, premature pawn push), with a couple of hung-piece and near-zero-loss false positives mixed in.

731.label: At the peak the move loses material outright — a greedy pawn grab or loose developing move punished by a tempo-gaining check (Nxe4→Qa4+, Bg4→Bxf7+ Ng5+) — while at medium it blurs into premature f-pawn pushes (f3, also f4/f6) that merely weaken the king/center and get undermined positionally rather than hanging a piece.

743.label: Top: from a winning position the player declines a free queen capture of an undefended rook—almost always the identical Qxa1+ with check; medium broadens to other missed winning captures (Qxa6, Qxc8, Qxh8, mostly still queen-takes-rook but not always with check) plus a few non-capture tactical/positional/endgame wins.

741.label: Top: a passive developing move (Be2, ...Bg7, ...d6, ...a5, castling) that misses a winning central knight capture—Nxe5 exploiting a loose Bg4 pin or Nxd5 removing a dominant outpost knight; medium keeps the 'quiet move skips a knight tactic' core but broadens to other captures/centralizations (Nxe4, Nexd4, Nbxd4, Nxg6, Ne5) and occasionally to allowing one's own material to fall (trapped rook, Nc7+ fork).

730.label: Top: a slow/non-urgent move (improving a piece or premature castling) ignores an imminent kingside pawn storm and is smashed open by a king-cracking break (g6/f5/fxg5); medium broadens the same failure-to-resolve-tension to central/queenside breaks (e5, cxd5, f5), piece sacrifices opening the king, and missed only-moves—diluted by a couple of pure hanging-piece blunders and one false positive.

756.chip: Missed mate: queen instead of bishop
756.label: Top: a forced kingside mate (Greek-gift Bxh7+/Bg6#) is thrown away by delivering check with the queen rather than the bishop, so the king escapes to f7/h8; medium keeps the identical queen-for-bishop substitution but broadens to other check/capture squares (Bf6+, Bxf7+) and to merely winning rather than mating lines.

750.chip: Hangs material via queen trade (or quiet queen move)
750.label: Top: a quiet queen move that offers a trade which, after the exchange, drops material (loose piece, pawn, fork) or dissolves a winning attack/mate; medium broadens to passive queen moves that simply hang a piece without any trade, plus stray non-queen moves (knight/rook/king) and a few missed defensive/winning resources.

739.chip: Passive endgame move over check (mate→missed win)
739.label: Top: a slow/passive endgame move (often a pawn push or piece-abandoning rook move) walks into a back-rank or cornered-king mate, or loses a pawn race, in a sharp rook endgame; medium broadens to squandering a winning or drawn position by skipping the required forcing check (Rb8+, e4+, Bg4+, etc.).

748.label: TOP: an attacking flank pawn break (g6/b6/g3) opens the player's own king or burns the tempo of a winning tactic, losing material; MEDIUM broadens to central pawn pushes and defender-stripping piece captures (Nxe5, Ng5, Bxf6) that likewise hang material or throw away a forced win.

758.label: Top: a knight is sortied to an advanced central square (d4/e5/e4) that gets kicked by a pawn (c3/f4/d3) and is trapped or lost in the refutation; medium broadens to queen/bishop sorties and other premature/slow moves that variously lose tempo, hang material, or skip a winning tactic.

737.label: Top is razor-tight: an opening move (Bg5, Nxe5, Nfd2, Nxe4, h3, Be7…) ignores the forced Qxd1+/Qxd8+ queen exchange on the open d-file, so the queen trade comes WITH CHECK and leaves the e4/e5 pawn or knight hanging — or concedes the move-order/castling-rights battle; at medium the constant blurs into 'overlooked the opponent's forcing reply' more broadly — zwischenzug Qxd1+ on other files (cxb7, Bg4-trapped), premature exchanges releasing tension (Bxf6), and over-optimistic tempo/sacrifice moves that get refuted (Bxf7+, Bh7+, f3+, Qg5), plus a couple of outright missed wins.

757.label: At the peak the player throws away a forced checkmate by choosing a quiet/natural move instead of the decisive (usually checking) blow — or, in a few top boards, outright hangs a piece by retreating into an undefended square; at medium it blurs to missing any forcing material-winning tactic (queen/rook checks, captures-with-check, forks) in an already-winning position.

753.label: Top: a needless check is played instead of capturing the undefended piece (usually the queen) in a winning position, squandering a forced win; medium broadens to other tempting moves—pawn pushes, developing or repositioning—chosen over the key capture, with the missed target blurring to rook/knight/pawn and several lines now hanging own material.

736.label: Top boards retreat a minor piece (esp. bishop, Bf4) forgoing a winning capture-then-knight-fork combination — a missed win; medium broadens to declining any indicated capture/exchange, where the passed-over move more often leaves the player's own piece hanging.

764.label: Top: an instinctive queen/rook check that throws away a forced mate (or clearly winning position) by handing the king an escape square, when a quiet killer (e.g. Bxf6, h4+, d3, Ne3) kept the win; medium broadens the offending move beyond pure checks — to king walks, captures and defensive consolidations, and to checks that outright hang the checking piece — but the recurring fault stays the same: a hasty forcing move forfeits the forced mate/win.

770.chip: Hangs material to weakening pawn push
770.label: Top is a loosening pawn push (b6/f6/g6/b3) that opens a diagonal or surrenders a key square and loses material to an immediate tactic; medium blurs from the constant 'pawn-move-creates-weakness' core across varied refutations (opened-line discovered attack, trapped piece, or knight fork).

768.label: Top: a passive or premature king move squanders the most efficient win in a K+P endgame (violating 'king must lead the pawn' / opposition, converting a forced mate or won pawn race into a slower win or draw); medium broadens to tempo-wasting rook, queen-check and knight moves that likewise downgrade a forced mate or winning conversion, though several boards are near-0cp non-blunders.

765.label: Top: in a won endgame the player walks past a hanging enemy piece (usually a rook) instead of the trivial king/bishop capture; medium: blurs to missing the only winning move or losing a tempo in pure pawn endgames where no capture is involved.

759.label: Top: a natural queen/piece redeployment ignores or walks into a knight fork or intermezzo that wins the queen (Nxg6, Ne2+, Nxd4, Nxe6, Ne6+, Nh6#); medium blurs to hanging assorted material to varied tactics, plus a few missed material wins and positional/endgame slips.

760.label: At the peak it's a quiet king move that throws away a dead-drawn pawn endgame (failing to capture/blockade a would-be passer, e.g. Kb7 instead of Kxb6); at medium it blurs into misplaced minor-piece moves in equal/drawn positions that drop material (knight to the rim missing the passed-pawn blockade, knight blocking its own bishop's escape), with some non-endgame outliers (allowed fork, missed mate) making the feature genuinely mixed.

778.label: Top: a king move in a pure pawn-race endgame that steps the wrong way (retreats/centralizes instead of escorting or racing), losing a tempo so the opponent's passer queens first; medium keeps the lost-tempo-in-a-race idea but broadens beyond king moves to other endgame moves (rook shifts, pawn pushes) and even blurs into tactical king-exposure errors.

775.label: Top boards are uniformly a knight snatching the e5/e4 pawn in the opening only to be cleanly recaptured (Halloween-gambit / Petrov-style 'free pawn' grab losing piece-for-pawn); medium keeps the same 'hang a knight around a central pawn' core but blurs the mechanism — other central captures (Nxd5), leaving e5 undefended by a knight move (Nd4), or moving a defender/pawn that strands the piece, plus a couple of materially-safe missed wins (Bxf7+, exf4).

782.label: Top: an opening f-pawn advance (fxe5/f5/f4) strips the king's pawn shield and loses material to Qh4+/Qh5+; medium broadens to other king-exposing moves (Bc4, b6, e6, knight retreats) punished by diagonal queen checks (Qa4+/Qb5+/Qh5+), with a few outright forks blurring the pattern.

774.label: Top: a plausible developing/undermining move leaves a minor piece (usually a knight) en prise to an enemy PAWN capture in the opening (e.g. d3/d6 'challenging' a pawn while the pawn just takes the knight); medium blurs to any move that ignores the real refutation—abandoning a defender, weakening the king, greedy captures, or a botched promotion—losing material or a won advantage rather than strictly a pawn-capture hang.

754.label: Top: a clearly winning position where a slow, tempo-wasting move skips the decisive continuation while staying materially safe; medium broadens to merely-better positions where the natural move concedes material or a tactic (fork, trapped/hanging piece, overload) over the refutation.

780.label: Top: captures an enemy rook on the back rank, letting an enemy pawn recapture and promote to a queen (often with check/mate); medium broadens to other captures or pushes that lose material, frequently by springing a passed pawn but blurring into generic hanging/positional concessions.

771.label: Top boards are nearly always declining a forcing queen exchange — usually with check (Qh4+, Qxd4+, Qb5+, Qd3+, Re1+→Qxe1) — that was the one resource to defuse the opponent's king attack; medium blurs this to passive queen retreats and other loose/greedy 'safe' moves that simply fail to neutralize the attack, sometimes hanging material outright.

784.chip: Missed faster win (passer push→any slow move)
784.label: Top: in a winning passed-pawn position, advances the passer instead of the immediate promotion-with-check or intermediate check that wins/mates faster; medium broadens to other slow moves (king sidesteps, queen shuffles, captures) that skip the decisive tactic or allow a defensive resource (perpetual/fork/back-rank), with several 0cp false positives diluting both tiers.

788.label: Top: a quiet, non-forcing move (no capture/check) throws away a clearly winning position by burning a tempo instead of the forcing continuation; medium blurs into passive repositioning from roughly equal positions that cedes initiative and loose pawns.

789.label: Top: a knight is thrust to a central outpost (overwhelmingly e5, also d4/d5/e4) where it's favorably captured/exchanged and material or the advantage collapses; medium keeps the knight-move signature but broadens the square (h5/f4/g3/d6) and mechanism to outright hung knights, defender-removals, and even bishop/king moves that drop a piece.

786.label: Top: a quiet non-forcing move (usually a pawn push like g2-g3 'luft') skips a forced mate or material-winning tactic in an already-winning position; medium broadens to captures/piece moves that abandon a key defender, hanging own material or allowing the opponent's mate.

799.label: Top: already-losing rook endgames where a rook/king move walks into an immediate back-rank rook mate (Rb8#/Rd1#); medium keeps the back-rank mates but broadens to other forced mates — passed-pawn promotion races and king-safety collapses — plus a few that merely squander a winning edge.

795.label: Top boards consistently leave the player's own QUEEN en prise to a counter-capture or zwischenzug while grabbing material or playing a fork (a move-order failure); medium positions broaden the hung piece to rooks/bishops and add back-rank, trapped-piece, and tempo motifs, but the constant is overlooking an opponent counter-tactic that wins the player's own material.

802.label: Top: withdraws a key kingside defender (rook off the file, or pawn-recapture opening a file) so the enemy queen infiltrates with check; medium broadens to any move leaving the own king exposed to a decisive attack, including leaving the king in the danger zone.

800.label: Top fires on king moves in won K+P endgames that should execute precise outflanking/opposition/promotion technique (mostly engine-best 0cp, with a few genuinely missing a faster mate or fastest promotion); medium broadens to other pieces and non-pawn endgames, adding real material/positional losses like a buried bishop, a hung knight, a fork, or a lost opposition tempo.

805.label: Top boards are uniformly forced back-rank checkmates (mostly mate-in-1, a few mate-in-2/3) that the player skips—frequently grabbing material instead of mating; medium keeps the weak-back-rank theme but blurs to longer forced mates (mate-in-3/4) and even non-mating back-rank/winning shots (e.g. Rd8+ winning, Qxf5+ trade).

796.label: Top boards are uniform: in a clearly losing endgame the player makes a king or rook move that leaves a piece (rook/knight/queen) hanging to an immediate free capture, either stepping onto an attacked square or ignoring an already-attacked piece; medium keeps this 'hangs a piece while already lost' core but blurs it — the material loss sometimes only arrives over 2-3 moves of the refutation, the phase isn't strictly endgame, and a few cases are non-material positional/tempo/king-safety slips that merely squander the one saving resource rather than dropping material outright.

806.label: Top: in a won endgame the player ignores a directly hanging enemy piece (usually a rook, sometimes a queen) that could be taken for free and instead plays a quiet king move or pointless check; medium broadens to missing queen captures, missed promotions/underpromotions, and tempo-losing king shuffles—generally skipping the one decisive winning move while staying materially safe.

798.label: Top: a won endgame where the player skips a free capture of a hanging enemy piece (king move instead of Nxc1/Kxe6/Kxd3/Kxf6); medium: broadens to general conversion failures — premature passed-pawn pushes, king misplacement, and even missed forced mates that throw away the win.

811.chip: Hangs rook in exchange sequence (any piece)
811.label: Top: a rook is placed on an open file/back rank and lost to a forced queen-winning exchange or back-rank combo; medium blurs to any piece (knight, bishop, queen) hung into a refuting capture/fork, plus some tempo-loss and missed-win cases.

797.label: Top: a bishop capture (or greedy queen grab) is immediately met by an enemy knight recapturing onto a dominant central outpost (e6/d5/c5/f5) with tempo or a fork on king/queen/rook — a move-order/exchange error; medium broadens to other capturing pieces and recaptures that only improve the opponent's knight positionally, plus a couple of unsound sacrifices that simply drop material to a king recapture.

818.label: Top: in an already-winning position the player ignores a clean knight fork/check (usually Nx+ netting the rook) for a passive or greedy move; medium keeps the 'skipped a forcing win' core but broadens beyond knight forks to any missed forcing tactic — bishop checks, knight-check mating nets, or the correct recapture (e.g. Rxc3+ over bxc3).

762.label: Top: opening positions with a king stuck in the center on the open e-file (often + Bc4–f7 pressure), where the player ignores the danger—either hanging material (Qxg5, allowing Qd4+ fork / Qxf7+) or skipping the consolidating e-file check Qe2+/Qe7+; medium broadens to middlegame e-file tactics, mostly MISSING winning checks (Qxe4+, Qxe6+, Bxg5+) plus a few plainly hung queens, so direction blurs from hung-own to missed-win around the same exposed-king/e-file motif.

815.label: Top is the premature central e5 pawn break (kicking the f6-knight, refuted by ...dxe5 to drop a pawn or wreck the structure); medium keeps the same overeager pawn-thrust idea but broadens the square to c4/b4/d4/h4/e4/d5 and a couple of overextending piece lunges.

822.label: Top: a repositioning/ignoring move leaves a piece (usually a knight) hanging to immediate capture or a short fork while neglecting a tactical threat; medium broadens the hung material to rooks, pawns, greedy queen grabs, trapped pieces, and king moves that abandon defense and walk into forced mate.

830.label: Top: a slow developing/pawn move (castling, ...c6, Bg4, Re1) misses a forcing winning central thrust—almost always ...d4 forking the c3-knight and e3-bishop; medium broadens to any quiet move that squanders the edge by skipping the key break, hanging a central pawn, or permitting a fork/back-rank shot.

823.label: Top: a (usually pawn) capture rips open the player's OWN king and is refuted by a mating attack or queen-winning recapture/discovery; medium: the same self-refuting capture/move idea blurs to ordinary cases where a minor piece simply hangs to a recapture or fork, with king safety no longer central.

804.label: Top: from a winning position (≈74%) the player chooses a slow, natural move — a retreat, prophylaxis, or routine development/pawn-grab — and passes up the forcing tactical win, very often a bishop capture or sacrifice (Bxh6, Bxg8, Bxh3, Bxa3); medium keeps the 'quiet move skips the concrete shot' core but blurs into roughly-equal/drawn positions and adds outright hung pieces (cxd5, trapped Bf7, Bxf2+) and positional/endgame lapses, so the direction splits between missed-win (≈65% safe) and hanging material (≈35%).

832.label: Top boards are pawn-endgame king moves that lose the opposition/key-square (king goes to the wrong square in a precise K+P fight); medium keeps the wrong-king-move idea but blurs to any king maneuver that wastes a tempo in the king march (Kxh2/Kxa3 pawn-grab detours, slow Ka7/b6 routes), with a few non-king tempo/material drops mixed in.

834.chip: Traded into lost pawn endgame (often rook)
834.label: At the peak, the player recaptures/trades the LAST ROOK to liquidate into a clearly lost king-and-pawn endgame (Rxe4, Rxg5, Rxb7, etc.); at medium it blurs to other simplifying captures (knight trades, rook-for-knight, grabbing the wrong piece) and into adjacent lost endgames (single-rook, R-vs-pawns) rather than pure K+P.

827.label: Top: grabs a 'free' but queen-defended piece (typically beside its own king) and gets mated or loses the queen to a recapture-with-check; medium: blurs to any greedy capture or defender-removal that simply drops material to a recapture/fork rather than forcing mate.

812.label: At top, the winning side plays a quiet/alternative queen move and misses a forcing deflection sacrifice (usually a check, e.g. Rg1+/Rxf1+/Bg8+) that wins the enemy queen outright; at medium it broadens to missing any decisive forcing shot in a won position—forced mate, zwischenzug, or a simple winning capture—and a few cases even hang the advantage instead of just skipping it.

833.label: Top boards are tempo-wasting/loosening moves with the king uncastled—especially the ...b6 flank push—punished by a tempo-gaining queen sortie (Qa4+/Qb3) that wins material; medium broadens to any slow move (delaying O-O-O, trapping own piece) that squanders an advantage and concedes material.

835.label: Top boards all play into an immediate, ignored forced checkmate against one's own king (back-rank or king-hunt mating net); medium blurs this to broader sharp king-safety failures — still mostly allowing forced mate, but now also missing one's own forced mate/winning tactic (e.g. Rh1#, Rxa2+) and hanging plain material (Bxf4, Qxf1+) in tactical positions.
