838.label: Top boards are reflexive king-chasing checks (esp. knight, e.g. Ne2+/Nh3+, but also Bh5+/f6+) that let the enemy king reach safety and squander a clearly winning attack instead of the quiet capture/fork; medium blurs the same king-escape error into sacrificial Greek-gift checks (Bxh7+/Be6+) and tempo-wasting checks/grabs (Rg1+, h6+, Nxa2) that toss a winning edge.

819.label: Top: a wrong-direction king move in a lost pawn endgame lets the enemy passed pawn promote (usually with check), converting slow loss into forced mate; medium broadens to other passive defensive moves (rook/knight) and king-safety blunders that walk into corner mating nets, no longer just passed-pawn races.

837.label: Top: a routine opening developing move ignores a free capture of an undefended bishop; medium broadens the free target to rooks/queens and to other ignored tactics (forks, skewers, hanging pawns).

842.label: Top is uniformly a knight sallying to an undefended rim square (Ng5/Nh4/Nh5) that the queen captures for free; medium broadens to other pieces and move-types left hanging to a queen grab — a rook on a5, castling or quiet/pawn moves that abandon a stranded knight, plus a few related blunders (knight trapped on the rim, a fork, a pawn pushed onto a defended square).

826.label: Top: in a winning/equal position the player makes a quiet developing or repositioning move (often a bishop) instead of a sharp central pawn break (d5/e6/e3/e7), forfeiting the win or tempo; medium keeps the 'natural move at a critical moment' theme but broadens the missed solution to other forcing tactics (knight outposts/forks, captures, promotions) and increasingly the quiet move directly hangs material to the refutation.

839.label: Top: a slow non-forcing KING move in a king-and-pawn promotion race that surrenders the decisive tempo so the opponent's passer queens; medium broadens to any slow move (rook/queen/knight/prophylaxis, even a greedy grab) and to missing the forcing resource (check, perpetual, blockade, back-rank) that wins or stops the same race.

846.label: Top: a king move (Ka3/Kh7/Ke8/Kd2) steps into a forced queen+rook mating net or mate-in-1/2/3; medium blurs to king/other moves that merely expose the king to decisive checks, losing material or squandering a winning/defensible position rather than getting cleanly mated.

845.label: Top: a bishop or queen thrust toward the enemy king (h3/h6/g5) that is a premature 'fantasy attack' — abandoning a defensive duty and hanging material (or misplacing the piece / skipping a cleaner tactic); medium keeps the over-ambitious-attack theme but blurs the piece and target, broadening to knight sorties, rook lunges, pawn pushes, and greedy queen grabs that overreach and drop material.

829.label: Top: a piece vacates its defensive square, hanging material to a forcing reply (often a check or fork with tempo); medium keeps the abandon-the-key-square seed but blurs in direction, equally often a materially-safe move that skips a win — missed piece-wins, a missed mate-in-one, and king-safety lapses.

852.label: Top is uniformly a bishop on an open diagonal skipping a free undefended rook to win the exchange; medium keeps 'missed capture of a hanging rook' but broadens the capturer/material (e.g. a queen grabbing a whole free rook on a1) and dilutes with unrelated lapses (hanging own piece, king-safety, tempo loss).

841.label: Top boards drop a full minor piece to a forcing capture/fork sequence after removing a defender or skipping the needed capture (e.g. Bxf3/Nxd2); medium boards keep the overlooked-forcing-reply theme but broaden to mere pawn losses, botched move-orders, unsound sacrifices, and pure tempo/positional concessions.

858.label: TOP: razor-sharp endgames where the ONLY move was to shove the passed pawn to the 7th/promote, but a slow king or piece-centralizing move threw away the forced win or draw; MEDIUM keeps the passed-pawn-race theme but blurs to broader promotion mishandling — premature/wrong promotion (f1=Q into Rxf1), trading off the piece that forces promotion, or king moves that weaken the promotion struggle.

860.chip: Hangs king to mate (broadens to material)
860.label: Top: in already-lost positions a king/pawn move (often back-rank or king-shield weakening) ignores or invites a mating attack, allowing or accelerating forced checkmate; medium keeps the king-exposure theme but blurs to general material loss—hanging a piece/queen, allowing a tactic, or an unsound sacrifice.

853.label: Top: ...Bg4 'attacks' the enemy queen for tempo but hangs the bishop (queen captures, or Nxf6+ deflects its sole defender); medium broadens to knight/pawn attacks on a queen that escapes with an intermezzo check, plus missed queen-captures and other greedy/tactical hangs.

859.label: Top: a pointless/premature queen check squanders a clearly winning position—skipping a stronger capture or quiet move (often a won-endgame conversion via Qxf7+/Qxa8) and letting the king escape or allowing a tempo-gaining interposition; medium broadens to checks that toss away a forced checkmate (wrong check lets the king flee) or hang material, so direction is mixed between missed win and self-inflicted loss.

856.label: Top boards are aggressive captures/sacrifices/thrusts (often a kingside attack like the Greek Gift) that directly hang a piece while the player stands equal-or-better; medium blurs this into quieter, greedier, or recapturing moves that abandon a key defender (or even skip a forced win/mate), so the unifying signature is 'own move loses material' but the attacking flavor dissolves.

857.label: Top boards uniformly miss a mate-in-one (typically Qxh2#/Qxg2# along an open diagonal/file vs a boxed-in king); medium broadens to missing wins generally — squandered won positions, slower-than-mate moves, and attack-dissolving queen trades, with a few hanging-piece/greedy outliers.

848.label: Top: a knight greedily captures a defended central pawn (e4/d5) and is recaptured or forked, losing a piece for a pawn; medium broadens to other pieces and even loose pawn pushes that similarly drop material in the opening.

862.label: Top: a quiet developing/safety move (castling, ...b6, ...Bd7, b3) skips a free ~1-pawn knight grab of a hanging central pawn, almost always Nxe4 (or Nxe5/Nxg4/Nxd5); medium keeps the 'passive move ignores an available tactic' core but the prize broadens to mate-in-one, a clean piece, or a pawn-with-attack, and bleeds into the opposite direction (the quiet move actually hangs material to a fork/back-rank), making it genuinely mixed.

861.label: Top: pure K+P endgames where a defensive king move abandons the opposition/blockade in front of an enemy passed pawn, flipping a dead draw into a forced mate; medium broadens to general king mishandling of passers — passive/tempo-losing king moves, stepping into checks, positions still containing pieces, and milder cp losses (plus a few borderline non-errors).

873.label: Top boards are queen checks (overwhelmingly Qh5+ recaptured by a queen on the open 5th rank) that hang the queen for nothing; medium broadens to checks with any piece — rook/knight/queen — that drop the checking unit to immediate capture or otherwise squander material.

865.label: Top boards hang a piece in the opening via a faulty knight fork or grabbing a defended pawn/square that gets recaptured in a single move; medium boards broaden to any over-aggressive opening sortie — unsound sacrifices and pieces that get trapped/lost over 2-3 moves.

855.label: Top boards are minor-piece sorties (almost always a bishop/knight, frequently 'attacking' a rook) that abandon a defensive job and get refuted by the opponent simply ignoring the illusory threat and counterattacking the king/back rank, costing material or mate; medium blurs the constant in two ways—the moving piece broadens to rooks/queens/pawns, and the error broadens from 'misplaced piece gets captured' to also 'materially-safe redeployment that skips a free winning capture.'

843.label: Top: a winning side misplaces/overextends a rook (Re2, Rc2, Re3, Re7), abandoning king defense so the opponent builds a mating net; medium keeps the 'wreck own king safety while winning' theme but broadens the agent to king walks (Kc1→Rc2#, Ke7, Kd6) and pawn/piece weakening (g6, Ne7), with a couple of outliers (missed mate-in-1, greedy grabs) blurring direction.

869.label: Top: materially-safe king moves in lost king-and-pawn endgames that misjudge opposition/blockade (frequently allowing the opponent's pawn to advance with a tempo-gaining check, e.g. Kb4/Kd2/a5 inviting d5+/c5+); medium keeps the king-move-in-a-lost-endgame core but blurs across endgame types (rook, king-safety, promotion) and includes many near-0cp 'non-blunders', so the unifying error is wrong king placement rather than an actual material drop.

876.label: Top: a king move in a won (usually endgame) position that dawdles instead of finishing — ignoring a forced mate or a hanging-queen capture (several peak boards are even 0cp best-move king walks in Q-vs-R checking races); medium blurs to any slow/non-forcing piece move (bishop, knight, rook, pawn) that merely delays the mate or skips a free winning capture.

870.label: TOP: in a clearly-won opening the player ignores a knight left en prise to a one-move pawn capture (exf6/dxc3/dxc6 winning a full piece) and instead develops/castles; MEDIUM holds the 'overlooked free capture' core but blurs the target to other hanging minors (bishop via cxb4) and the capturer beyond pawns (Qxf6, Bxf6, gxf3), with a few drifting toward king-safety/tempo misses of a winning move.

868.label: Top: in a won endgame, greedily captures the opponent's dangerous passed pawn with the only winning piece (queen/rook/bishop, even via Kx that abandons it), getting recaptured into an insufficient-material/bare-king draw; medium blurs to broader endgame conversion errors — wrong-piece captures, suboptimal pawn trades, or king moves — that squander the winning advantage without fully drawing.

884.label: Top: a capturing exchange (repeatedly ...Rxe1) played to 'simplify' that actually hangs the queen to an existing attacker or to a check-gaining recapture; medium broadens to other captures/defender-moves that lose material to a tactic (zwischenzug gxf3+, undefending a rook, exposing the king) when the player trades expecting a clean simplification.

877.label: Top boards hang a rook or bishop to an immediate one-move recapture (frequently by the enemy king), usually via a flashy check/capture or active placement that ignores the piece is undefended; medium boards broaden the hung unit to any piece (knight, queen) and broaden the refutation from a plain recapture to multi-move tactics like forks, discovered attacks, and exchange-winning combinations.

875.label: Top boards hang a piece (often the queen) by moving away its sole defender or mis-ordering a capture in a winning position; medium boards broaden to hanging pieces via overlooked forks/pins and walk-into-tactic moves, with a few pure missed material wins mixed in.

872.label: Top boards constantly feature a player in a critical/losing position who avoids the liquidating queen trade or queen-capture that was the only saving (or winning) resource — instead retreating/relocating the queen or playing a passive rook move — and hangs material to the refutation; medium blurs this to greedy or careless captures (Qxa5, Qxe4) and file/diagonal-opening moves that walk into a refuting tactic (pin, discovered check, perpetual).

883.label: Top: the QUEEN leaves a critical defensive post—usually a greedy pawn/piece grab or a pointless check—exposing its own king to a forced mating attack or losing the queen; medium broadens to king/rook/pawn moves that vacate a key guard square and allow mate (plus a few positional/draw-throwing outliers).

887.label: Top: player makes a capture (Bxc6/Nxc6/Bxf6 type) or queen move that leaves the own queen attacked/undefended, refuted by a knight grabbing it with check or zwischenzug (Nxf3+, Nxd3+, Nxe4); medium keeps the hung-queen theme but broadens to the queen being taken by any piece (rook Rxb4/Rxb7 or knight Nxc5/Nxd8) without check, with a few near-noise/positional cases.

878.label: Top: a forcing move — almost always a check (Bxf7+, Rh8+, Nc2+, Re1+) or outright sac — that hangs material instead of simply grabbing the free/hanging enemy piece or making the obvious recapture; medium keeps the same skip-the-priority-capture / wrong-move-order theme but blurs beyond checks to non-check tempo losses, greedy/wrong-capture choices, and a few missed in-hand wins.

890.label: Top: a quiet/non-capturing move overlooks an enemy queen hanging for a free capture; medium keeps the same 'missed free win' theme but broadens to also missing hanging rooks, forced mates (mate-in-1/4), and correct move-order or right-piece recaptures.

898.label: Top boards directly degrade own king safety — a king walk into the open center (Kxd2) and a queen move inviting Nb5+tempo and a pawn-storm — while medium positions blur into related self-harming moves (a bishop block that traps the king in the center, a bishop retreat that opens a checking diagonal) and one pure tactical lapse where a self-obstructing knight allows a winning fork on d6.

880.label: Top: a slow rook-doubling/buildup move that forgoes an available forcing check or mate; medium blurs the piece (pawn/knight moves too) and the outcome, sometimes outright hanging material to the refutation rather than just skipping a win.

885.label: At the peak (and in the medium sample) the constant is a premature ...f7-f5 pawn thrust in the opening that weakens the king/d5-square and concedes material or advantage from an equal-or-winning position; the broader top set blurs away from f5 into other opening moves (g3, d2, Nd5, Bb4, c5) that similarly hang own material in a winning/equal position.

879.label: Top: a knight greedily captures a pawn (often a passer) in a drawn position and is recaptured, liquidating into a clearly lost king-and-pawn endgame; medium blurs to broader piece blunders—misplaced/hung knights and other pieces allowing forks, mates, or missing wins—that flip a drawn or won result.

907.label: Top boards are pawn-endgame king-march/pawn-race tempo errors that squander a win (or are near-zero-loss moves in already-lost races), the constant being a natural king move or pawn push that loses a critical tempo or takes the wrong direction; at medium this blurs to rook and minor-piece endgames, blockade/promotion-timing failures, and even missed tactical wins and a queen blunder into mate.

888.label: At the peak the player gives up a piece for a flawed attack in a winning/equal position—usually a bishop, with one outlier being a sound rook trade and another a queen trade that merely misses mate; medium narrows to the textbook unsound Bxf7/Bxf2+ king-attack sacrifices that simply hang the bishop for a pawn.

909.label: Top boards consistently drop a full piece by moving into a capture or stripping its defender, while medium boards blur into lesser material (pawn/exchange), a missed faster win, and king-safety collapses that allow forced mate.

914.label: Top boards are passive or misplaced ROOK moves (Rc5/Rd4/Ra7/Rg1, or skipping Rxh7/Rd1+) that surrender the tempo and activity needed for active defense, mostly in rook/pawn endgames letting the opponent's passer or activity win; medium blurs to king/pawn/bishop/knight moves (Kc5, Ke7, b6, a3, Nxd5) that likewise forfeit the only defensive resource and concede a passed-pawn race.

891.label: Top: player declines a clearly-best simplifying/saving QUEEN TRADE (keeping the queen active, grabbing a pawn, or giving a free check) and concedes a clean pawn or small tactic; medium broadens so the avoided trade now hangs the queen outright, walks into forced mate, or drops the queen to a fork.

897.label: Top boards leave a piece directly hanging to an immediate one-move capture (usually a knight/king move that abandons a guard or opens a line—often a bishop snapping it on a diagonal); medium broadens to the same self-weakening neglect but the material is lost over a 2-3 move refutation, blurring into greedy pawn-grabs, king-exposure, and tempo-losing moves.

919.label: Top: in an already-winning position, skips the one decisive forcing capture-with-check (recurringly Qxe6+ taking the key defensive bishop) and plays a slow/aimless move, throwing away a forced mate or clean material win; medium keeps the 'had a forcing winner but didn't play it' core but broadens to missing mate-in-1, intermezzo/winning checks (Qb3+, Ra3+, Qd5+) and even reflexive non-mating checks, with a couple of cases shading into hanging material outright.

901.label: Top: a king tuck or king-exposing defensive move walks into a forced, usually immediate checkmate (back-rank/king-safety); medium keeps the king-safety theme but blurs to slower mates and moves that simply hang material.

921.label: Top boards are all unsound opening piece-sacs/grabs (overwhelmingly Nxf7, plus Bxd4/Bxc7 pawn-grabs) that drop a minor piece for a pawn in a drawn position; medium blurs the peak by keeping the 'hangs own material' core but broadening to any hung piece (rook on h8/d8, bishop) and even walking into mate across the middlegame/endgame.

920.label: Top: a flashy forcing check (capture-check or 'fork' check) that hangs own material outright instead of the simple capture; medium keeps the pointless-check theme but broadens the cost from hung piece to squandering a forced mate/win (and occasional bad trade/tempo checks).

913.label: Top: a pawn push (f4/f5/d6) skips the needed e-file capture, dropping a central pawn or opening lines onto the king; medium broadens to any quiet/developing move that ignores central tension and gets refuted by a fork, discovered attack, or favorable opponent capture.

930.label: Top boards consistently hang a central d5/e5 pawn by playing a non-capturing pawn/piece move instead of the forced resolving capture (dxe4/dxe5), refuted by a simple pawn grab; medium keeps the same 'failed to resolve central tension' error but blurs the punishment to chased pieces (...e4), pawn forks, and Qh5+ king hits.

935.label: Top: capturing/trading a powerful central pawn (e/d, often en passant like exf6/exd3/dxe6) that releases central tension and squanders a winning position; medium broadens to any premature pawn move—flank captures (cxb6, hxg4, bxc3) or pushes (f4, b6, e4, d6)—that loosens the structure or opens lines for the opponent.

931.label: Top: in an already-losing pawn-promotion race the king marches the wrong way, wasting the single tempo needed for counterplay so the enemy passer queens uncontested; medium keeps some wrong-direction endgame king moves (Kf4, Kf2, Kb6, g4 move-order) but blurs into assorted material-losing blunders — hanging pieces, walking into forks/discovered checks, and greedy grabs.

927.label: Top boards are uniform: a knight grabs the b4/b5 pawn (Nxb4 / Ncxb5) and is recaptured by the a- or c-pawn, dropping a full minor piece for one pawn; medium blurs the mechanism to other greedy/loose minor-piece play — bishop pawn-grabs (Bxb4, Bxg4), overextended Nd4 outposts that get trapped, and moves that abandon a defended piece — but the constant is netting a minor piece down.

926.chip: Hangs piece on forcing check (often queen)
926.label: Top: a queen check (usually a capture-check) that hangs the queen to a simple king recapture, blowing a forced mate; medium broadens to any piece's greedy check or capture that drops material to a short refutation (or merely squanders the win).

923.chip: Hangs rook to forcing reply (any piece)
923.label: Top: rook moves in lost endgames that walk into a forcing capture-with-check or exchange that loses the rook/decides the game; medium broadens to other pieces (knight, king into mating nets) and dilutes into purposeless tempo-losing checks/moves that merely accelerate the loss.

937.label: Top: a piece (usually the queen) vacates a square where it tactically guarded a piece or covered an infiltration square, hanging material or allowing a decisive enemy queen check (Qxf2, Qe3+, Qxe8); medium broadens to any piece/pawn move (f4, g6, Kh6, b6, Nh2, wrong-piece recaptures) that surrenders a key square and lets the opponent infiltrate or win material positionally — with a couple of non-blunders mixed in.

893.chip: Pawn chase lets bishop escape (queen at medium)
893.label: Top: a pawn thrust (usually f3/g4/b5) is played to 'put the question' to an enemy bishop, which calmly retreats to safety—and in the sharpest cases that bishop was actually hanging and could have just been captured for free (Qxg4/cxb4/fxg5); medium broadens to pawn-chasing the queen (b4 vs Qa5) and other premature pawn pushes/trades that the opponent simply sidesteps or punishes.

942.label: Top: opening 'tempo'/developing moves (pawn or minor-piece) that strip a defender or open a diagonal, leaving a pawn/piece en prise to the enemy QUEEN (frequently a queen-check fork or grab of the corner rook); medium broadens beyond the opening to middlegame/endgame king-safety-weakening moves and queens escaping an attack to capture, still typically losing material to a queen raid.

939.label: At the peak it's a won endgame where a forcing queen/rook check hangs the moving piece to immediate capture (e.g. Qe6+→Rxe6, Qe3+→Rxe3); at medium it blurs into other squandered wins—rook/king moves and premature checks that hang material or miss a faster mate while still materially winning.

918.label: Top: in a won position, ignores a free hanging enemy queen (Bxc3/Qxd8/Qxa6 etc.) and usually hangs own queen in return; medium keeps the 'won game, decisive move skipped' theme but blurs to overlooking other free material (rook/exchange), greedy pawn-grabs, missed mates, trapped pieces and tempo losses.

928.label: Top: king-safety neglect that walks into immediate mate-in-1 (king tucked into a mating net, or the sole back-rank/diagonal defender removed), with a couple of outright hung major pieces; medium: same neglect punished by a forced mate several moves out (often a small mate-vs-mate eval swing) via pawn pushes, greedy captures, or sideways king walks.

925.label: Top boards: a quiet, weakening, or over-ambitious move that hangs material—often a fork or free capture exploiting a removed defender or released pawn tension; medium boards broaden to passive tempo-loss and positional moves that squander the advantage without directly losing material.

949.label: At the peak, the player is in a clearly winning position and plays a routine developing/castling move instead of a concrete forcing material-winning shot (typically Qe5+ snapping the a1-rook or Be4 hitting the undefended a8-rook on an open line); at medium it broadens to any natural-looking move that throws away a winning edge by missing the single precise continuation — overlooked tactics, tempo-losing piece moves, or unsound sacrifices — rather than a clean rook-grab.

946.label: Top: Black's f6-knight, attacked by the e5 pawn, jumps to e4 (or d5/g8/h5) instead of the saving ...d5 break and is won by a tempo move or immediate capture; medium broadens to any piece — bishop, queen, or pawn — moved onto a square where it hangs or runs into a decisive tactic.

952.label: At the peak the player hangs the QUEEN by moving it directly to an undefended square (clean one-move blunder); at medium it blurs into hanging any piece — and increasingly INDIRECTLY, by moving a defender, opening a line/back rank, or wrong capture order, sometimes even allowing mate.

950.label: Top boards miss a knight (occasionally bishop) fork delivered with check that wins a rook/queen/exchange; medium boards broaden to any missed winning forcing-check tactic — still forks, but also deflections, intermezzos, and simplifying checks into won endgames.

956.label: Top: a quiet/greedy move that ignores an immediate one-move mate on the open diagonal into the castled king (Qh7#/Qh2#/Qg2#), where g6/g3 was the only defense; medium: broadens to multi-move kingside mating attacks and h7-infiltration material wins, plus a few adjacent material-losing tactics (knight forks, trapped queens).

948.label: At the peak the player declines the decisive rook exchange (Rxf5/Rxe4/Rxe5) that simplifies a winning—or once drawn—endgame into a won/drawn pawn ending; at medium activation this blurs into any passive or wrong king/rook conversion move, sometimes in already-lost positions, mixing missed-wins with outright hangs.

938.label: Top boards relocate/develop a minor piece (bishop or knight) onto a square where a pawn advance hits it with tempo and wins it outright; medium broadens to any passive or tempo-losing move (queen retreats, quiet pawn moves, greedy grabs) refuted by a forcing tactic, sometimes only a large eval drop rather than direct material loss—so the set is genuinely mixed between true hangs and positional/tempo errors.

979.label: Top boards consistently release the tension with a trade (Bxc6/Nxf8) and miss a knight leap to d5 that forks/attacks the queen for a clean win; medium blurs to capturing the wrong pawn/piece while still missing the Nxd5 that wins a pawn with tempo on the queen.

947.label: Top: a knight grabs a hanging bishop (Ne4xd2-style) and recaptures into equality, missing a winning knight fork or zwischenzug; medium broadens to any tempting capture or recapture (often with check, any piece) that trades into equality while overlooking the stronger tactic, mate, positional improvement, or correct move-order.

977.label: Top boards are premature passed-pawn pushes in pure pawn endgames where the pawn is simply blockaded by the king or outraced (throwing away a win/draw); medium broadens to rook endgames and middlegame positions where the same hasty push additionally walks into a tactical refutation (Rh6+ deflection, Rxg2+, Ne5+) or skips a stronger plan (king activation, exchange sac) rather than just being blockaded.

985.label: Top: an opening position where the player skips the free central-pawn grab Qxd4 (once Qxd5) and instead plays a developing/queen move; medium broadens to missing any available free material or short tactic — hanging pawns/pieces, knight forks, and cxd5/Qxe4-type pawn wins.

971.label: Top: a queen check to the rim (Qh8+/Qh1+/Qa8+/Qa1+) that the king calmly sidesteps, stranding the queen offside and often forcing a queen-for-rook trade; medium broadens to rook checks, non-check material grabs, and wrong-piece checks that skip a forced mate (Rc7#, Qc6#, Bg6#).

968.chip: Released pawn tension into recapture (often pawn endgame)
968.label: Top: in pawn endgames a pawn capture (often a check) releases the tension and lets the enemy king recapture toward the center into a winning, active K+P position; medium broadens to pawn captures/pushes in passed-pawn and middlegame structures that concede a favorable recapture or connected passers, with several near-0cp non-errors mixed in.

986.label: Top: a natural opening move (castle/develop) leaves an undefended bishop hanging—usually in unresolved bishop-vs-bishop tension—to a free one-ply capture; medium broadens to other minor pieces and short tactical motifs (forks, pins, trapped/overloaded bishops).

943.label: TOP: a capture/attacking move (usually a bishop, e.g. Bxf6) hangs the QUEEN by overlooking the opponent's forcing in-between reply — typically an enemy knight's intermediate capture, fork, or discovered/back-rank check (Nxf3+, Nxd3, Nxf2+, Nxb6+), where the player should have eliminated that knight (Nxe5) first. MEDIUM: blurs to hanging ANY piece (rook, bishop, even just a pawn) via plainer overlooked recaptures and forks, and bleeds into tempo/positional losses (a3, Be4, h5) rather than a strict zwischenzug.

967.label: Top: in a clearly winning position, a quiet queen/developing/castling move skips a decisive pawn break (e5/d5/e4/f4, often exploiting a pin) that wins material; medium broadens the missed blow to other winning tactics—forks (Nxe6, Qa4+), mating/attacking threats, wrong recaptures—with a minority that outright hang material.

963.label: Top: a routine opening developing move ignores a concrete forcing capture (often of a strong centralized e5 knight), usually missing a clear win; medium keeps the same quiet-developer habit but blurs into the middlegame across a wider tactic range (forks, pins, exchange sacs) and more often hangs own material via the refutation.

984.label: At the peak it is consistently liquidating the sole blockading minor piece (usually a knight, sometimes a bishop) by capturing/trading into a lost king-and-pawn endgame where White's passers run; at medium it blurs into abandoning the king's shelter or leaving a defender hanging, conceding material or allowing forced mate.

997.label: Top: a routine opening developing move (or premature ...Bxf2+/castling) leaves an undefended minor piece—almost always a bishop, often the c5 bishop grabbed by bxc5 or a c4 bishop by dxc4—to be won for free; medium blurs to hanging knights and rooks (e.g. to a skewer) and even missing free captures outside the opening.

994.label: Top: a slow pawn-push or king move throws away a won K+P promotion race, frequently by failing to capture the piece blockading the queening square (Kxg7/Kxa2/Kxb5); medium broadens to any tempo loss in passed-pawn races (repositioning the king instead of immediately pushing one's own passer), but the cluster is noisy — several 'mistakes' are actually 0cp best moves and one is an unrelated back-rank mate.

989.chip: Hangs material to overlooked tactic (often piece)
989.label: Top boards play a natural developing/quiet move that hangs a clean piece or the exchange to a forcing tactic (frequently a knight fork or interference); medium broadens to softer outcomes — positional pawn sacrifices, trapped pieces, slow exchange leaks, and occasional missed wins — where the refutation is less sharply forcing.

999.label: Top boards uniformly skip a forcing knight fork delivering check that wins the exchange/rook (or a full piece); medium blurs to forks netting only a pawn, other knight maneuvers, and a few non-knight tactics (back-rank/overload), including occasional hangs into the opponent's fork.

993.chip: Squandered win via forcing trade/check (broadens to hangs)
993.label: Top: a tempting forcing capture/check — usually a rook (or queen) trade with check — that simplifies a clearly winning position down to equality (often by removing a back-rank/key defender); medium blurs to any greedy capture or pointless check that outright hangs a piece (queen/rook) or throws away a forced mate.

992.label: Top boards are near-identical opening bishop sorties to g4/g5 that 'attack' the enemy queen for an illusory tempo and then either lose the piece (queen escapes, often via the Nxf6+ deflection or Qxb7/removal-of-guard) or simply waste tempi; medium broadens to other pieces making the same unsound tempo-attack on the queen (Nc5, Rb6, Qd7, Be4/Bc4/Bh4) that hang material or squander a winning edge, and occasionally just miss a cleaner capture.

988.label: Top boards are consistently an opening minor-piece or queen relocated to a passive/exploitable square that hands back a clear edge to a refuting central break or tactic; at medium this blurs into rook misplacements, slow pawn moves, ignored forks, missed winning captures, and endgame inaccuracies.

1000.label: Top: in a winning position the player plays a non-checking move (often a capture) and skips an immediately available forced mate, usually mate-in-1 to mate-in-3; medium broadens to skipping forced wins generally — still mostly missed mates but also material-winning forcing/check sequences (e.g. Nd6+, Qxf2+) and faster-mate inaccuracies.

998.label: Top: Black abandons or fails to support the e4 outpost knight in open Italian/Two Knights lines and is refuted by central blows (Nxe5, Qh5+, e-file pins); medium broadens to any under-defended central knight lost via deflection of its lone defender (...c4), forks, or tempo-losing retreats.

990.label: At the peak a king/bishop move in an already-lost endgame directly hangs a piece (bishop, rook, knight, even queen) over a short refutation; at medium it blurs to passive moves that let a passed pawn promote or a tactical fork/deflection win the material, all accelerating an already-losing endgame into a hopeless one.

1003.label: Top: a self-exposing move (usually a king walk or removing the one defensive check/escape square) that turns a lost-but-playable or drawn position into forced mate; medium blurs this to any decisive own-material blunder — still some king-hunt/mate-in-1, but increasingly just hanging a piece to a check/fork or letting a hard endgame collapse on eval.

1010.chip: Hangs material on quiet pawn move
1010.label: Top: a prophylactic 'luft' pawn move (h3/g3, f4) ignores an immediate tactical demand and hangs a piece—usually a rook—to a simple capture; medium keeps the same 'made a slow/non-forcing move instead of the only critical one' idea but blurs to king moves, wrong captures, and other quiet plays that drop varied material (pawn/exchange/piece) or skip a forcing tactic.

983.label: Top: a plan-based or quiet move (pawn push, king step, development) hangs a full piece or skips an elementary winning capture/mate; medium: the same habit blurs into subtler positional, tempo, or single-pawn losses.

995.label: Top: a quiet pawn/king move in a won rook endgame leaves the player's own rook en prise (often a mutual rook-capture race), so the rook is lost; medium broadens to simply not grabbing a free hanging rook (occasionally a bishop) that then escapes — i.e. a missed win rather than an outright hang.

982.label: Top: a routine recapture/piece-trade (often Bxc4/Bxd5 killing a b5-fork) squanders a clearly winning position by skipping the decisive tactic; medium broadens to outright hanging a piece by moving away its defender (or a greedy pawn grab).

1016.label: Top: in a winning opening position the player skips the crushing Qh5+/Qh4+ check that punishes an f-pawn-weakened king (typically winning the h8 rook or launching a mating attack) by playing a quiet knight retreat/developing move; medium keeps the same 'skipped forcing queen-check' theme but broadens beyond the kingside diagonal to other winning queen checks (e.g. Qa4+ snagging a loose knight, or a missed mate).

1001.label: Top: a king/pawn move in a critical passed-pawn endgame ignores the single saving or winning resource (the right pawn push or the capture stopping the enemy passer), losing the race; medium broadens to misplaced rooks/queens and slow moves that abandon the passer or back the wrong plan.

1006.label: Top: a clearly winning position thrown away by a slow non-forcing move (often a pawn push) instead of the one decisive continuation; medium keeps the tempo-loss theme but broadens to king moves, material-hanging moves, bad trades, and merely-equal positions.

1009.label: Top boards are uniformly already-lost positions where the player fails the single critical defensive task against an enemy passed pawn—wasting a tempo (h4, Nxa3, c4) or hanging a piece (Kg7, Ba4, Rb5) or walking into a capture-promotion (Ra8→bxa8=Q)—and the pawn queens; medium boards keep the lost-position/passed-pawn-promotion core (cxb1=Q, a8=Q, b6 passer) but blur outward to other decisive blunders in losing positions such as king-safety checks (Ke7→Qg5+), trapped pieces (Bc5), and discovered-attack mates (Qe3) beyond pure promotion races.

1019.chip: Hangs queen on open file (any line)
1019.label: Top boards consistently hang the queen on an open (usually d-) file to an enemy rook—often via a capture-direction error (dxc3/dxc5/cxb4/dxc6) that opens the file or by parking the queen on it; medium broadens to the queen hung on any open line/rank to a rook, knight, or bishop, plus a few related greedy queen captures and missed wins.

1023.label: Top: king or piece vacates the critical square blockading an enemy passed pawn (gxf4, Kf4, Ng2, Bb2, Kd4, Nb3...), letting it queen by force in the endgame; medium blurs to neglecting any key defensive duty — failing prophylaxis/square-control or even leaving a piece hanging — so the opponent's main plan crashes through.

1008.label: Top: a queen relocation deserts a back-rank rook (forcing Rxe1#/Rxa1# or dropping it outright) in a winning position; medium blurs the deserter to rooks/bishops/pawns abandoning any defensive duty or key file, squandering the win via hung material, missed tactics, or positional collapse.

1021.label: Top boards are forcing queen/rook checks that are materially safe but let the king escape and forfeit a faster forced mate or stronger quiet move (tempo loss); medium broadens to the same 'patzer sees a check' impulse where the check now actively hangs the checking piece (Bxa5, Nxe6) or trades/squanders a winning position.

1014.label: At the peak, in a losing pawn/promotion endgame the player plays a passive non-capturing move and skips the one saving king-capture of a dangerous pawn or rook (Kxf6/Kxc5/Kxb3/Kxg7/Kxa2/Kxd7/Kxh2), losing the race a tempo too late; at medium it broadens to any tempo-wasting or mispositioned endgame move (king retreat, pawn-sacrifice, correct rook/king placement) that fails to stop the opponent's passed pawn or mating net, where the precise resource is no longer a capture.

1027.label: Top: a king move steps onto a more exposed square, walking into a mating net or losing material to a forcing refutation; medium broadens to any passive/misplaced piece move (rook or queen) that neglects the key threat and gets punished tactically.

1043.label: Top: a queen-for-queen capture/check that liquidates into a lost (or drawn) K+P pawn endgame, throwing away an available perpetual-check draw or counterplay; medium keeps the 'trade queens into a losing position' core but broadens to non-pawn endgames, down-material trades, and queen trades that walk into a mating net.

1029.label: Top boards are the king itself walking into the open center (Ke7 dodging Qh5, Kd1/Kd2/Ke2) and getting mated/forked by coordinated queen+knight checks; medium broadens to any king-weakening move — pawn pushes (h3/f4), retreats, or vacating defenders — that exposes the king to a decisive check sequence (with a few stray hanging-pawn/missed-win cases).

1031.label: Top boards are almost uniformly a premature knight sortie to b4/b5 refuted by a queen check on the a-file (Qa4+/Qa5+) that wins the piece or forces it back with two lost tempi; medium blurs the target square/piece to other premature minor-piece lunges in the opening (Ng4 hanging to Qxg4, Bh3 surrendering the center) that drop material or tempo.

1017.label: Top: uniformly QUEEN moves (centralize/trade-offer/consolidate) in endgames that throw away a won or equal position, punished by a forcing check, a perpetual, or a queen trade into a lost pawn ending; medium keeps the 'tidy-up move squanders the endgame to an overlooked forcing refutation' idea but broadens the piece (rook/knight/king/pawn) and the consequence (now including outright mate).

1039.label: Top boards uniformly leave a directly undefended enemy queen uncaptured (one-move free-queen grabs like Qxh4/Nxg5/Rxa3); medium broadens to queens still winnable but via slightly less direct means—knight forks, perpetual-prevention, or forcing queen trades—while the core error stays 'ignored a free/winning queen.'

1018.label: Top: a winning position (usually a kingside/mating attack) is thrown away by a quiet retreat, prophylaxis, or material grab that ignores a decisive attacking blow (Bxh7+, Bh6, Qh2, Bxg7, Qxg7#); medium broadens to missing any decisive resource — a winning capture (Qxa2), passed-pawn push (f7), or centralizing tactic — and sometimes to a move that hangs material outright or lets the opponent attack the player's own king.

1026.label: At the peak the player is already winning and overlooks a forced checkmate (usually mate-in-one) by greedily snatching material—queen/rook—or playing a natural developing move; at medium strength this blurs into any failure to find the strongest winning continuation in a favorable position (greedy pawn/material grabs, wrong checks that dissolve the mating net, tempo-losing or positional slips).

1013.label: Constant: player captures with their bishop and is worse after the forced recapture; top boards skew to outright material loss (bishop hung for a pawn on g2/b7/g7, or recapture winning more), while medium blurs into materially-even but unfavorable trades whose recapture activates the opponent's previously-passive bishop on the long diagonal.

1052.label: Top: uniformly hangs an attacked bishop—almost always the b5/b4/a-file pawn capturing a light/dark-squared bishop that needed the Bb3/Bb6 retreat; medium keeps the 'left own material hanging' core but broadens the dropped unit to knights and pawns (forks, recaptures, undefended center pawns) beyond just bishops.

1057.chip: Hangs material on a check (often queen)
1057.label: Every board is a 'patzer sees a check' blunder; at the top it's a queen check that hangs the queen itself or burns the decisive/holding tempo, while at medium it blurs to minor-piece sacrifice checks and checks played instead of a simple winning capture.

1049.chip: Hangs queen, greedy capture (broadens at medium)
1049.label: At the peak, a greedy pawn capture (dxe7/dxc6/dxc3) opens the d-file or f2-diagonal to the player's OWN undefended queen and loses it (Bxf2+ deflection or direct Qxd-file); at medium the mechanism blurs — non-pawn captures/retreats that ignore a tactical threat lose broader material (queen, exchange, or piece) via opened lines, knight forks, queen-traps, or king-safety attacks.

1046.label: Top is tightly clustered: in won endgames the queen (or rook) captures the opponent's dangerous passed pawn with check and is simply recaptured, often turning a win into a draw/trade — though several flagged boards are actually the correct liquidation; medium blurs into unrelated premature moves that throw away the advantage (Bxf3 into a Bb5 pin, Kc6 into d5+, a tempo-losing Ke3).

1058.label: At the peak the move ignores a direct threat against the king — allowing a forced mate on the h-file or a Greek-Gift sacrifice — while at medium activation it blurs into garden-variety blunders that simply hang a minor piece (or trap the queen / drop a passed pawn) by overlooking the opponent's immediate forcing refutation; in all cases the player walks into lost material that was averted by the engine's best move.

1050.label: Top: a minor piece greedily grabs a central (usually d-file) pawn in the opening and hangs to the queen's recapture (Qxd); medium broadens to assorted careless opening/early-middlegame moves that drop material to a wider mix of refutations (forks, discovered attacks, king-side/king-safety collapses) rather than a clean queen recapture.

1047.label: Top boards are slow king moves in rook endgames that waste the one tempo needed for a winning/drawing rook tactic; medium broadens to any passive or premature move (pawn pushes, queen moves, some hanging pieces) that skips the position's required active resource.

1064.label: Top: a forced mate (usually mate-in-1) is thrown away by grabbing material with an obvious capture (queen/rook/bishop/knight) or a tempting fork; medium keeps the same 'forced mate squandered' core but the culprit blurs from greedy captures to any inferior move — a slow developing move, the wrong check, or a non-forcing centralization (with one case missing a winning exchange rather than mate).

1044.label: Top: a dominant (usually dark-squared) bishop captures a rook on f8 to win the exchange, abandoning a forced mate or the attacking piece; medium broadens to other greedy material grabs (knight-for-bishop trades, taking the exchange over a full piece, or capturing into a counter-tactic) that net nominal material while surrendering a dominant piece, initiative, or a bigger win.

1060.label: Top: a passive, tempo-wasting move (slow king/rook shuffle instead of a pawn push, king march, or check) squanders a forced mate—frequently a back-rank or passed-pawn race—from a clearly winning position; medium keeps the 'winning position thrown away by a slow move' core but broadens to discarding any winning edge—missing forcing sequences, allowing perpetual/trades/simplification, and sometimes outright hanging material in the refutation.

1063.chip: Hangs material on bishop move (Be6/Be3 peak)
1063.label: Top: developing the bishop to e6/e3 loses material to the d5 pawn-fork or a Bxe3/fxe3 recapture; medium broadens to assorted bishop (and a few minor-piece) moves that hang material via forks, trades, overloads, or a missed capture.

1071.label: Top fires on moves that fatally compromise the king's safety with the king still exposed/uncastled — chiefly f-pawn advances (f3/f4) tearing the king's shield, plus a king-exposure neglect (b8c6 instead of Kc8); medium narrows to the f3 push that blocks development and delays castling, inviting the central break/refutation.

1077.label: Top is uniformly hanging the queen — either moving it onto an attacked square or capturing/removing the piece that defended or blocked the line to it (Qg3, Bxg5, Nxf6, exd5, Bxb7); medium keeps the queen-loss theme (move-order/blocked-defender drops like Rxc6, Bxe5) but blurs to also include greedy captures that walk into a forced mate (bxc5→Rh1#, Nxg6→Qg7#).

1065.label: Top boards are near-identical recaptures like hxg6 that open the h-file to a queen on h5, hanging the undefended h8 rook (Qxh8); medium keeps the 'natural move leaves own material en prise' core but blurs the piece and motif — king/pawn/queen moves that drop a knight, exchange, or rook to a simple capture or short refutation.

1061.label: Top boards consistently miss a winning kingside bishop capture/sacrifice—usually Bxh3 (also Bxh6/Bxg6)—from a winning/unclear position, playing a passive bishop retreat or wrong move-order instead; medium broadens to the Greek Gift Bxh7+ and other missed tactics, and increasingly the chosen move itself hangs material (rook on g4, allowing Nxc7 fork or Qxe5).

1073.label: Top boards hang a piece outright to an overlooked capture or tempo-check; medium boards broaden to eval-dropping king-safety/tempo/positional (even endgame) moves that concede material or advantage more slowly.

1059.label: Top boards are constant knight checks (Na6+/Ng5+/Nd7+) that ignore a winning discovered check and leave the knight hanging while the king escapes; medium broadens to queen/king/pawn checks and self-trapping moves that likewise let the king slip away and squander the win, blurring between hung material and a missed forced win.

1082.label: Top boards are nearly all a knight greedily grabbing the central e5 pawn in the opening only to be simply recaptured by Nxe5 (sometimes via an e-file pin against the uncastled king), losing a full piece for a pawn; medium broadens to other greedy/central captures (Qxe4, Nxe4, Nxf2, Bxf5) and opening piece moves that hang material to recapture, pin, or fork.

1081.label: Top boards are a clean missed knight fork winning material—almost always leaping in to fork both enemy rooks (or queen+rook) for the exchange while the player instead made a quiet/natural move; medium keeps the knight-fork core (Nxe5+, Nb6) but blurs to other missed forcing material-wins—deflecting checks, in-between move-orders (Bxf7+ first), and forcing sacrifices (...Bxf2+, ...d2+).

1083.label: Top: a greedy capture or defender-shuffle that abandons the first/back rank, walking into a forced back-rank checkmate (no luft); medium blurs the same defender-removal idea into broader king-safety collapses (Kh1/g5 mating nets, queen/back-rank infiltration) plus a few deflection-style material losses.

1080.label: Top: in a clearly won endgame the player makes an idle pawn push / king move / pointless check instead of simply grabbing a hanging enemy ROOK, throwing away or slowing the win; medium keeps the 'won-endgame-skips-the-easiest-win' theme but blurs the missed target to knights/queens and even to non-capture wins (interference, king-leads-pawn technique, capture-with-check).

1095.label: Top: greedily grabs material (usually with the queen) while missing a forced back-rank mate; medium broadens to any move (checks, attacks, queen trades) that skips a forced mate or the single strongest winning shot.

1069.label: Top: pure king-and-pawn endgames where a quiet pawn push (g5) or wrong king march hangs a pawn or lets the opposing passed pawn through, converting a draw/holdable loss into a loss; medium broadens to rook/minor-piece endgames and king-routing slips that likewise fail to blockade or catch the passer.

1075.label: Top boards consistently squander a winning position by missing a forced mate or king-hunt — playing a slow consolidating or materialistic move (Qxf2, axb3, Rg1) instead of the forcing blow; medium boards blur into overlooking the single critical move more generally: missed material-winning tactics (Nxe5, Qxe5), premature/positional errors (Qd5, Kf7, a3+), and natural moves that allow counterplay or hang material (b4, h6).

1085.chip: Hangs piece in active endgame (often rook)
1085.label: Top fires on a loosening piece move that concedes decisive material or tempo in king-active endgames (bishop hung to a pawn, rooks left uncoordinated, king march/discovered-check refutations); medium narrows to the concrete case of a rook stranded and lost after a misjudged endgame move.

1107.label: Top: in a dead-lost endgame the king flees to the corner/rim (Ka7, Ka8, Ke5, Kg7, Kh5), decentralizing and shortening resistance or accelerating mate; medium broadens to any passive/non-optimal king (or even pawn) move that loses a tempo in an already-lost endgame rather than maximizing defensive coordination.

1067.label: Top: a quiet king move in a lost K+P/passed-pawn endgame that loses the king-race or mis-blockades, letting the enemy passer promote (often WITH CHECK) into forced mate; medium broadens to other passive pawn/piece moves—and even still-winning positions—that likewise ignore the decisive threat, whether an unstoppable passer or a king-safety/mating net.

1110.label: Top boards play a passive/quiet move (a3, b3, Kc2) that skips the decisive Rxf7 grabbing the f7-pawn and the 7th rank; medium broadens to skipping Rxd3, which captures a hanging piece/forces mate — i.e., any materially-safe move that forgoes a winning rook capture.

1078.label: Top boards are queen moves that hang or trade the queen and squander a winning position (king-safety / hanging-piece themes constant at the peak); medium broadens to any piece blundering material to a forcing reply — fork, skewer, discovered attack, trapped piece, or back-rank mate.

1099.label: Top: a slow/quiet pawn move (b3, c3, h3, b4) skips a forcing queen check (Qa4+/Qb5+/Qh5+) that would exploit the opponent's uncastled king before it castles; medium keeps the exposed-king theme but broadens beyond the queen check to other tempo-misses, non-queen checks and knight forks against the stuck king (with a few outliers where the player even hangs own material trying to attack).

1111.label: Top: king-safety blunders—usually a king move (Kc5, O-O-O, fxg4, Kxh3-bait) that exposes the king to a decisive checking attack ending in mate or heavy material loss; medium blurs to any move that ignores the king's exposure and walks into a winning check or knight fork (Nf7+, Ne5+, Rb1+, Ra3#) netting material.

1102.label: Top: a forced defensive rook exchange on an open file (overwhelmingly the c-file: Rxc1/Rxc8/Rxd1/Rxa8) is available but the player makes a passive king/pawn/knight move and drops the exchange or a full rook in the 2-3 move refutation; medium blurs to any skipped critical simplification or correct capture/move-order (Bxg5, Bxc5, Rxd2, move-order sequences), including a couple of missed wins rather than pure hangs.

1105.label: Top: in a losing rook endgame, a passive/misplaced rook move (Rc8, h5, a5, Ra1, Rf1) lets the opponent's advanced passed pawn queen when only an active rook sac/checking resource (Rxa2+, Rxh7+, Re7+, stalemate Rd1+) saved; medium broadens to simply mislocating the rook (Rf1) rather than the lone pawn-stopping sacrifice (Rxb2) — though a few boards instead miss a winning simplification/blockade.

1118.label: Top boards uniformly hang/trap an own bishop by playing a natural developing or pin move instead of resolving the diagonal tension (Bxd7+/Bxe2/Bxd2+), letting it be won; medium blurs to any hanging minor piece (knights on e4/e5/c3, bishops on g4/h4) and occasionally a missed free capture.

1115.label: Top boards leave an undefended bishop en prise for an immediate clean one-move capture (or fail to grab the opponent's free bishop); medium blurs this to other minor pieces (knights), forks/deflections, and pieces lost over 2-3 moves of refutation, mixing in a few missed-win cases.

1116.label: At the peak it's uniformly a quiet/developing move that opens or fails to block a diagonal so an enemy bishop snaps off an unmoved rook (Bxf8/Bxf1), hanging the exchange; at medium it blurs to material hung more broadly via line-opening or ignored threats — a full piece, exchange-plus-pawn, a queening passed pawn, or en passant — plus a couple of king-safety/false-positive cases.

1114.label: Top: a slow flank/pawn move neglects king safety and permits a kingside attack or sacrifice (Greek-Gift Bxh2+, Nd4/Qh5, opened h/g-file, failing to play h3 vs a Bg4 pin); medium: same quiet/tempo-losing neglect but the refutation broadens to general tactics — forks, blocked own pieces, or a squandered winning edge.

1119.chip: Missed forced mate (broadens to winning attack)
1119.label: Top boards abandon a forced checkmate—frequently the dark-square Qg7#/Bh6 net—by playing a distracting capture or repositioning move; medium boards keep the squandered-kingside-attack core but broaden from strictly forced mate to any winning attack, dissipated via patzer checks, premature trades, or slow prophylactic moves.

1113.label: Top: a quiet/wrong-order move fails the required preparatory capture or keeps tension intact (recurring Bg3 'capture-first' move-order blunders + defender-removing pawn pushes that hang a piece); medium: same 'non-forcing move in a tactical position' idea but blurs into any motif — allowing or missing forks, pins, and winning shots.

1123.label: Top boards are routine developing/castling moves that skip the Bxf7+ sacrifice (or Ne5) punishing an uncastled king on the weak f7 square; medium boards broaden to missing other forcing destructive sacrifices and tactical strikes — Greek Gift Bxh7+, Bxg2+/Bxf2+ deflections, Fried Liver Nxf7, and combinations winning the queen — on a wider range of squares.

1127.label: Top: in a clearly winning position the player skips a forcing rook check (skewer or back-rank) that wins a major piece, instead grabbing a pawn or making a quiet king/pawn move; medium broadens to forcing checks winning a minor piece (knight) or wrong-direction/pointless checks, plus a couple of near-zero-loss cases that dilute the pattern.

1098.label: Top: sharp king-safety blunders where a king move or a defender-removing capture walks straight into an immediate winning/perpetual check, skewer, or piece-loss; Medium: broadens to slower tempo-losing or positional moves that abandon a key defensive square/piece, with the king attack or material loss arriving a move or two later.

1120.label: Top: a minor piece (often the f3 knight) abandons its defense of a central pawn/piece, hanging it to immediate capture; medium broadens to undermining pawn pushes and greedy captures that leave own material en prise.

1112.label: Top: a move exposes the queen to an immediate capture-with-check (Bxf7+, Rxf6+, Bxd2+), losing it for little; medium broadens to other heavy pieces (rook/bishop) and to forcing refutations that aren't always checks — undefended-piece grabs, back-rank mates, and promotion threats.

1129.chip: Hangs bishop to pawn trap (any piece)
1129.label: Top: an active/developed bishop is left where a single pawn advance (a5 on Bb6, g4 on Bf5/h5, b5 on Bc4) traps and wins it; medium broadens the trapped/lost piece to any minor or even rook (Ng7, Nb2, Nf6, Rf4, Bg7) and to non-pawn refutations, with some near-misses that are queen-recapture/positional drops.

1124.label: Top boards are imprecise queen moves in winning positions that skip the unique mating setup (Qh6); medium blurs to any tempo-wasting move—passive retreat, move-order slip—that squanders a won advantage, occasionally even hanging material in the refutation.

1121.label: Top: missed an immediate forced mate—usually a back-rank/exposed-king mate-in-1-to-3—by grabbing a pawn or playing a passive rook move; medium keeps the 'skip the kill for material' behavior but broadens the missed win to any decisive tactic (skewer, fork, longer mating net, tempo conversion), with a few near-equal alternatives mixed in.

1101.label: At peak, every board immediately snatches the enemy queen and overlooks a saving zwischenzug/intermezzo (usually a check) that would preserve material; at medium it blurs to greedily capturing any piece (often a rook) while missing an in-between check or, increasingly, a forced mate.

1131.label: Top is laser-focused on ...g7g6 (or g2g3) pushed to chase the enemy queen off h5/h4, which opens lines and hangs the h8 rook to Qxe5+/Nxg6 with the king stuck in the center; medium keeps the same king-weakening pawn-push-hangs-material idea but blurs the specific move (g6 plus b3, a2, c6, f6) and occasionally shades into missed wins.

1096.label: Top boards are almost uniformly an undefended knight on e5 left uncaptured (best move Nxe5) in a winning opening; medium broadens to other missed material-winning captures (Qxd4, Bxd5, Nxd8) and to ignored own hanging pieces on varied squares, with the consequence ranging from just squandering free material to losing one's own piece over 2-3 moves.

1133.label: Top boards are queen CHECKS that land on a square covered by an enemy piece (bishop/knight/rook/pawn/king), letting the queen be captured for free and squandering a forced win; medium broadens to greedy queen capture-checks (e.g. Qxe5/Qxa8+) where the queen grabs a pawn/rook but is then lost in the exchange.

1138.label: Top is near-uniformly a missed bishop strike on the f-pawn (Bxf2+/Bxf7+) punishing the uncastled/exposed king after a quiet developing move; medium broadens to other king-hunting sacrifices and forcing mates (Bxh7+, Bxh2+, Nxg7+, Qxf7#, Nd4#).

1122.label: Top: a queen capture-with-check that trades queens straight into a hopelessly lost (pawn) endgame, throwing away the queen as the only defensive/perpetual resource; medium blurs to other forcing captures/checks that squander the result — grabbing a pawn into a missed forced mate, or even non-queen moves that allow a king fork or hang material.

1134.label: Top: a king move (typically to h4/h5/h1/edge or corner) walks into an immediate forced checkmate from a drawn-or-lost position; medium broadens to king moves that allow slower mates or lose decisive material, with a few non-king tempo/fork blunders in similar losing endgames.

1139.chip: Hangs piece on pawn push (any move)
1139.label: Top: a pawn thrust intended to kick/attack enemy pieces (often two at once) that ignores a tactic and hangs material; medium blurs the constant pawn-push into any tempo-gaining piece, king or queen move that walks into a material-losing refutation, plus a couple of materially-safe missed-win cases.

1140.label: At the peak the player promotes a pawn directly next to the enemy king (premature promotion that hangs the brand-new queen/knight), throwing away a won endgame to capture; at medium strength this blurs into broader king-and-pawn endgame technique slips that let a winning position drift toward a draw — and several boards aren't even blunders, so the feature is genuinely mixed.

1128.chip: Hangs rook to intruding bishop (→any piece)
1128.label: Top: player ignores an enemy piece (usually a bishop wandered to b7/g7/b2/g8) that is hitting their corner rook, playing a quiet developing/castling move and hanging the rook; medium: broadens to any declined free capture (e.g. missed Kxf7), a directly hung knight, or even an allowed fork/king-safety lapse.

1136.label: Top: a tempo-wasting queen check abandons a key defensive post and the king simply sidesteps to safety, so White's attack crashes through and material is lost over the 2-3 move refutation; medium broadens to bishop/knight/rook checks that either directly hang the checking piece or squander a clearly winning/saving non-check, the constant being that the chosen check is itself the losing move.

1152.label: Top boards are uniformly a safe move that skips grabbing an undefended ROOK for free (Qxf3/Bxd5/fxe6 etc.); medium keeps the missed-rook/exchange-win core but broadens to other skipped material-winning tactics (Bxb8, Bxf5, Bh6, fxg4) and an occasional own-piece hang.

1155.label: Top: pure K+P endgames where the king walks the wrong direction (grabbing a side pawn or abandoning a blockade) and loses the pawn race, letting an enemy passer promote; medium blurs into rook endgames, positional bishop/king placements and pawn-structure pushes in losing endgames, plus several near-zero-loss king moves that aren't real blunders.

1135.label: Top: a king move that declines capturing/eliminating a hanging or attacked enemy knight (which then escapes to an outpost or forks); medium: the same missed knight capture but executed by any piece, occasionally hanging own material instead.

1149.label: Top is consistently a bishop-for-piece trade (or king recapture) that simplifies into a lost king-and-pawn endgame; medium blurs to broader endgame capture errors — a missed winning pawn push, an allowed back-rank mate, and a knight fork — alongside the same losing trades.

1158.label: Top boards are all opening developing moves (usually ...Bc5/Bc4, or c3/Nc3) that ignore the f-pawn's central capture and hang the e5/e4 pawn to fxe5/fxe4; medium keeps the 'develop-and-neglect-defense' theme but broadens the hung material and refutation (b7 to Qxb7, g5 to Nxg5, e5 to Nxe5, a trapped Na4, or a Nb5–Nd6+ fork).

1169.label: Top is uniformly the queen walked into a capture and lost for far too little (often a greedy rook/bishop grab that's recaptured); medium broadens to any piece hung — rooks and knights left en prise — plus a couple of queen trades/king moves that surrender material or compensation.

1148.label: Top: a clearly winning position thrown away by a quiet, loosening move (flank pawn push a4/a5, restraining-piece retreat Ng5, or queen sortie Qf3/Qf5) that abandons a key defender/restraint and hands the opponent a freeing ...d5 break or a material-winning tactic; medium blurs the eval (equal/unclear) and the motif, adding straight removed-defender hangs (c5, Bxc5, Be7), greedy pawn grabs (Nxe4), and king-safety moves that walk into mate.

1159.label: Top boards take a near-winning position (+185 to +389) and crash it 170-224cp with a loosening pawn push or loose piece move that hangs material within 2-3 moves of the refutation (knight on g5/f4, bishop on Bd3/b3, pawn on Bh6); medium blurs to a purely positional/tempo inaccuracy (d5) that concedes much of the edge without actually losing material.

1160.label: Top: a rook move (often a self-pin to the same file/rank) that allows a rook exchange transitioning into a trivially lost pawn endgame where the opponent's passed pawn promotes; medium keeps the allowed-rook-trade-into-lost-endgame core but blurs into other conceding moves — queen trades, rook moves that permit mate or hang the exchange — i.e. any simplification/move that concedes a decisive resource.

1156.chip: Allowed passed pawn to queen (or mate)
1156.label: Top: an endgame king/knight/rook move (often a tempting check that misroutes pieces) fails to blockade an enemy passed pawn, letting it queen from a drawn/won position; medium: broadens to allowing any decisive endgame resource — promotion, back-rank/Rh2# mate, a fork, or a dropped piece — all single-ply 'safe' but losing over the 2-3 move refutation.

1167.label: Top: a guard is vacated (defender of a key square/file/piece) so material hangs, often to a rook invading the 7th rank; medium blurs to any material-losing move—greedy pawn-grabs that get trapped, walked-into forks/discovered checks, and king moves ceding key squares.

1166.label: Top boards: a passive/quiet move (frequently a king move) in a tactically charged spot skips a decisive forcing win — a queen check or promotion that wins a piece, or even mate-in-one — and occasionally walks into loss; medium boards: the same passivity blurs into minor tempo-losing endgame inaccuracies in already-decided (won or lost) positions.

1163.label: Top: a rook check throws away a drawn rook endgame—hanging the rook (Rg4+→fxg4) or gifting the decisive tempo (Rh6+/Rg5+/Rh4+); medium keeps the 'endgame-blowing move' core but blurs the check/rook constraint into king walks into mate, lost opposition, and skipped winning captures.

1173.chip: Hangs to ignored tactic (pawn kicks knight)
1173.label: Top: a pawn advance chasing a centralized enemy knight (very often on d5) overlooks a forcing tactical refutation that wins material; medium broadens the same 'kick' idea to other tempo-gaining moves (pawns chasing bishops, piece moves, even recaptures) that likewise ignore the refuting tactic.

1177.label: Top boards are already-losing positions where the player skips the unique defensive resource (Rc8/Rac8/wrong recapture), letting a knight or rook crash into the king for forced mate or material; medium softens to a positional queen move (Qa3) that concedes a key diagonal, allowing a knight infiltration that wins a pawn and starts a slower kingside attack.

1178.label: Top boards are a tempting material grab (usually capturing the queen) that overlooks a forced mate-in-1; medium blurs to longer forced mates (mate-3/4/11) plus a few greedy captures that merely squander a winning edge rather than a mate.

1175.label: Top boards are queen-and-pawn endgames where a precise forcing queen check (Qxh5+, Qxe2+) for mate or to halt the passer was missed and a slow queen/king move let the win slip to a draw; medium broadens to rook/knight/king moves that likewise fail to stop the opponent's passed pawn, squandering a won endgame — though many activations are actually 0cp non-blunders in the same queen-vs-passer setting.

1176.chip: Wrong move order loses material (queen trade)
1176.label: Top: opening positions where the player captures or develops instead of trading queens (or inserting a check) first, hanging material or wrecking structure in the refutation; medium broadens to general move-order/defender-removal slips (e.g., a pawn push dropping a knight to a fork) that cost material or a winning position.

1179.label: Top: already lost, the player ignores an attacked rook/queen and the single saving capture/exchange (e.g. Rxe3, Qxf4), hanging a major piece and often walking into forced mate; medium broadens the unit and resource — any piece (knight, pawn) or any lone saving move (recapture, luft/a3, centralizing retreat, en passant) is overlooked in a losing position, again losing material or allowing mate.

1165.label: Top: a bishop capture/recapture that scores as an even trade but backfires—typically opening lines (often the f-file) against an exposed/uncastled king or exposing/losing another piece; medium broadens to any natural capture (pawn/knight/rook) that ignores a stronger move or walks into a recapture, pin, or zwischenzug, losing material or throwing away the win.

1185.label: At the peak a move removes/deflects (or vacates) the sole defender of a minor piece—usually a bishop—so it drops outright; at medium it blurs into a positional move (Qb7) that ignores a piece's vulnerability and concedes a forced trade into a losing endgame rather than losing material immediately.

1182.label: Top boards almost uniformly miss the dark-squared-bishop sac/check ...Bxh2+ (also Qxh2+ / White's Bxh7+) — a Greek-Gift-style h2/h7 shot against the exposed king; medium blurs this to other missed king-attack tactics: a clearance-sac Bxh2+, but also back-rank Qe1+, diagonal/exchange-winning checks (Bxf3, Be3+), and a purely positional structure error.

1183.label: Top boards decline a simplifying trade/capture into a clearly won pawn or minor-piece endgame (or play a pointless tempo-losing check instead); medium positions broaden to missing any forcing win — clean captures, knight forks, pawn pushes, mates — and include several near-0cp non-blunders plus one hung queen, making the signal genuinely mixed.

1193.label: Top: a slow king/repositioning move instead of advancing the passed pawn to the 7th/promotion (or removing the promotion-square defender); medium keeps the 'skipped the decisive winning move in a winning position' core but broadens beyond promotion to other passed-pawn advances, back-rank/mating tactics, and mate-preserving moves.

1198.label: Top: hangs the queen by ignoring a one-move threat—typically an irrelevant pawn capture leaving Qg4 en prise to ...Bxg4 (or capturing onto a defended square); medium keeps the threat-blindness theme but broadens to other decisive losses, allowing a back-rank mate or liquidating advanced passed pawns.

1200.label: Top: a queen/bishop is lunged to the h-file for a speculative kingside attack that abandons defensive duties (d-pawn, b7, back rank) and hangs material; medium broadens to any active/material-grabbing move that neglects a key defensive responsibility or piece coordination (blockade, pin, f-file, back rank) and drops material or the game.

1188.chip: Hangs to knight tactic (broadens to any)
1188.label: Top: a natural developing/plan move (often a pawn push or piece development) ignores a forcing tactic and an enemy KNIGHT wins material — fork (Nxc2+, Nxd4, Nb6), capture of a now-undefended piece (Nxf4, Nxg6, Nxe6), or sacrifice/combo (Nd6+, Bxf6/Nxf6+); medium keeps the 'natural move ignores a tactic, loses material' core but the punishing motif blurs to bishop captures (Bxa6, Bh6), central pawn breaks (e5-e6, d5), and discovered attacks (Bh7+), with a couple of missed-wins (Ne5, Qxf5) instead of pure hangs.

1195.label: Top: premature opening attacks—wayward queen sorties (Qh5/Qf3/Qxf7) and f7 sacs that hang the queen or the c4 bishop in a Scholar's-Mate setup; medium broadens to any over-optimistic, natural-looking move that simply drops material (rook, pawn) beyond the opening.

1168.label: Top: a tempting forcing capture (usually with check) trades off the player's own key attacking piece, so a simple recapture/interposition consolidates the opponent and dissolves a winning attack (sometimes a forced mate); medium broadens to any imprecise move — quiet developing moves, pawn pushes, king moves, knight repositionings — that lets a recapture or zwischenzug collapse a clearly winning advantage.

1190.label: TOP: a piece (usually a rook) abandons defense of an open file/back-rank or exposed king and is punished by a decisive rook invasion or back-rank mate, where the correct move was almost always the simplifying rook trade (e.g. Rxe8); MEDIUM keeps the 'neglected defense → lost material' core but blurs the punishment to knight forks, king-side attacks, hung pawns and tempo/endgame slips rather than the clean back-rank/file invasion.

1199.label: Top: opening positions where the player ignores a free minor-piece capture/recapture (very often a bishop, on c6/c3 or simply hanging) and drops a full piece; medium blurs into broader material/tempo errors—moving the wrong piece into a hang, tempo-losing developing moves, and positional miscaptures—plus a couple of near-best moves that aren't real blunders.

1201.label: TOP: in a won endgame, skips a forcing queen-check sequence that mates or wins a rook, playing a quiet queen move/pawn push instead; MEDIUM keeps the won-endgame 'declined the forcing win' theme but broadens to rook/pawn checks and mate-in-one, with some non-checks, non-blunders, and even self-inflicted tactics.

1192.chip: Hangs rook in lost endgame (or tempo)
1192.label: Top: in already-losing rook endgames, a rook (or rook-deserting king) move that either hangs the rook outright (Rxf4/Rxc5/Bxe5/Kxe3) or squanders the one tempo needed to stop a passed pawn; medium broadens the mechanism to pieces walking into forks/deflections and king-safety mates, and spills out of the pure endgame into the middlegame.

1197.label: Top: a passive queen move/retreat (or queen trade) forgoes a forcing check — usually a draw-saving perpetual or a winning checking sequence; medium blurs to rook/knight/pawn moves that skip the active resource, which is no longer always a check.

1203.label: Top boards lose a winning/equal eval to a precise forcing refutation — queen-fork or pawn-storm/king-attack punishing an exposed piece or king (Ba6→Qa4+, O-O-O→c5, Qe2→Nd4); medium blurs into general passive/misplaced-piece moves that forfeit material or a concrete tactical win (Ng6 instead of Ng4).

1205.label: Top boards lose a key tempo in a passed-pawn/promotion race by skipping a forcing tempo-move—usually a check (Bc5+, g5+, Rxe3+, Qa4+) or the only blockade—so the enemy pawn queens; medium broadens to any slow king-walk or non-forcing move that wastes the tempo needed to win or hold the same promotion race.

1212.label: At the peak the move walks the king into an immediate forced mate (Kg2→Rxh2#) by abandoning key escape-square control; at medium it broadens to misplacing a piece (wrong piece to f6, queen invasion, non-capture) that surrenders a tactical/defensive resource and drops material rather than mating.

1206.label: Top: king walks the wrong direction in a king-and-pawn race, losing the passed-pawn promotion contest by a tempo; medium retains some slow-king-vs-passer cases but blurs into other endgame material losses (hung/trapped pieces, wasted tempi, even a mating attack).

1204.label: Top: a quiet developing/repositioning move leaves a minor piece (usually a knight) hanging while skipping the resolving capture; medium broadens to hanging the queen or simply squandering a winning edge by ignoring the position's tactical priority.

1202.label: Top: Black greedily grabs a central pawn (usually d4) in the opening and loses the recapturing piece, where Bb4+ was right; medium blurs the object to the queen (...Bxd1) that walks into a Bxf7+/Nd5# mate and adds king-walks-into-mate plus a few materially-safe missed tactics.

1221.label: Top boards all play a natural developing/castling move and miss the decisive 6.Qd5-type queen centralization that double-attacks f7 and a hanging knight; medium keeps the same 'winning opening, played a quiet move, skipped the forcing win' theme but broadens the tactic to Nb5 knight forks, free captures (Qxg5), and even missed mates.

1225.label: Top boards uniformly hang the QUEEN from a won position—usually a developing/idle move that ignores an enemy bishop attacking it, punished by Bxd8 (sometimes Nxh5/knight-fork over 2 moves); at medium it blurs to hanging or losing any material (bishop to a rook battery, queen to Bxc5, trapped queens) and even non-hang blunders (missed captures, endgame tempo loss, king-safety pushes).

1217.label: Top is uniformly a bishop developed to pin a knight (Bg5/Bb5/Bb4/Bg4) that hangs the bishop/loses material to a counter-tactic (diagonal check like Qa4+/Bxf7+, or Nxe4/Bxf2+ hitting the undefended bishop); medium broadens to any move that hangs a piece (still often a bishop), with a couple of squandered-win/tempo cases blurring the edges.

1220.label: Top: a king move in an already-won (or drawn) endgame loses tempo and abandons its key duty — supporting one's own passer, halting the enemy passer, or guarding a critical square (or chasing a pawn) — throwing away the result; medium blurs the piece, with rook, pawn, and even knight moves likewise squandering the winning/drawing endgame.

1226.label: Top boards miss an obvious capture of an undefended enemy ROOK while already winning; medium boards keep the 'ignored a free enemy piece' theme but broaden the target to any hanging piece (knight, queen).

1211.label: Top: in a winning endgame, throws away a forced mate via a non-forcing, materially-safe move (often a wrong pawn push or under-promotion); medium broadens to milder tempo/precision lapses that merely let the advantage slip — and even to the defending side weakening its own king.

1223.label: Top: a greedy opening queen pawn-grab (usually Qxb7) that leaves the queen stranded/trapped and often ignores a free piece or mate; medium broadens to other over-extended queen sorties (Qh5, Qb6, Qxc3, Qa6) and some non-queen loose moves that get punished by tempo gains, traps, or forks.

1239.label: Top boards: a materially-safe (usually queen-grabbing) move skips an immediate forced mate, classically mate-in-one capture-blindness; medium boards keep the 'missed win' core but blur from clean forced mate to passing up the single precise move that sustains a winning mating attack.

1234.label: Top: a natural quiet rook/piece move hangs material by overlooking the opponent's tactical counterblow (fork, double attack, or discovered attack); medium blurs in direction to the same quiet-rook move skipping its OWN winning double-attack (missed win).

1237.label: Top boards are a bishop sortie to b4/b5 (often a hanging check) snapped off immediately by an a-/b-pawn (axb4/axb5); medium broadens to bishops parked on a4/a5/e6 that get trapped or forked by a pawn advance (b4, d5, c4) rather than captured on the spot.

1241.label: Top: a pawn advance in the endgame that surrenders a key square, tempo, the opposition, or a defensive capture-with-check and throws away a winning/drawn position ('king first, pawns second'); medium broadens to structurally-weakening pawn pushes (isolated pawns, lost outposts, released tension) across any phase, plus a couple of analogous advantage-squandering piece moves.

1219.label: Top: from a winning opening, plays a quiet pawn move that ignores a free hanging piece (usually a bishop) and often walks into a king-side check; medium broadens to overlooking any winning capture (knight/rook/pawn) or a self-weakening quiet move that throws away the won position.

1235.label: Top: a fork-/tempo-grabbing check (most often a KNIGHT check like Nxc2+/Ne3+) that the king calmly sidesteps (Kd1, Kf2, Kb1...), abandoning a vital defender and hanging the checking piece while a real threat (e.g. Qg7#) goes unanswered; medium blurs to any piece's purposeless check (rook/queen/bishop) — and even quiet moves — that the king/opponent neutralizes by stepping aside, sometimes skipping a forced win rather than hanging material.

1240.label: Top boards almost uniformly miss a back-rank-exploiting queen check delivering forced mate or winning material; medium keeps the 'played a quiet move, skipped the forcing win' theme but blurs the motif to other missed shots—non-back-rank mates, promotions, sacrifices, and hanging-piece grabs (plus a few outright hangs).

1247.label: Top: a rook left undefended is snapped off by the enemy QUEEN (often with check along an open diagonal); medium: still a hung rook but the capturer broadens to bishop/king as well as queen (with a couple of outliers — a greedy pawn-grab and a missed forcing tactic).
