1210.label: Top: a quiet bishop/knight retreat or development around a knight either orphans one's own knight or skips capturing an exposed enemy knight (e.g., Nxh4), costing a piece; medium: the same non-forcing 'develop/retreat/castle instead of the required capture' move broadens to any piece and varied motifs (forks, pins, king-safety, passed-pawn breakthroughs).

1242.chip: Hangs piece ignoring sole defense (often decisive)
1242.label: Top: an off-task move (luft, centralizing, or a grab) ignores the only saving move and walks into forced mate or drops the queen/a full piece; Medium: the same neglect of the critical threat leaks smaller material (exchange/pawn) or a weakening pawn push that just forfeits a winning edge.

1243.label: Top boards drop a minor piece to a centralizing knight fork (Nd5/Nd2/Ne5), typically after neglecting the freeing ...Bxc3; medium boards broaden to knight forks hitting the queen+rook/bishop (Nd4/Ne3) and blur into general opening tempo-loss, missed key captures, and plain hanging pieces.

1250.chip: Hangs piece by deserting defender (often fork)
1250.label: Top: a quiet piece/pawn move abandons the sole defender of a key pawn or square, usually punished by a decisive knight fork; medium broadens to any move leaving a pawn/piece hanging for a plain capture (incl. wrong recapture and queen wandering).

1233.label: At the peak the player squanders a forced win or invites a king-attack/mate by choosing an inferior active move (check, capture, or retreat) in a sharp middlegame, while at medium activation it blurs into more ordinary blunders that simply leave a minor piece or rook hanging to a basic capture.

1244.label: Top: a tempting knight (or queen) check/grab the opponent simply recaptures, hanging material from a winning/drawn position (with a few that instead skip a forced mate/perpetual); medium broadens to bishop/queen/pawn checks that are inferior forcing moves, sometimes only squandering the win positionally or by tempo rather than hanging outright.

1259.label: At the peak, the feature fires on slow flank-pawn advances (a5/b4/b5/g5/a6) that neglect development and get hit by a central break or knight tactic; at medium it's the same wing-pawn tempo-loss (a6), with f-pawn pushes (f3/f6) and a misplaced bishop development (Bd6) blurring the edge between pure positional loss and outright dropped material.

1180.label: Top boards are routine opening developing/castling moves that hang one's own loose bishop on an exposed square (h3/a6/g4/b7/h6); medium boards blur the direction toward missed bishop captures, move-order/tension errors, and bishops trapped by pawns.

1262.label: Top boards almost always shove a piece (usually a knight) straight onto a square where it's captured cleanly for a pawn or nothing, or ignore a direct hit on it; medium blurs to hanging higher material (queen/rook), often via a short 2-move tactic, and mixes in a few missed-win/tempo cases.

1255.label: Top boards uniformly lose the OWN QUEEN to a forcing combination (Bxh2+/Rxd1 deflection off an undefended d1-queen, or a greedy Qxe4/Qxc3 grab trapped by an open-file pin/skewer/clearance), while medium positions broaden to hanging ANY piece—bishop, rook, or knight—via pins, skewers, forks, or removal-of-the-guard, with a couple of softer positional drops.

1263.label: Top: greedily grabs a side pawn, abandoning the defender of its own critical passed pawn, which the opponent immediately recaptures (squandering a win); medium broadens to leaving any pawn or even a full piece undefended after moving its protector.

1257.label: Top boards consistently miss a winning pawn fork (classically b4 double-attacking queen + minor, or c6/c5 breaks); medium broadens to any squandered winning resource—missed non-fork tactics plus positional concessions and king-safety hangs.

1252.label: Top: a tempting queen check or greedy capture squanders a forced mate or queen-winning fork (the correct shot is usually a knight fork/discovered check/mate sequence); medium: the same wrong-forcing-move habit blurs to throwing away smaller material—extra pawns or an avoided queen trade—rather than a forced mate.

1264.label: Top boards are structurally damaging pawn advances (e3e4, f7f6) that wreck the center and hang a central pawn; medium blurs to any slow, non-forcing move—rim-knight reroutes (Na4, Nf6→h7), passive development/retreats (Bd3, Be7), and prophylaxis (a6, h6)—that surrenders tempo, central control, or a single critical tactical shot.

1245.label: Top: in a clearly winning position a natural/quiet move (castle, retreat, pawn push, routine recapture) squanders the lone decisive forcing shot (queen centralization, skewer, double/discovered attack); medium broadens to missed simple knight forks and exchange-winning captures, with the direction blurring — about half the boards instead hang material or allow the opponent's fork rather than purely skipping a win.

1251.label: Top: rook (occasionally queen) captures a pawn WITH CHECK in a won endgame and is recaptured by the king, throwing away a forced mate/huge edge; medium broadens to queen-for-pawn/knight trades and indirect refutations (forks, wrong capture order, tempo-losing checks) with much smaller swings or even non-blunders.

1267.chip: Hangs knight on vain check (med: missed mate)
1267.label: Top boards are flashy non-capturing knight checks that simply hang the knight outright; medium boards broaden to knight checks that let the king escape, squandering a forced mate or perpetual draw rather than losing material.

1271.label: Top boards are rook moves that abandon the back-rank/king defender (e.g. Re3, Re7) walking into back-rank mate or deflection; medium broadens to any piece (pawn push, king step, bishop move) vacating a square that shielded the king, punished by a decisive check or breakthrough (Bb4+, Rd2+, Qxg6+, h5#), with a few drifting into missed-win/positional collapses.

1272.label: Top: in a winning position, played a safe quiet move instead of capturing a completely undefended enemy bishop (Rxd4/Kxf3/Kxe5 etc.); medium keeps the missed-capture theme (still mostly bishops) but blurs into defensive lapses that hang own material or walk into forced mate.

1275.chip: Wasted tempo, passive king move (any piece)
1275.label: Top: a tempo-wasting king move in a passed-pawn endgame where the decisive pawn-push (or rook-behind-passer) was required instead; medium broadens to any passive/slow move — king, pawn or bishop — that squanders the one critical tempo, with some now walking into outright tactics (forks, mate).

1281.label: At the peak it's razor-sharp king-and-pawn opposition/blockade failures — the king steps off the ONLY drawing square (e.g. Ke1 instead of Kf2, Kf8 instead of Ke7), surrendering the blockade in front of the passer and turning a dead draw into a forced loss as the pawn queens; at medium it blurs into general passed-pawn mishandling — failing to get the rook behind the pawn, advancing/abandoning a pawn that frees the enemy passer, or king/piece races (sometimes only an inaccuracy, even one near-0cp non-blunder), no longer confined to pure opposition or to lost-draw positions.

1268.label: Top: a losing king steps to the rim — overwhelmingly the h-file (Kh4/Kh5/Kh7) — walking into a rook/knight mating net or dropping a pawn with tempo; medium broadens to any losing king drift, especially wrong-direction marches that lose the pawn race (Kg2/Kb8/Kf4/Kd1), plus a few passive non-king moves.

1285.label: Top: an endgame king- or knight-move that arrives too slow or goes the wrong way to halt an enemy passed pawn, which then promotes and wins; medium keeps the same passer-failure but blurs the failing piece to rooks and dilutes with other positional/king-safety/deflection material losses.

1294.label: Top: in a clearly winning position the player skips a bishop move (almost always Bb5, also Bb4/Ba4) that pins or attacks the enemy queen to the king and wins it; medium blurs to any missed winning resource or allowed enemy tactic — missed captures, missed forced mate, allowed knight forks, trapped/hung pieces — i.e. failing to find the one precise move in a sharp position.

1277.label: Top: a tempting ROOK check (open/d-file or castling-check) thrown in instead of the precise winning queen move or forced mate; medium broadens to checks with the wrong piece (bishop/queen) or wrong square, plus some non-check stragglers, all skipping the stronger tactic.

1292.label: Top boards are almost uniformly a rook (sometimes queen) check that just gets captured—sacrificing the piece for a meaningless, follow-up-less check; medium positions keep the 'hang your own major piece' core but blur the trigger, adding queen-led blunders and greedy non-check captures of defended squares that also leave the piece en prise.

1290.label: At the peak the player skips a forcing check/zwischenzug that mates or wins the queen, choosing a quiet non-forcing move instead; at medium activation this broadens to checks that win only lesser material or merely save the position, plus a few non-check positional best moves.

1287.label: At the peak, a clean forced mate-in-1/2 is thrown away by playing a tempting check (or wrong-piece/wrong-move-order capture) that lets the king slip out of the mating net; at medium it blurs to squandering forced wins or saving draws via the same 'checking-reflex' forcing moves, occasionally slow pawn pushes or moves that even hang material.

1282.label: Top: from a winning position the player makes a capture (usually with check) that trades into near-equality, forfeiting a much stronger preparatory/intermediate continuation; medium broadens to non-checking captures, pawn pushes, and even quiet positional/tempo moves that similarly squander a winning or clearly better position.

1274.label: Top: a won position collapses when a careless king/queen move walks into a forcing check or fork that wins the QUEEN (or throws away a forced mate); medium: same forcing-check motif but surrenders only lesser material (exchange, rook, pawn) or just bleeds a winning edge via tempo/positional self-harm.

1279.label: Top: a won pawn endgame thrown away by a passive king move or pawn push that skips the decisive king-march/capture; medium broadens to pointless checks, a trapped-queen sortie, and drawn middlegame king moves that walk into a tempo check, blurring from won-endgame king play to any idle non-converting move.

1299.label: Top: a quiet non-capturing king/pawn move leaves doubled rooks on the open c/e-file to win the exchange via a forced Rxc8/Rxe8 sequence; medium keeps the 'slow move skips the needed rook trade' core but blurs the punishment to other ignored tactics (hanging queen Qxc5+, back-rank Rd1+, bishop deflection Rxc1+).

1298.label: At the peak the player squanders a won endgame by ADVANCING A PASSED PAWN (e4, h5, a5, a7) instead of the precise concrete capture/exchange-sacrifice that converts (Rxd6, Bxa7, Rxc7, Rxg6); at medium it blurs to any quiet repositioning/check move (Qg7, Qe8) that skips an available winning capture (Qxe4, Qxh3) — with a substantial fraction of 0cp non-mistakes (best-move or only-move boards) mixed in, hence the low consistency.

1296.label: Top: a developing bishop move in a level opening hands the enemy QUEEN free material—either capturing the bishop itself on c5 (Qxc5) or grabbing the b7/g7 pawn it left undefended (Qxb7/Qxg7); medium blurs the picture, broadening to other developing moves (knight to c6, Bg4 inviting Qb3) and to non-queen captures (dxc6) or even missed wins, so the constant 'piece hangs to a queen raid' degrades into 'a developing move drops material to some capture'.

1295.label: Top boards uniformly hang the queen to a routine knight capture in an equal opening (a quiet move ignoring the knight's attack); medium blurs to hanging lesser material—pawns and bishops—and bleeds into knight forks and king-safety mates.

1291.label: Medium is tight — a slow luft pawn move (a3, g3) refuted by an infiltrating queen check (Qe1+/Qc1+) that wins material; the peak keeps the 'quiet move ignores a forcing reply' idea but blurs into varied decisive blunders (discovered double-attack, hung rook, king walking into g5+/Rxg2+ mate) and a few missed wins.

1305.label: Top positions are almost uniformly a missed knight fork to c2/c7 (Nc2+/Nxc7+) that hits the king-on-e1 and the a1-rook to win the exchange or more; medium broadens to any tactic punishing the same exposed/uncastled king — queen forks (Qxc3+), knight checks winning the queen (Nxe7+/Nd6+), with a couple of cases tipping into outright hangs (Re8+, Qf3).

1301.label: Top boards remove the back-rank/king's defender (or march the king in) allowing a forced mate—usually a back-rank mate; medium broadens to general king-safety failures (castling into attacks, king marches, vacated guards) plus a few plain hung pieces and missed wins.

1308.label: Top boards are a well-placed minor piece (usually a knight) grabbing a pawn and getting simply recaptured—an unsound 'attacking' sac that just loses material; medium broadens to other pieces, exchange sacrifices, and wrong-target/move-order captures that drop material to a straightforward refutation.

1319.label: Top boards near-uniformly skip Bxg7 winning the exchange on the open long diagonal while in a winning opening; medium broadens to other long-diagonal captures (Bxa8/Bxb7/Bxc3/Qxg2) and occasional off-diagonal material wins (Qxd4) or related tactics.

1309.label: Top: in a won position the player promotes a pawn to queen one move too early and the fresh queen is immediately captured (almost always by a rook on the open file/square), where an intermezzo check or prep move was needed; medium keeps the 'self-inflicted material loss that throws away a winning advantage' core but blurs the mechanism — hanging other pieces (queen/rook to a rook capture) or dissipating the win via loose trades/positional moves rather than strictly promotion.

1310.label: Top boards are uniformly quiet/passive moves (h3, Qe2, a3, Bg5, Qd5) that let Black castle out of central danger when only the prophylactic Ba3 kept the king trapped, squandering a winning edge; medium blurs to any failure to exploit the exposed/uncastled enemy king—allowing the escaping ...d5 break, missing free captures (Qxd6, Qxg5) or forks (Nxc2), and move-order slips.

1313.label: Top positions are clean, catastrophic throws of a clearly winning game—hanging a major/minor piece (often by moving its sole defender) or missing a mate-in-one—while medium positions broaden to smaller-swing advantage losses spanning missed non-mating tactics, greedy captures, and passive tempo/positional moves.

1314.label: Top: the queen (or other key defender) leaves its post guarding a king-shielding pawn/square (often f3) and gets refuted by infiltration like Qxf3/mate; medium blurs to any passive or misplacing move that surrenders a critical square or defensive resource, letting the opponent break through against the king or win material.

1316.label: Top boards squander a forced mate by playing a quiet king/piece move instead of the obvious free capture (hxg5, Kxf7, Nxd2, fxg5); medium boards blur to missing winning pawn pushes/conversions in won endgames (g5+, fxg5) — all materially-safe moves that throw away an already-won position rather than losing own material, though a few weaker top boards instead drift/lose material from non-winning positions.

1317.label: Top boards constantly decline a free undefended enemy piece in the opening (usually a stray bishop on a6/h6/h3) by playing a routine developing move—fianchetto, castle, or knight develop—often hanging their own piece in the process; medium blurs into broader opening missteps where the same auto-pilot developing move overlooks a winning tactic, loses tempo, or even allows mate.

1320.chip: Hangs king to queen check (often mate)
1320.label: Top: a weakening opening pawn move opens the king's diagonal and is mated by Qh4#/Qh5+/Qxf7#; medium broadens to queen checks (Qa5+/Qa4+/Qh4+) that fork or win a piece rather than deliver immediate mate.

1326.label: Top: a quiet developing/repositioning move ignores a completely undefended enemy QUEEN one move from capture (Qxe5, Nxd4, Qxd8, Rxb3); medium blurs to missing other hanging material — free minor pieces (Bxb7, Bxg7) and queen trades that net a pawn.

1312.label: Top: a rook captures a pawn with check (usually on the 7th rank) and is simply recaptured, surrendering a full rook for a pawn (or both rooks for the queen); medium broadens to other forcing captures/checks and premature trades — including queen sacs and equalizing exchanges — that liquidate a winning or equal position into a draw or loss.

1321.label: Top: a quiet developing/repositioning move skips the winning central knight capture 'Nxd5!' that wins material via a fork after the forced recapture; medium keeps the missed-tactic core but blurs to other knight captures (Nxd4/Nxe4/Nxg6) and noisier king-safety/endgame misses.

1322.label: Top: in a won endgame, skips immediate pawn promotion (typically c1=Q+ with check) and lets the opponent blockade the queening square, throwing away a forced mate/win; medium broadens to advancing a passed pawn prematurely instead of activating the king/rook, again inviting a blockade or liquidation.

1338.label: Top: a bishop greedily captures a defended central pawn (almost always d4) and is simply recaptured, losing the bishop for a single pawn; medium broadens to knights (Nxd4/Nxe4/Nxb4) and other targets (e5, a6) plus a few looser cases of grabbing a defended/protected pawn.

1300.label: Top: clearly-winning positions (mostly pawn endgames) thrown away by a committal/loosening pawn advance the opponent refutes with a pawn break; medium blurs to middlegame piece moves and smaller/equal edges squandered via hanging material, forks, or pins.

1335.label: Top: a king move steps into a forced checkmate (Qe2#, Qxf7#, Rh1#, mating king-marches) from drawn/losing positions; medium broadens to king (or occasional piece) moves onto exposed squares that lose material to checks/forks, with a few cases blurring into pure positional king-exposure and missed-win/tempo errors.

1327.label: Top boards are self-destructive moves—greedy captures or king walks (Qxc7, Kd7, Bd3, Rbxb2, Rd7)—that fatally expose the player's own king and walk into an immediate FORCED CHECKMATE (back-rank/king-safety nets); medium blurs this so the punishment is frequently just MATERIAL LOSS (hanging queen Qxg4/Ra8, trapped queen Be2, lost knight Nxf3+) rather than mate, though king-safety mates (Nxh7, Qf2, Qxf7) still recur.

1333.label: Top: winning (often rook) endgames where the played move is technically suboptimal — frequently missing the cleanest forcing conversion such as a simplifying rook trade into a won K+P endgame, an exchange sac for a passer, or a skewer (several are near-0cp non-blunders); medium blurs into broader endgame-technique errors — greedy pawn grabs that throw the win to a draw, wrong-piece recaptures, premature checks, and missed forcing rook wins — that squander more of the advantage.

1329.label: Top boards uniformly ignore an immediate forced queen mate-in-one (Qxh7#/Qxf2#-type, usually while greedily capturing); medium broadens to queen checks that win material or force mate in 2–3, with a few plain hanging-piece blunders.

1346.label: At the peak the player has a clean immediate forced mate (frequently mate-in-one like Rf8#/Qf8#/Nb3#) but plays a quiet or greedy non-forcing move instead; at medium it blurs to missing longer multi-move forced mates and decisive winning attacks rather than a single mating blow.

1337.label: Top boards are all opening knight moves that hang a minor piece (the knight itself, or a bishop it was defending); medium broadens to any opening move—pawn, queen, bishop or knight—that drops material or walks into a tactical refutation.

1339.label: Top: a winning opening position is thrown away by hanging a minor piece—mostly a greedy central pawn-grab (Nxe5/Nxe4 leaving a piece undefended) or a loose ...Bb4 pin that drops the e5 point; medium keeps the 'squander a winning/equalish opening' theme but blurs the cause—Bb4/e6 hangs refuted by Qa4+ alongside non-hanging tempo losses (Qe7, Qb6+, Nb4), premature pawn pushes (f5, g5, c4) and king-safety errors (Kg7).

1343.label: At the peak the mistake is consistently neglecting the single prophylactic a4 (a developing/repositioning move like Bd3, Nc5, Rd1 lets the opponent's thematic ...a4 queenside lever in); at medium it stays the same a4-pawn-lever prophylaxis theme (Nc5/a4), with the top set occasionally blurring to other flank/center pawn breaks (e5 allowing h5, c5 allowing Ne4).

1349.label: Top boards uniformly miss a mate-in-one (usually a Qh#-corner mate) because the player reflexively fires a pointless check that lets the king escape to safety; medium blurs the win from strict mate-in-1 to longer forced mates and forcing material-winning lines, but keeps the same root error—a wrong/escaping check (or move-order slip) that hands the trapped king a flight square.

1340.label: At the peak, in dead-drawn knight endgames the player plays a knight check or king step instead of simply grabbing a hanging queen (Nxh5/Nxb6) — a clean missed material win; at medium it blurs into other materially-safe but suboptimal knight/defensive moves (tempo-losing knight checks, fortress lapses) where the squandered resource is no longer specifically the queen.

1348.chip: Allowed enemy pawn to promote (king→any piece)
1348.label: Top: in a lost endgame the KING walks the wrong way (or off its blockade/critical square), letting an enemy passed pawn queen — often turning lost-but-fighting into forced mate; medium keeps the lost-endgame failed-defense theme but broadens the offender to any piece (rook off a1, knight off d6, even a pawn) abandoning a blockade/recapture, and blurs into pure king-safety mating-net collapses not driven by a passer.

1323.label: Top: an h-pawn capture of a minor piece on g5/g4 (hxg5/hxg4) that, after the hxg recapture, blasts open the h-file straight at the player's OWN castled king, trading material but conceding a winning attack; medium blurs into assorted greedy/premature pawn-and-piece captures (dxc4, Bxg5, gxf5, cxd6, Bxe6) and loose pawn moves punished by line-opening, passed pawns, or attacks not always against one's own king.

1358.chip: Hangs queen grabbing defended piece (any piece)
1358.label: Top boards are uniformly a queen capturing a (usually pawn-defended) piece and being immediately recaptured, losing the queen for a minor piece; medium broadens to any piece greedily grabbing material and getting refuted by a recapture or opened line (losing the exchange, a rook, or the advantage).

1365.label: Top boards all skip a decisive rook check/infiltration exploiting an exposed or back-rank king (Rd8+, Re8+, Rd7+, Rd1#, Rf1+) in a winning position; medium positions keep the 'missed forcing strike on the loose king' theme but broaden the piece to queen checks/infiltration (Qc8, Qc8+, Qd8+, Qg5) and other major-piece blows.

1367.label: Top: pure king-and-pawn endgames thrown from won to drawn by pushing the passer (or wrong king step) instead of leading with the king to take the opposition; medium broadens to general winning-endgame conversion/tempo slips (many barely-cp or not even blunders, plus a few off-theme king-safety/hanging cases).

1303.label: Top: an undefended enemy queen sat capturable in a single move (usually by a knight or bishop) but the player chose a quiet developing move or grabbed a lesser piece, throwing away a ~5-6 pawn win; medium holds the hanging-queen theme but blurs out to also missing free rooks, one-move discovered-check wins, and occasionally even hanging one's own queen.

1351.label: Top: a quiet/repositioning move (centralize, develop, prophylaxis) ignores an available forcing material-winning tactic; medium broadens to also include greedy captures and passive moves that actively hang own material to the refutation.

1342.label: Top boards are king moves in losing rook-and-pawn endgames that let the relevant passed pawn promote (or walk the king into a promotion/king-hunt mate); medium keeps the same passed-pawn mishandling but blurs to rook/queen moves and assorted tactics (skewer, hanging rook, back-rank mate).

1357.label: Top is dominated by self-weakening pawn pushes that crack open one's own king and force mate from a difficult position; medium keeps the self-inflicted theme but blurs to rook/king/queen moves that hang material or allow back-rank/fork mates.

1355.label: At the peak a quiet/prophylactic or greedy move ignores an immediate king-safety/kingside threat (f2, g2, g7, pawn shield) and hangs material to a crashing attack; at medium it blurs into overlooking general tactical threats anywhere (forks, discovered attacks, hanging pieces) and occasionally missing one's own winning tactic.

1372.label: At the peak the player overlooks a concrete forced checkmate (usually mate-in-1/2/3, mostly back-rank/king-safety) while playing a materialistic capture or quiet developing move; at medium it blurs into missing any decisive resource — a winning tactic, the only saving defense, or a tempo/material edge — rather than strictly a mate, with a few cases tipping into outright hanging a piece.

1371.label: Top boards are king-safety lapses—a king/queen move or greedy capture that walks into a forced checkmate (rook second-rank/g-h-file ladder or queen mating net); medium broadens to moves that allow decisive checking attacks that merely win material or, often, force a perpetual-check draw that throws away the win rather than delivering mate.

1382.label: Top: king retreats to the corner/back-rank and walks straight into a one-move (or near-forced) checkmate; medium broadens to king retreats that lose material or a slower forced mate via checks/skewers/exposed king.

1341.label: Top: in a won/lost promotion endgame a passive king/rook move declines a free capture of a hanging enemy major piece (rook/queen) or a winning fork (Kxc3, Kxe8, Rxd2, Qxg3, Nd3+); medium blurs the same material theme in the other direction — hanging one's own knight (Na5/Nc5/Nf5) or king drifts that lose the pawn race or walk into mate — and several engine-best/0cp moves are misfired as blunders, so direction is genuinely split between missed-win and hung-piece.

1370.label: Top boards uniformly overlook an undefended enemy rook capturable for free in one move (usually by king or bishop) while playing an unrelated king/pawn move; medium boards blur to grabbing the wrong/lesser piece or to tempo, positional and king-safety inaccuracies that merely squander an already-winning position.

1378.chip: Hangs bishop to pawn tempo (often check)
1378.label: Top is uniformly an opening bishop check (Bb4+/Bb5+/Bg5+) that's refuted by a pawn block or push gaining tempo (c3/c6), losing the bishop or wasting moves; medium keeps the bishop-hit-by-a-tempo-pawn theme but blurs to non-checking bishop sorties (Bg4/Bd6/Bxe5) and a few unrelated tempo/material blunders (Ke6, Nbc6, Rdxe2, d6).

1392.label: Top: White makes a developing move—almost always a bishop (Bd3/Bd2/Bd5)—that leaves the centrally-posted Nd4 hanging to Nxd4 when the correct Nxc6 resolved the tension; medium broadens to other hung central units in the same opening structure (e5-pawn falling to Nxe5, Bg5 to Nxe4), still after skipping the same Nxc6 exchange.

1383.label: Top boards are drawn pawn endgames thrown away by a king misstep (Kf6, Kb5) or premature pawn push that loses the draw; medium blurs into broader passed-pawn/promotion mishandling and other endgame errors, several of which are near-best or missed-faster-win rather than outright losses.

1386.label: Top boards consistently miss or mis-order a forcing rook check (Re8+/Rd8+/Rc8+) that exploits the opponent's exposed king on an open file to win or save material; medium blurs to queen checks (Qg4+/Qf2+) and even non-check positions where a piece is simply left hanging.

1359.label: Top: a winning endgame is thrown away when a rook (or queen) forcing capture/check gets immediately recaptured—often by a pawn—losing material; medium blurs this to any piece (bishop/knight/queen) and even quiet moves across any phase, hanging material or trading into a lost position rather than via a clean rook recapture.

1374.label: Top: a premature central pawn capture (mostly exd5) that opens the position while underdeveloped and hands the opponent a tempo-gaining central recapture/knight outpost (d5/e5); medium keeps the 'capture releases tension' core but broadens to flank captures (bxa4, cxb4, axb5) and varied punishments—forks, hanging recaptures, and king-safety attacks rather than just a central outpost.

1391.label: Top: from a winning position the player makes a quiet/retreating move (often the queen) that overlooks a forcing capture or sacrifice setting up a fork, pin, deflection, or mate to win decisive material; medium broadens to other pieces and to simpler one-move captures of hanging pieces, sometimes where the chosen move also hangs own material.

1404.label: Top: an early queen sortie (Qg5/Qh5/Qf6/Qd6/Qg4) left immediately en prise to a pawn, bishop, or knight in a one-move oversight from an equal opening; medium keeps the opening material-loss theme but blurs the piece (rook via a-pawn/fianchetto exposure, queen via Nf3-leaving-Qd4) and the depth (multi-move pins/forks/tempo refutations like Bb4, Ndb5, g4–Qh4+).

1373.label: Top: a quiet king move or king-weakening pawn push (played instead of the one forced capture) walks into a decisive tactic—mate, absolute pin, or fork—on the exposed king, hanging heavy material; medium broadens to any non-capturing move (retreats, pushes, lesser piece moves) that ignores the sole saving/winning capture, mixing clear hangs with missed wins.

1395.label: Top: a non-addressing move (usually a king move or greedy capture) ignores an enemy passed pawn one step from queening, letting it promote/decide; medium broadens to failing to neutralize any critical threat — king-safety attacks, back-rank mates, hanging pieces, and forks.

1394.label: Top: hangs a minor piece for nothing, most often via an unsound sacrificial bishop check (Bxf2+, Bxf7+) or a simple oversight dropping a knight/bishop; medium: broadens to losing material (piece, exchange, or pawn) through overlooked forks, deflections, overloaded defenders, and mis-captures further into the game.

1400.label: Top: a quiet developing move (usually a bishop) ignores White's Bc4+Ng5 battery and hangs f7 to Nxf7, forking queen and rook; medium keeps the 'ignored opening fork' core but blurs to Nxc7+ rook/queen forks and other unaddressed early tactics (queen trap via Bc2, Nd6#, Bxh7+).

1406.label: Top is a constant unsound Fried-Liver-style Nxf7 (and Nxf2) knight sacrifice refuted by a simple king capture; medium blurs to assorted opening blunders that drop material around the f7/king-safety zone (hanging pieces, even a missed Bxf7+ win).

1408.label: Top is a premature central pawn break (almost always ...d5/e4) that hangs a clean pawn with the king still uncastled; medium keeps the premature-pawn-push theme but broadens to flank lunges chasing a piece (g5/b5/f5/c6, plus a stray develop/recapture) where the punishment ranges from dropping a pawn to allowing a sacrifice or fork that wins more.

1405.label: Top boards uniformly skip a free winning capture of an undefended rook (frequently Qxb3); medium boards still skip a rook capture but it broadens into defensive must-takes to halt a king attack/mate and occasionally targets another piece.

1369.label: Top: greedy captures (often a bishop in the opening) that ignore an enemy pawn breakthrough/check shattering the king (...exf2+, gxh7+, bxc2+); medium blurs to any move — tempo losses, missed simple captures — that overlooks the single decisive tactic (fork, skewer, mate, or promotion).

1398.label: Top: a clearly winning/better position is thrown away by a routine quiet move (castle, pawn push, piece reroute/retreat) that skips the one precise winning shot — frequently a centralizing knight (Ne5/Ne4/Nd5) or a fork; medium broadens beyond pure 'missed conversion' to also hanging material outright (Bd3, Rb7, Rcd8 into mate) and greedy grabs / bad trades, while keeping the same 'plausible-but-wrong move at a critical moment' signature.

1411.label: Top: a king move steps onto an exposed square and walks straight into forced mate (Kf7/Kg8/Kh1/Kd8); medium keeps the self-exposed-king theme but blurs to pawn advances that shatter the king's shield (g4, b3) and a few tempo-loss/missed-win king misplacements rather than pure mate-walks.

1415.label: Top: queen walks onto an attacked square (typically a bishop's open long diagonal, e.g. g2) and is captured for a bishop; medium broadens to hanging rooks/other pieces and occasionally just ignoring a tactic or trading into a lost position.

1412.label: Top: a quiet repositioning move—often king centralization (Ke6/Ke4)—wastes the critical tempo and skips the only forcing win (capture or pawn break) in a winning endgame; medium broadens to passive pawn pushes (f6/g6/g5) and other slow maneuvers that squander wins or equality, with a little noise (one mate allowed, one trapped piece, one non-blunder).

1407.label: Top: a bishop declines the thematic capture (Bxc3/Bxe2/Bxf3) and retreats onto a diagonal where a pawn thrust (b4–c5, g4, g5–f4) traps it; medium broadens to other declined-trade retreats—knights and other pieces—punished by tempo checks (Bb5+), forks (Nd4), or a hanging rook rather than pure pawn-trapping.

1397.label: Top boards play a passive king/queen/capture move that walks into a forced mate or decisive king-hunt (the one defense ignored); medium boards keep some mates but broaden to hanging material via greedy captures and pins, plus tempo/positional slips in already-losing positions.

1410.label: Top: a slow/greedy rook or king move throws away a winning or drawn endgame, most often letting an enemy passed pawn race or promote; medium keeps the lost-endgame theme but blurs the mechanism to king-exposure (checks/mating nets) and outright piece hangs.

1421.chip: Hangs material via backfiring check (often Bxf7+)
1421.label: Top boards are uniform unsound bishop-sacrifice checks (Bxf7+/Bxf2+/Bxh2+) that hang the bishop for a pawn with no attack; medium broadens to other self-damaging forcing moves (Qa8+, Be6+ premature checks, Qe2 hanging a rook, the greedy Bxa4) that lose material or squander a winning advantage.

1426.label: Top is uniformly a queen-giving check that hangs the queen to an enemy knight; medium keeps the self-hanging check but blurs the recapturer to bishop/king/queen/pawn and occasionally a non-queen piece or a pointless check that also skips a win.

1418.label: Top: an inactive/exposing king move in a won endgame throws away the win—either walking into a tempo-gaining rook check or skipping a forced mate/promotion instead of the active continuation; medium broadens to any piece move (knight, rook) and to merely-equal positions also collapsed by allowing the opponent a tempo-gaining check.

1420.label: Top: a slow, non-forcing move (king walk, prophylactic pawn push, or routine piece development) directly hangs own material to a concrete refutation, often via open files or king exposure; medium keeps the same 'quiet move when forcing action was required' theme but blurs the outcome to also include missed forced wins/mates, trapped pieces, en-passant breaks, and slower positional concessions.

1424.label: Top: a quiet/repositioning move (pawn push, king walk, rook or knight retreat) skips capturing a hanging/undefended enemy piece for a clean material win; medium broadens to other missed winning captures (forks, sacrifices, even mate-in-one) and blurs in a few cases where the same quiet move instead leaves one's OWN piece hanging.

1423.label: Top boards are quiet, tempo-losing king moves in winning endgames (plus the recurring f5+ pawn-fork miss) that squander a forced mate or material win; medium broadens to other slow rook/pawn/bishop/queen moves that skip a decisive capture, check, or fixing pawn, throwing away won pawn endgames and forced mates.

1434.label: Top boards uniformly miss a winning/mating queen check against an exposed or uncastled king (almost always Qh4+/Qh5+-type) in favor of a slow pawn/knight move; medium broadens to other forcing exposed-king tactics—queen forks (Qd5+), mate-in-ones, and reflexive wrong-checks (b5+, Rh1+)—and occasionally to quiet moves that themselves hang material rather than purely skipping a win.

1439.chip: Hangs piece to recapture (often pawn fork)
1439.label: Top: capturing White's centralized e5-knight (Nxe5/Bxe5) is refuted by dxe5/fxe5 — a pawn fork hitting the d6-bishop and f6-knight, or ripping open the f-file against the king; medium broadens to trading other centralized pieces (d4/d5/e4) where a pawn (or simple) recapture wins material or squanders a winning advantage.

1393.label: Top boards are losing-position king moves that hang a rook by skipping the forced rook trade/capture (Rxd1/Rxc8/Rxd8/Rxf7); medium blurs to any quiet, non-addressing move (king, bishop, queen, pawn) dropping any piece — knight, bishop or rook — often to a fork or check, with a few shading toward missed wins/positional drift.

1440.chip: Allowed enemy pawn to queen (or mate)
1440.label: Top boards uniformly let an enemy passed pawn promote to a winning queen—usually by grabbing material/checking or pushing one's own pawn instead of blockading/checking; medium boards keep the same ignored-promotion theme but the queening now more often forces mate (and blurs into king-misplacement, slow piece repositioning, and even a pure back-rank mate).

1428.label: Top is tightly consistent—a queen (or rook) trade via capture+check that simplifies a drawn/holdable position into a lost king-and-pawn (or minor-piece) endgame, surrendering the only piece that stopped a passer; medium loses this thread entirely, blurring into an unrelated grab-bag of forcing blunders (hanging a pawn, walking into a fork or mate, miscapturing/missing a bigger win).

1422.chip: Allows opponent decisive gain (top: king pawn-race)
1422.label: Top: in a lost king-and-pawn endgame the king (or knight) heads the wrong way or steps into check, letting the opponent's passed pawn promote—often with check leading to forced mate; medium broadens to any decisive concession (back-rank mates, Qa4+ knight-forks, unblocked hanging pieces, lost rook-endgame trades) and even a couple of missed wins in non-losing middlegames.

1443.label: Top: a quiet developing/pawn move hangs the f3-knight to the simple ...exf3 pawn capture in the opening (constant: minor piece lost to a pawn); medium blurs to hanging other pieces (bishop/knight to a queen recapture, loose pawns) and to slow tempo-losing moves that ignore an available opening tactic (e.g., Ng5/Nxe4).

1448.label: Top is a uniform unsound bishop sacrifice on the king (Bxf7/Bxh7/Bxh2/Bxf2) that recaptures to a lost piece with no real attack; medium keeps the same king-targeting sacrifice but blurs to add a knight version (Nxf7) and an occasional non-sac missed tactic.

1429.label: At the peak the player skips a unique forcing winning resource (a capture, fork, check, or en passant — often the only good move) in a winning/critical position by instead playing a quiet repositioning move; at medium it blurs so the slow move (a passive piece relocation or a pawn push) not only misses the win but creates a target or opens a line, letting the opponent's refutation seize the advantage or win material outright.

1445.label: Top: a rook redeployed to an open file (repeatedly Rd8/Rc8) is left en prise and lost to a capture, frequently delivered with check, throwing away a winning or equal position; medium broadens to queens, bishops, and knights pushed to 'active'/centralizing squares that likewise hang material or squander the win by ignoring the concrete tactic — so the constant is the 'activity-seeking' relocation while the piece type and exact penalty (hang vs. missed win) blur.

1453.label: Top boards uniformly walk into an immediate mate-in-1 (typically by playing an aggressive move—often attacking the enemy queen—while ignoring a standing mate threat); medium blurs to forced mates delivered over several moves (mate-in-4/6) plus a couple of plain material losses.

1438.label: Top: a quiet developing move was played instead of harassing/trapping an enemy queen that grabbed material on b2/b7 with a b-file rook (Rb1/Rb8/Rab1); medium broadens to failing to punish an exposed queen on any square (c6/f5/e-file) and blurs further into own-side king-safety and hanging-piece lapses.

1430.label: Top: declines a winning capture of a hanging enemy piece (usually a knight, often via the queen, e.g. Qxb5/Qxd4); medium broadens and flips direction to careless moves that hang one's own piece or walk into forks/mate, plus some pure positional/endgame drift.

1457.label: Top: slow/indirect king-and-rook maneuvers wasting a tempo in winning endgames (often near-0cp false-flags); medium broadens to prophylactic opening moves and redundant transposing checks — but contaminated by a few true material drops (Ra1, Re8, missed Nc6+ fork).

1449.label: Top boards blow a winning position by hanging a major piece (queen/rook), usually instead of an available forcing win/mate; medium blurs the material to minor pieces, pawns, exchange-losing trades, and tempo/positional slips that throw away the won eval.

1473.label: Top boards miss a clean mate-in-1/2 (usually a queen check vs an exposed king), often by grabbing material instead; medium broadens to deeper mates (3–6) and right-idea-wrong-execution cases (wrong check or move-order lets the king escape).

1459.label: Top boards are central pawn breaks (...d5/...d4/...e5 or a wrong central recapture) that drop a pawn to a simple recapture (fxe5/exd5/cxd5/exd4+); medium broadens to flank or kingside pawn advances (b5, c5, g4, e6, f5) and miscaptures that likewise hang material, with a minority that instead skip a tactical win.

1472.label: Top boards consistently hang a minor piece (usually a bishop, often to a pawn capture like axb6) by playing a 'natural' developing/repositioning move that ignores a concrete capture threat; medium blurs this to any piece lost via a tempo-gaining attack (and a couple of missed wins), so the constant is 'ignored immediate threat → lost own material,' which broadens from bishop-to-pawn at the peak to general piece/tempo loss.

1468.label: Top: an aggressive/centralizing piece move (Qf3, Nd3, Nc4, Rc2, Bf6) that walks into a forced favorable exchange simplifying into a clearly worse/lost ENDGAME or structure; medium keeps the active-looking move but blurs from clean forced trades to general positional/tempo concessions (Bd5 ignoring the urgent rook contest).

1475.label: Top boards are queen-trade captures (Qxd1/Qxd8) that abandon a winning attack on an exposed/uncastled king, missing material or a continuing assault; medium keeps the same premature queen exchange but broadens the trade square and the squandered win — now also forgone forks, free pawns, and pure positional/attacking pressure rather than only king-hunt material.

1450.label: Top boards are uniformly rook captures that start an even trade while skipping a deflecting check/zwischenzug (Bxh6+, Ba6+, f7+, Nc6+) that would have won the exchange or forced mate; medium blurs to other capturing pieces and a wider set of skipped wins (knight forks, outright mates, or quiet positional shots) rather than purely deflection-check intermezzos.

1465.label: Top: natural opening moves — minor-piece development or central pawn pushes (Be6, Bd2, d5, f5) — that ignore a vulnerable piece or central tension and drop material to a short combination (removing-defender/fork); medium blurs into passive bishop retreats and slow queen reroutes (Bb3, Bg3, Qe1, Qd6) that squander an edge, miss a tactic, or only concede positionally.

1455.label: At the peak a committal pawn push (d6, e4) directly hangs a piece by neglecting its defense; at medium it blurs to any slow flank/repositioning move (Nh5, b6) that abandons a key defender or king cover and is punished either by material loss or a decisive kingside attack.

1474.label: Top: purposeless checks that either hang a queen/bishop outright or waste a critical tempo while improving the enemy king; medium broadens to checks that merely drive the king to a better square and to non-check tempo-losing king/pawn moves.

1479.label: Top: hangs a full minor piece (almost always a bishop on f3/f6) by playing a quiet developing move—Be7, Be2, castling—instead of the obvious recapture; medium broadens to wider opening capture/tension errors (missing exd5/dxe5 captures, removing a key defender, or grabbing the wrong material), still mostly losing material but occasionally just missing a winning capture.

1477.label: Top: a quiet or tempo-wasting move ignores an urgent tactic and lets a minor piece (typically the bishop, often to a b4/Bg2-type break or a knight fork) be won; medium broadens to any material dropped after a slow move that neglects the opponent's immediate threat.

1485.label: Top: a wrong-move-order bishop capture (mostly Bxf6/Bxf3) that ignores an in-between move — typically exf6 or Nxf6+ — and hangs material in the resulting trade; medium broadens to any move (pawn pushes like b5/g6/c4/a6, castling, other captures) that overlooks an immediate tactical refutation (zwischenzug, fork, free capture) and drops a piece.

1476.label: Top: a passive queen blockade (Qa1/Qa8) or slow king/pawn move in a queen+passed-pawn endgame abandons the saving perpetual check, letting the enemy pawn promote; medium broadens to any tempo-wasting passive move (king-exposing steps, slow pushes, dropped attacks) punished by promotion, forks, or a king hunt.

1454.label: At the peak the best move is uniformly a queen exchange (Qx) that the player declines or plays in the wrong order, hanging their own undefended queen; at medium this blurs to any skipped critical capture/simplification — removing a king-defender, wrong capture order, or a missed tactic — often involving non-queen material rather than a queen trade.

1495.chip: Hangs queen to open-diagonal bishop (any material)
1495.label: At the peak a natural developing move hangs the queen to an enemy bishop on a wide-open long diagonal (Bxd8 / Bxd1); at medium it broadens to hanging or losing assorted material — and occasionally missing a win — by playing a routine move that ignores an existing tactical threat.

1496.label: Top: in a winning position the player grabs material immediately (usually a safe king-capture) instead of first inserting a stronger tempo-gaining check/zwischenzug (Nd6+, b3+, b5#, g5+, g4+, g6+) that wins more or mates; medium blurs to quiet/trade moves that squander the edge through general tempo loss rather than a clear missed intermediate check.

1478.label: At the peak the player hangs a rook/queen by skipping the one forced capture-or-trade that would stop an enemy passed pawn from promoting; at medium it blurs to forced captures in general material situations (queen deserting a defender, even a missed winning capture) plus a few near-equal non-blunders.

1480.label: Top: trades the queen for a rook (often with check) into a still-winning endgame, throwing away a forced mate; medium: blurs to any move that squanders a winning/defensible position — hanging a piece, missing a capture, or allowing a fork.

1497.label: Top boards: a quiet developing/pawn move (b3, Nc3, a3, Qc7, Na5) ignores a forcing knight strike in the opening center—most often Nxe5/Nxg5/Nxe4 exploiting f7; medium blurs to other missed shots (Bxe7, Ncxe5, Nxe4) and even greedy/quiet moves refuted multi-ply by Nxf3+ forks or Bb5+, so direction mixes missed-win with hanging material.

1484.label: Top: a major-piece move (mostly queens, some rooks) that allows or initiates an exchange simplifying into a clearly lost endgame; medium blurs into other piece trades, back-rank/fork tactics, and missed winning captures.

1467.label: Top: a clearly winning position (passed-pawn/promotion or up-a-piece) is spoiled by an imprecise capture/move-order slip or a missed clean win, often still leaving an edge; medium broadens to outright blunders that hang a major piece, allow forced mate, or skip a free capture.

1490.label: Top: a tempting check/push/trade lets the opponent's passed pawn promote—almost always by removing or trading away the only piece that blockades/stops it in a lost endgame; medium: blurs to any plan-driven move (king march, greedy grab, wrong reroute) that abandons a critical defensive duty—often still a passer or promotion square, but sometimes a guarded pawn, key square, or available draw.

1498.label: Top boards are passive/wrong-direction KING moves in pawn/rook endgames that burn the critical tempo and squander counterplay or the winning breakthrough (loss accruing over the refutation); medium blurs to slow rook moves, premature pawn pushes, and even outright hanging pieces in middlegames.

1487.chip: Hangs material (often whole piece in won game)
1487.label: Top boards throw away a winning/won position by hanging a whole piece or walking into mate (with a minority that just skips the clinching capture like Rxf3/Qxf5); medium broadens to roughly equal positions losing pawns, allowing mate, or dropping material through opened diagonals/files, removed defenders, and trapped pieces.

1505.label: Top: played a slow piece-attack instead of the winning tempo-gaining QUEEN check (Qb6+/Qa4+/Qb3+/Qxc6+, often a zwischenzug) and let the target escape; medium blurs the 'queen check' constant into any missed forcing resource or non-forcing/slow move (king walks into attacks, passive development, endgame king moves, missed winning captures) that squanders a won/equal position.

1503.chip: Missed pawn thrust vs knight (or queen)
1503.label: Top boards are uniformly a passive/quiet move that skips the forcing pawn thrust (f4 vs Ne5, also g4/b4/c4/g5) which attacks or traps a misplaced enemy KNIGHT, squandering a winning edge; medium keeps the 'pawn-break-to-hit-an-enemy-piece' theme but broadens the target from knight to queen (b4 hitting Qa5+Nc5, c6) and blurs into adjacent errors — self-weakening pushes, hung own pieces, and missed forks/mates.

1504.label: Top: declined a forcing check (frequently a forced mate) in favor of a quiet/non-forcing move; medium broadens to any missed winning tactic—back-rank, discovered, trapped/hanging-piece wins and quiet recaptures—where the win isn't always a check, plus a little greedy/positional noise.

1518.label: Top: a bishop check (Bh6+, Bh5+, Be3+, Bg4+) played from a won position that either hangs the bishop or lets the opponent block/escape, throwing away a forced mate or winning advantage instead of the concrete crusher; medium keeps the same 'patzer sees a check' essence but blurs to knight and rook checks (Ne5+, Rh8+, Rxe8+) — direction is genuinely mixed between hanging the checking piece (~60%) and a safe check that merely skips the win (~40%).

1506.label: Top: a quiet non-capturing move (often ...d6) hangs a full piece by ignoring central pawn tension / an available capture in the opening; medium broadens to passive or premature opening moves (b3/c4, early ...Qb6/Qb3, Bg2) that mishandle the same central/opening tension but only drop a pawn or tempo, and occasionally flip direction to missing a win like Qh5+.

1499.label: Top: in a won pawn endgame the player commits to their own promotion—usually pushing their passed pawn one square (b2/b3/c3/a7) or wrong-pawn/wrong-capture promotion technique—instead of the single precise move, so the opponent's counter-passer or sac wins the race; medium broadens to any king/rook/queen move (positional rook shuffles, king maneuvers, failing to halt the enemy passer, even a king walk into a skewer) that throws away the unique winning/saving resource in a sharp winning endgame.

1512.label: Top: winning/mating endgames where a forcing queen check (often delivering or speeding up mate) was skipped for a slower or self-destructive move; medium broadens to general imprecise endgame conversion — king/pawn-endgame technique, missed perpetuals, tempo-losing checks — with a minority of greedy captures that hang material over a few moves.

1501.label: Top: a quiet kingside pawn move (h6/h5/e6) lets a knight smash the king's pawn shield via Nxg6/Nxe6 (forced fxg6, doubled pawns, open f-file); medium blurs to other pieces left for a knight capture (Nxe5) or king left exposed, now winning outright material rather than just wrecking structure.

1525.label: Top: a piece (usually the queen) leaves a critical defensive duty—typically declining a forced queen trade—so an immediate capture wins material; medium broadens to any piece (bishop/knight/king) repositioning that skips a needed capture/exchange, including development tempo-losses, trapped-piece and back-rank motifs, still hanging material.

1536.chip: Hangs bishop on f7 sac (or f2)
1536.label: Top boards are uniformly unsound Bxf7+ bishop sacrifices by the c4-bishop with no developed pieces to follow up; medium broadens to premature minor-piece sacs on the weak f-square for either color (Bxf7+/Bxf2+, also from h5) plus a few stray over-optimistic captures like Qxf7 or Nxe4.

1535.label: At the peak, the player skips an obvious capture of the opponent's completely undefended queen (Qxh1, Rxh8, Bxc7, Nxb4); at medium it broadens to missing other free winning captures (rook Bxf1, pawn Nxe4) or other clean wins (Bxe7, forced mates), with an occasional own-piece hang by castling into Bxh6.

1517.label: Top: a slow non-forcing move (often a flank pawn push like h3/a4/b3/g3) fails to challenge a dominant enemy rook on an open file or 2nd/7th rank, conceding material/initiative over the next moves; medium broadens to general passive, greedy, or careless moves that lose material or skip a forcing win, with the active-rook anchor only sometimes present.

1534.label: At the peak the player drops a minor piece (bishop/knight) via a greedy capture or loose advance that's met by a simple recapture; at medium it broadens to any material—queen, rook or pawns—lost to recaptures, tactics (fork/pin/overload) or slower positional collapse.

1524.chip: Hangs material to overlooked tactic (often tempo-loss)
1524.label: Top boards squander a winning/even position via a tempo-losing or king-weakening natural move (g6/h6 pushes, queen/knight retreats, vanity checks) that invites the opponent's tactic; medium boards blur into blunter material drops—removing a defender, wrong recapture, or ignoring an undefended piece.

1538.chip: Hangs knight in f7 sac (or f2)
1538.label: Top is dominated by the Fried-Liver-style Nxf7 knight sacrifice (plus the mirror ...Nxf2) that the king simply recaptures, leaving a piece down for one pawn in a roughly even opening; medium narrows to the pure Bg5→Nxf7 sac with the same trivial Kxf7 refutation.

1528.label: Top boards hang a piece/pawn by leaving it undefended—removing or failing to supply a defender (classically a loose f3-knight grabbed by Bxf3, or abandoning c6/b2)—while medium boards keep the material-losing tactic but blur across broader oversights: back-rank mates, forks, wrong-way recaptures, greedy grabs, and even declined saving trades.

1502.label: Top: from a winning position a loose tempo-losing move (often the queen) misplaces a piece or abandons a key guarding square, missing the single precise winning continuation; medium broadens to roughly-equal positions where the loose move instead outright hangs material via forks, trapped pieces, or king-weakening pawn pushes.

1527.label: At the peak the player makes a slow prophylactic or retreating move (a4, Ng5-e4, Rc1) that squanders a winning position by skipping the demanded forcing central break/attack (f4, e5, d4, Bxg6) while staying materially safe; at medium it blurs to similar passive moves that miss tactics (Greek Gift, en passant) or directly drop material by allowing a pin or removing a key defender.

1529.label: Top: in an endgame the player plays a quiet king/pawn move and skips the single forced capture (queen/rook/pawn, often with check) that was the only move to hold or win; medium blurs to skipping any one precise winning resolution—promotion, rook lift, or exchange sac—not necessarily a capture.

1545.label: Top: capturing/trading the queen (or rook) into a hopelessly lost (occasionally only drawn) pawn endgame, the strong piece being the player's whole advantage; medium keeps the trade-into-worse-endgame theme but blurs to minor-piece trades and other captures/moves that instead simply hang material, drop a forced mate, or skip the one saving move.

1541.label: Top: a forced checkmate—almost always mate-in-one with the queen (frequently Qxf2#) against an exposed king—is overlooked for a natural recapture/developing move; medium broadens to missing the single best move that preserves a winning or drawn position (longer mates, a winning capture, a saving check/perpetual, or avoiding hanging material).

1530.label: TOP: a queen/rook moved to an aggressive square (often doubling rooks or a queen sortie) that abandons the king/mating net — missing forced mate or hanging the king to mate; MEDIUM blurs to any active queen/rook move that hangs material to a tactic (discovered attack, undefended piece) or misses a win, losing the king-specificity.

1551.label: Top: an immediate recapture skips a needed intermediate check/capture (zwischenzug), leaving a bishop hanging for free; medium keeps the wrong-recapture-order theme but broadens the hung piece to knight/rook and the missed intermezzo to trades/desperados, with a few looser positional miscounts.

1559.label: Top boards uniformly drop a piece to a clean one-ply capture—either the piece just moved (rook lift to a3/h6) or a defender removed leaving the queen/rook en prise; medium boards keep the same self-inflicted-loss core but blur from material into king-safety, where the careless move instead exposes the own king to mate or a decisive attack (g4+, opened files, shattered pawn shield).

1550.label: Top: a forcing queen-trade — almost always a queen check like Qx+ — voluntarily liquidates the queens and dissolves an otherwise winning king-attack/mating net; medium keeps the 'throw away the win by simplifying' core but blurs the mechanism to non-checking queen trades, wrong-order/wrong-piece queen moves, and even imprecise king-tempo or missed-mate moves that surrender a won position.

1552.label: Top boards are king pawn-grabs in pawn/passed-pawn endings (Kxb5, Kxf5, Kxg6) that put the king on the wrong side and lose the resulting promotion race; medium blurs to pawn pushes (b4, b6, a5) that waste a tempo and let the opponent's passer queen first — though several boards (e.g. Kxb5/Kxf5) are flagged as near-zero-loss false positives.

1560.label: Top boards are uniformly a safe rook move that declines the decisive rook exchange into a won king-and-pawn endgame; medium broadens to other missed winning simplifications — queen trades, exchange sacs, and grabbing free pieces — all skipping the conversion.

1557.chip: Hangs queen on a check (rook at medium)
1557.label: Top is consistently a queen capture-with-check (Qxg7+, Qxf1+, Qf7+...) whose forcing 'check' is refuted by simple recapture or an unfavorable queen-for-rook trade, squandering a winning attack or forced mate; at medium the piece blurs to rook checks (Rxf1+, Re8+, Rf4+) and other forcing captures that likewise hang the piece or skip a cleaner win.

1554.label: Top positions almost uniformly miss a winning queen check (Qh5+/Qa4+/Qa5+) that exploits an uncastled or ...f6-weakened king in the opening to win material; medium blurs to missing the precise forcing move more generally — right-square/wrong-piece checks (Bb6+ vs Qb6+), knight checks/forks (Nd2+, Nd8+), purposeless checks instead of the winning one, and even quiet preparatory or pawn-endgame precision.

1562.label: Top: in an already-losing position the player makes a king-exposing move (often the king itself walking, e.g. Kg2/Ke2/Kh3, or a rook abandoning a defensive square) that converts 'lost-but-fighting' into a forced mate; medium broadens to any move that removes a key defender or simply hangs a piece, sometimes still allowing mate but often just dropping material.

1563.label: Top: from an already-losing position, plays a non-defensive queen/pawn/king move that ignores a forced checkmate against its own exposed king; medium keeps the 'ignored critical threat' theme but blurs from forced mate to also include hanging material (queen/exchange) and king-exposing endgame errors.

1556.label: Top boards are greedy opening pawn/piece captures (often removing the f7- or king-shielding knight) that strip the king's defense and get hit by a winning check (Qf3+/Qh4+/Qxg2); medium broadens to any king-weakening move — pins/developments that get forked (Bb4, Bg4), loosening pushes (h3, f5, exf5), even a king march into mate.

1553.label: Top: a quiet pawn/bishop/queen move (no capture/check) ignores a concrete threat or removes a defender, dropping a minor piece to a direct capture or simple knight fork; medium keeps the 'quiet move enables a material-winning tactic' core but blurs the motif (pins, discovered attacks, exchange-winning shots, king forks/mate) and the material (up to queen/exchange or forced mate).

1564.label: Top: a passive 'natural' move (king step, pawn push, retreat) ignores a standing forced mating attack on the player's own king, allowing forced mate; medium broadens to ignoring any immediate tactical obligation—hanging a piece/pawn or skipping the required defensive/capturing move.

1544.label: Top: in an already-winning position a tempting check/forcing move loses tempo toward mate (or hangs the checking piece) when a clean capture or faster mate was available; medium broadens to outright missed forced mates and free captures passed up for natural aggressive or developing moves.

1567.chip: Hangs piece on vain check (often queen)
1567.label: At the peak, a queen check that simply hangs the queen on a defended square (or skips a winning capture); at medium it broadens to rook/bishop checks and to merely tempo-wasting checks that improve the enemy king — with a couple of genuinely sound forcing checks mixed in.

1570.label: Top: a routine developing move (usually castling) misses the decisive Qa4+/Qa5+ check on the a4-e8 diagonal, a fork winning a loose minor piece (almost always the Bb4) off the uncastled king; medium broadens to other forcing queen-checks winning loose material (Qxc3+, Qe3+, Qd4+, Qa4+→Qxe4+) and shades into positions that instead hang material to the opponent's analogous queen-check/fork.

1582.label: Top boards are almost uniformly a missed checkmate-in-one (a 'safe' pawn push or rook shuffle that hands the trapped king an escape square); medium blurs to missed longer forced mates (2–11 moves) and occasionally just skipping a decisive material/positional win.

1565.label: Top: rook checks in lost endgames that either drive the enemy king to a stronger square or simply hang the rook ('patzer sees a check'); medium broadens the checking piece to queen/bishop/pawn and adds capture-checks/sacrifices that likewise help the opponent or shed material, so the harm splits between hanging material and pure tempo/eval loss.

1583.chip: Passive king in lost endgame (edge→any wrong-way)
1583.label: Top boards: in a clearly losing endgame the king drifts to the rim/corner (Kh5, Ka3, Ka6, Kh4, Kf7) instead of centralizing or supporting the key pawn/blockade, often turning the loss into a forced mate or unstoppable promotion; medium broadens to any wrong-direction/passive king move toward the edge—including already-lost positions where the move is barely (or not) a real mistake (0cp).

1543.label: Top: a natural king sidestep (Kf8/Kf1/Kd2) declines capturing the free checking bishop on f7/f2 in the opening when Kxf7/Kxf2 wins a full piece; medium blurs to other declined king captures (Kxd5, Kxg7), missed non-king captures and forks (Nxg6, hxg4, Ne7+), and king moves that simply walk into a winning attack.

1569.label: Top is tightly a rook (sometimes queen) check that forces a simplifying exchange of the player's most active piece — surrendering the advantage or trading into a lost endgame; medium keeps the 'tempting check' core but blurs the failure mode, adding queen/discovered checks that hang the checking piece outright (back-rank, Rxh8) or skip a clearly stronger win (Nc5 trap, fxe6, Rxe6).

1580.label: Top: a king step onto a diagonal/file unmasks a discovered check that wins material; medium keeps discovered checks but broadens to other walk-into-a-tactic blunders (back-rank mates, hanging a piece on a defended square, exposed-king lines).

1578.label: Top: a quiet, non-forcing rook (or queen) move overlooks the position's tactic and hangs material to a fork/discovered-check/back-rank shot (or skips a forcing win); medium broadens to any non-capturing move—king walks, wrong-rook, tempo-losing developing moves—that concedes material or the initiative rather than strictly hanging a piece.

1573.chip: Hangs bishop on unsound capture (any minor)
1573.label: Top: an over-aggressively advanced or capturing bishop is left en prise or dumped in a losing trade (often Bf6/Bxf6, also Bxd5/Bxg6/Bxg3); medium blurs the piece to knight sacs (Nxf2/Nxf7) and pawn captures that open lines onto an undefended piece, even slipping into a missed-win retreat.

1585.label: Top: a winning endgame where a king/pawn move skips the clean rook-for-knight exchange-sacrifice that liquidates into a trivially won K+P endgame; medium broadens the missed liquidation to any minor-piece capture or exchange (bishop, knight, king-takes-knight) that simplifies into a winning endgame.

1572.label: Top boards are greedy/decisive captures that walk straight into a forced checkmate (overwhelmingly mate-in-1, king already in a self-made net); medium keeps the 'ignored the opponent's decisive threat' core but blurs the consequence—some still allow mate-in-1, others merely drop the exchange/queen (Nxd2, Qxf6, Bxg1) or concede a winning positional/king infiltration (a3, b6, Kh8).

1590.label: Top boards are winning kingside attacks where a slow queen/rook-to-h move (Qh3/Qh4/Qh5/Qh6, Rxh3) skips a forced mate or piece-winning capture; medium blurs to lesser kingside imprecisions — tempo/move-order losses, hung rooks to a bishop, and allowing a defusing queen trade — plus some false positives where the h-file attacking move was actually best.

1591.label: Top boards are passive moves—king walks/retreats or back-rank-blind moves—that ignore or step into a forced mate or mating net (king-safety constant at the peak); medium broadens to the same threat-ignoring/non-defending moves that instead hang a piece or pawn for plain material loss.

1581.label: Top: king/queen moves that expose the monarch and lose material to a lines-opening attack (Kh7, Kh8, Kg2, Bxh2+, Qg6+); medium broadens to pawn-shelter pushes (h4/g5/g6/f6) and slow moves that ignore king safety — though a real minority are plain hung pieces or missed winning captures.

1594.label: Top: failed to find the unique rook/piece sacrifice with a deflecting check that converts a won/drawn position into a winning or holdable king-and-pawn endgame; medium blurs to other precise endgame resources (pawn-sac deflections, opposition, active rook checks) and occasional loose trades, with direction mostly 'missed' but a quarter of cases actually hanging material.

1596.label: Top boards are won/drawn positions where the player skips an immediate winning queen check/capture (Qxg3+, Qxh3+, Qxg6+, Qh6+) for a slow preparatory move, letting a defensive resource (g4, ...Rg8 trapping the queen, or a perpetual) save the opponent; medium broadens to any missed forcing blow — non-queen checks (Nxd5+, Ng5+, Rh8+), move-order errors, and greedy pawn-grabs (Rxa2, Rxh2, d4) — that either hang material or squander the forcing win.

1593.label: TOP is uniformly a tempo-wasting check that hands the enemy king a safer escape square and throws away a won/equal position; MEDIUM keeps the spite-check core but blurs into checks that outright hang material or skip a forced mate/perpetual, plus a few non-check single-good-move squanders.

1592.label: Top boards almost all miss a single decisive forcing CHECK in an already-winning position — typically a queen capture-with-check (Qxe3+, Qxd4+, Qg3+, Qxg5+, Qxe4+, Qxa1+) — the player instead playing a passive/aimless queen move; medium broadens to non-checking winning shots (Qxd2, Qxf2, Ne6/Nxf3 forks, Qxf5) and additionally blurs into outright hangs of material (f6 pin, Bxh2, Rg1 allowing mate, Re4), so direction shifts from clean 'missed win' at the peak to a missed-win/hang mix at medium.

1599.label: At the peak the player greedily grabbed material (usually the queen, often with check) and converted a forced checkmate / fastest forced win into a merely winning position; at medium strength it blurs to simply passing up the single strongest move (a winning check/tactic or attack-preserving move) in an already-better position, settling for a smaller edge.

1602.label: At the peak, the player makes a quiet/natural developing move in a clearly winning position and skips a decisive forcing shot — repeatedly the Bxf7+ sacrifice, plus a hanging-piece grab or mate-in-1; at medium this blurs to any passive/slow move that squanders the advantage by missing the single best continuation, occasionally even one that outright hangs material.

1597.label: Top boards consistently give back the queen with check to capture the opponent's advanced passed pawn (usually the a-pawn) in a still-won endgame, conceding material via the immediate recapture (Qxa7+/Qxh6/Qxf2 met by KxQ); medium blurs to a flat queen-hang (Qxf2 → +556 to +50) and even non-capturing moves (Rc8) that merely squander the fastest forced win, so direction wobbles between 'hangs queen' and 'missed faster conversion.'

1605.label: Top: a major piece is shuffled to a passive back-rank square (Qd4-a1) that abandons king defense and invites a forced attack/mate; medium blurs the piece type and direction — a rook self-block (Ra1-d1 allowing Rf1+ mate) plus a slow king-hunt check (Qg4-b4+) that merely misses a faster mate rather than losing material.

1601.label: Top: a natural opening developer walks into a winning knight fork, overwhelmingly Nc7+ forking king and rook (royal fork); medium keeps the 'developing move loses material to a refutation' core but broadens the tactic to pawn forks, Nf7 forks, plain hanging pieces, and overloaded defenders.

1576.label: Top boards hinge on a decisive forcing check the player missed or allowed—often a winning capture-check, back-rank/king-attack mate, or the wrong recapture that drops the check; medium broadens to general material-losing or win-missing blunders where the forcing-check element fades.

1608.label: Top: a developed/pinning bishop (light-squared on g4-h5 or dark-squared on h4-g5) is left hanging or trapped, often by skipping the tension-resolving Bxe2 or by playing g3 that boxes it in; medium keeps the hung-bishop core but broadens to knights (and occasionally the queen) left en prise via the same move-order/zwischenzug oversight.

1603.chip: Hangs to check on opened line (capture)
1603.label: Top: a (usually pawn) capture toward the own king opens a diagonal, refuted by a recapture-with-check (Bxf4+/Qxd4+/Bxe5+/Bxe6+) that wins material; medium broadens beyond captures to any move (piece relocation, pawn push, king step, abandoned guard) that opens a line/file to the king or vacates a defender, punished by a check or check-sequence (incl. skewers) netting material.

1610.label: Top boards are king-exposing/non-defensive moves in already-lost positions that walk into a FORCED MATE (king-safety blunders, mostly king moves); medium blurs to the same failure-to-defend allowing decisive MATERIAL loss instead (forks, back-rank, hanging pieces, discovered attacks).

1607.label: Top boards are an opening minor piece (usually a knight) hung by grabbing/sacking on a central pawn (e4/f2/d4) with no compensation, refuted by a simple recapture or fork; medium blurs to any material-losing opening move — bishops/knights placed en prise, king-weakening pawn pushes (f6/f5/h3) inviting sacrifices, premature castling, and one missed mate.

1588.label: At peak, a winning side commits an active blunder hanging a queen or rook; at medium activation the mechanism blurs to passively missing a forced mate or a free piece — same theme of throwing away a won position, opposite direction (hang vs. missed win).

1612.label: At the peak it's a winning position where a pawn discovered-check (dxc4+/exd5+/d6+) wins the queen but the player instead retreats or temporizes (Be7, Qf4, Ra8); at medium it blurs to missing any decisive finish—forced mates (Nf5+, Ng5+), winning captures (Qxh8, Qxd8), or correct move order—often by a passive/wrong check or by abandoning the active piece that delivered the win.

1631.label: Top: knight grabs the f7 or f2 pawn as an unsound 'fork' sacrifice that White/Black simply recaptures (Kxf7/Kxf2/Qe2+/Qf3), losing a piece for a pawn; medium keeps the same idea but blurs to knight-fork grabs on other squares (Nxc7+, Nxc3, Nxe4) that likewise just hang.

1626.label: Top: a bishop snaps off a 'free' pawn—almost always the fianchetto pawn on b7/g7/g2/b2—and is simply recaptured, losing a minor piece for a pawn; medium broadens the piece and refutation, adding knight pawn-grabs (Nxe4 punished by Qa4+ fork) and even a hung rook.

1615.label: Top: a completely won endgame (K+R or Q vs K) is squandered—usually into a draw—by playing a needless or wrong-square check instead of the decisive capture/trade/promotion; medium broadens to other non-converting moves (inefficient rook reposition, pawn push, missed fork) with smaller eval loss.

1614.chip: Passive king move loses tempo (or pawn)
1614.label: Top positions are passive king retreats/non-active king moves that squander a tempo in already-lost positions (often hastening a forced mate); medium broadens to slow pawn pushes and other inactive moves that fail to activate the king, with a few genuine material/tactical errors (hung knight, missed Qa5+, greedy Nxh2) blurring the pattern.

1624.label: Top boards are uniformly king-safety mating situations where the move abandons the king's key defender (g2/h2/g3) or ignores an imminent mate—and a few mirror it by missing a forced mate/winning sac; medium boards blur to any critical-moment failure to find the single forcing move (tempo losses, hanging pieces, forks, promotions), not always involving mate, so direction splits ~60/40 between hanging (allowing the opponent's win) and missing one's own win.

1629.label: TOP boards are tempo-grabs chasing the enemy queen that hang the player's own material (frequently the queen itself); MEDIUM broadens to any forcing/attacking move on a knight, rook or bishop that overlooks a refutation netting the opponent a piece.

1635.label: Top: a knight is parked on an undefended central square (almost always Nxd4 grabbing a pawn) and is immediately captured by the queen (Qxd4) for a clean piece; medium keeps the hung-knight core but blurs the capturer and context — the refutation may be a pawn, a check (Qxe4+), or a short tactic (Bb5+), the moved piece can even be a bishop (Bg4→Qxg4) or a knight left en prise while castling, so it broadens from 'knight hung to queen' to 'minor piece hung to any capture.'

1617.label: Top boards ignore a decisive attack on the king (forced mate, or the critical queen-trade defense), letting the enemy attack crash through; medium boards keep the 'overlooked enemy threat' core but blur the motif to any tactic that simply wins material — forks, back-rank shots, hanging pieces, or tempo-gaining infiltration.

1638.label: Top: from a winning opening, a routine developing/castling move skips the decisive d5 (or d4) pawn break that forks the c6-knight and e6-bishop; medium blurs to other missed central breaks (e5, cxd5, Nd5) and to positions that ignore central tension and hang material to a tactic.

1622.label: At the peak, a side with an advantage/initiative squanders it by playing a slow natural move (a check, pawn-grab, or developing move) instead of the time-critical pawn-break/attacking breakthrough; at medium this blurs to also include missing simpler resources (captures, forks, mate-in-1) and moves that outright hang material.

1639.label: Top: a rook moved to attack/chase the enemy QUEEN hangs material to a capture or mating net; medium keeps the rook-harasses-a-piece motif but broadens the target to other pieces (knight/rook) and the penalty to include missed wins and tempo loss.

1647.label: Top: a light-square bishop sortie to g4/g5 (phantom pin, no Nf3) hangs outright to a capture (Qxg4, Nxg4, or deflection); medium broadens to other unsupported bishop developments (Bf5, Bh6, Bd6) that hang or merely lose tempo, with a couple of missed-win outliers.

1633.label: Top: in a 100%-winning position the player ignores a hanging enemy QUEEN (Nxb5/Nxd8/Rxa5/Bxe2/Nxd1/Rxc6), playing a lesser capture, retreat, or develop instead; medium broadens to skipping any free win — a hanging minor piece, a winning pawn grab, or a forced mate — and the direction blurs between purely missing material and outright hanging one's own piece.

1634.label: Top boards walk the king into mate or piece-winning forks/checks (king exposure constant at peak); medium broadens to any move that hangs material to an overlooked forcing reply — back-rank mates, queen/exchange loss, or simply leaving a piece undefended.

1651.chip: Hangs to pawn break (often e5 fork)
1651.label: Top: a quiet/developing move ignores unresolved central pawn tension and is crushed by the e5 pawn-fork hitting bishop (d6) + knight (f6); medium keeps the 'failed to resolve the center' core but broadens the punishing pawn break (d4/e4/dxc5/dxe6) winning a piece, a pawn, or decisive space.

1640.label: Top boards cleanly drop a whole piece/major material to an immediate enemy capture the player overlooked (a move that opens a line to its own piece or ignores a standing capture/promotion threat); medium broadens to greedy pawn-grabs that hang a rook and a few materially-safe moves that simply miss a winning capture.

1648.label: Top: a pawn push meant to evict/chase a KNIGHT backfires because the knight hops forward or captures instead of retreating, dropping material; medium blurs the chased piece to bishops too (and occasional rook chases), with the punishment broadening to varied tactics—queen checks, other-piece forks, free recaptures.

1650.label: Top: sacrifices a dominant/active knight via a 'useless' check or unsound fork (fork-square defended) that White simply captures; medium keeps the same hang-a-piece-with-check idea but broadens the surrendered piece to bishops and queens (and a few non-knight pieces walking into a free recapture).

1644.label: Top is uniformly White squandering the winning forcing check Qh5+ against Black's missing-f-pawn king (open e8-h5 diagonal) by playing a slow developing/pawn move; medium blurs into assorted opening king-safety/material lapses not tied to Qh5+ — hanging pieces (...f5 leaves g7 to Bxg7, ...Bxd6 hangs the bishop) and removing the e5 defender (...Na5 allows Nxe5+ mate).
